title: AIT Systems Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Company

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.

Role

The AIT Systems Integration Engineer owns functional and system-level testing of our spacecraft and the verification tracking for each satellite campaign. Working within the Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) team, you will take the satellite from integrated subsystems to a flight-ready, fully verified vehicle.

You will bridge systems engineering, subsystem teams and the AIT Engineering Functions. You will turn requirements into test procedures, run and lead test campaigns, and make sure every requirement is closed out with traceable evidence before launch.

The role suits someone who knows SmallSat development approaches, is hands-on with Hardware and Ground Support Equipment (GSE), and understands how satellite subsystems behave together.

Responsibilities

Functional and system testing

  • Own the functional and system test programme for the spacecraft, from unit-level acceptance, integration, thought to whole System End-to-End Testing.

  • Write, review and run test specifications and procedures, including basic functional testing, FDIR, end-to-end tests and mission/day-in-the-life simulations.

  • Lead test readiness reviews and test review boards, and sign off test reports.

  • Run tests before, during and after environmental campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMC) to confirm spacecraft health.

  • Diagnose anomalies, raise and track Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), and drive root-cause investigations with subsystem engineers.

  • Develop and maintain automated test scripts and telemetry/telecommand (TM/TC) databases used for testing.

Verification tracking

  • Own the verification matrix (VCRM) for the satellite campaign, mapping each requirement to its method: test, analysis, inspection or review of design.

  • Plan the verification approach with Systems Engineering and keep it current through the campaign.

  • Collect and link verification evidence, and report close-out status against milestones.

  • Prepare verification data packages for key reviews (e.g. CDR, TRR, QR, PSR/FAR) and customer acceptance.

GSE and test infrastructure

  • Specify, integrate and validate Electrical GSE, including power supplies, battery simulators, RF test sets, umbilicals and break-out boxes.

  • Maintain the spacecraft checkout software and ground segment interfaces used on the AIT floor.

  • Make sure GSE is calibrated, configuration-controlled and safe for use with flight hardware.

Integration and campaign support

  • Support subsystem and payload integration, including electrical interface checks, harness verification and safe-to-mate procedures.

  • Plan and schedule system test activities within the wider AIT campaign.

  • Support launch campaign activities, including transport, launch site checkout and launch vehicle interface testing.

  • Work to cleanroom, ESD and flight hardware handling standards, and contribute to lessons learned for future missions.

Requirements

  • Degree in Aerospace, Electronic, Electrical or Systems Engineering, Physics, or equivalent experience.

  • Typically 3+ years in spacecraft AIT, systems integration or test engineering.

  • Hands-on experience with functional and system-level testing of satellites or space subsystems.

  • Familiarity with SmallSat development approaches: agile, rapid iteration, protoflight models, and pragmatic use of COTS components.

  • Working knowledge of satellite subsystems: EPS, OBC/C&DH, ADCS, communications (TT&C and payload RF), propulsion, thermal, structures and payloads.

  • Experience using and setting up GSE, including EGSE, checkout systems and RF test equipment.

  • Experience with requirements verification and maintaining a verification matrix through to close-out.

  • Comfortable with lab equipment: oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, spectrum analysers, logic analysers.

  • Familiarity with common spacecraft interfaces and protocols (e.g. CAN, I2C, SPI, RS-422, SpaceWire, CCSDS).

  • Clear technical writing for procedures, test reports and NCRs.

Desirables

  • End-to-end involvement in at least one satellite mission that reached launch.

  • Test automation and scripting in Python or similar, and experience with spacecraft control or checkout software (e.g. OpenC3/COSMOS, Yamcs, SCOS-2000).

  • Experience planning or supporting environmental test campaigns (vibration, TVAC, EMC).

  • Knowledge of ECSS standards (e.g. ECSS-E-ST-10-02 Verification, ECSS-E-ST-10-03 Testing) or NASA equivalents.

  • Requirements management tools (e.g. DOORS, Jama, Polarion, Valispace).

  • Launch campaign experience at a launch site.

  • Cleanroom and ESD-certified flight hardware handling.

  • Eligibility for UK security clearance, or the ability to obtain it, if required by the programme.

Personal attributes

  • Takes ownership: drives tests and verification to close-out without waiting to be asked.

  • Methodical and detail-focused, with a strong sense of safety and quality around flight hardware.

  • Calm, structured problem-solver when anomalies appear under schedule pressure.

  • Communicates clearly across disciplines, from subsystem engineers to programme managers and customers.

  • Comfortable in a fast-paced SmallSat environment, balancing rigour with pace.

  • Willing to work flexibly during test and launch campaigns, including occasional travel.

Why NewOrbit Space?

  • Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

  • Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

  • Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

  • Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.

  • Hybrid working - One dedicated remote day per week.

  • Visa sponsorship and relocation support - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.

title: Algorithm Engineer (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
What is Anori Tech doing?

The world talks about batteries, cells and the energy transition. Almost nobody talks about the Battery Management System (BMS) that makes them work.

As battery applications multiply, from robotics and mobility to data centers and grid-scale storage, BMS complexity is exploding. Legacy BMS architectures were never built for this: too rigid to keep up with new requirements, they've turned the BMS into the bottleneck of battery development.

We're building something different: a novel software-defined BMS architecture combined with an AI-driven configuration process. It gets battery manufacturers the right BMS for their exact use case within days, regardless of application or cell chemistry.

We're building the battery management system platform of tomorrow. Delivered in days, not years.

Join us and shape one of the fastest growing markets in the energy sector: The BMS market.

Our Motivation

At Anori Tech, we believe everything is energy, and progress runs on it. With Anori we actively shape the energy transition: from oil to electric, from low to high efficiency. We need batteries for this transition and almost all batteries need a BMS. We strive for Shenzhen speed and German engineering quality. Our objective: put Europe back on the map in the race for the energy transition and build technical leadership out of Hamburg.

About the Role

A BMS is only as good as what it knows about the battery. As our Algorithm Engineer, you'll develop the algorithms that tell the Anori BMS what is happening inside the cells: state of charge, state of health and balancing. And you won't stop at the concept: you'll design algorithms, implement them in our embedded Rust firmware and validate them on real hardware. Later on, the role grows into the cloud, where data pipelines and fleet analytics will build on the models you create today. You'll work closely with Stefan, our CTO, and our firmware and hardware engineers.

Start date: from January 1, 2027

What You'll Do

  • Develop the algorithms that estimate SoC and SoH for different cell chemistries and applications

  • Design balancing strategies that fit the hardware and use case

  • Build battery models (e.g. equivalent circuit models) and parameterize them from measurement data with statistical rigor

  • Implement your algorithms directly in the embedded Rust firmware, efficient enough for constrained hardware

  • Design experiments and evaluation methodologies: analyze failure modes, quantify trade-offs between accuracy, robustness and compute cost

  • Support in building data pipelines and fleet analytics in the cloud

What You Bring

Must have

  • Hands-on experience with state of charge and state of health estimation, shown in a product, publication or substantial project. For example Kalman-type filters, H∞ filters, observers, or coulomb counting with model-based correction

  • Deep understanding of battery behavior and modeling, e.g. equivalent circuit models, hysterisis, ageing or also physics based models

  • Experience implementing numerical algorithms on embedded, constrained hardware (e.g. in Rust or C/C++ - heads-up our firmware is written in Rust, and we'll help you get up to speed)

  • Strong Python skills for modeling, simulation and data analysis

  • Critical, analytical, systematic thinking: you reason from first principles, make your assumptions explicit and challenge existing paradigms

Strongly preferred

  • Experience with cell balancing algorithms and their effects

  • Working with real cell data from test benches or cyclers

  • Signal processing fundamentals: FIR/IIR filter design, sampling and aliasing, noise characterization of sensor data

Nice to have

  • Data pipelines, fleet analytics or cloud experience

  • Machine learning methods for battery data, for example data-driven state of health estimation or anomaly detection

  • Model-based systems engineering and requirements engineering (the skills, not the paper)

You don't tick every box? Apply anyway. No one matches a job description 100%. If this role excites you and you are motivated to grow yourself into it, we want to hear from you.

What We Offer

  • Work on a product with purpose that redefines the state of art: our product is a key part to enable competitive battery energy storage.

  • Work directly with the founding team on decisions that shape the company. The team is small, so your ideas will matter. A lot.

  • Challenging engineering in an industrial, but research-near environment. We bring research into the industry.

  • A modern stack and methods: Rust, MBSE, everything as code, and the best tools and techniques for the job, chosen on merit.

  • To be both supported and challenged: room to grow, and the expectation that you will.

You might be a fit if

descriptionHtml:
Le département Sales compte une trentaine de personnes réparties entre la qualification des prospects et le closing. Leur objectif commun : accompagner les prospects jusqu’à la signature du contrat en Assemblée Générale.

Notre cycle de vente est long et complexe en BtoC (3 à 4 mois en moyenne). La particularité ? La copropriété doit voter à la majorité lors de son assemblée générale pour souscrire à notre solution.

En tant qu’alternant·e Sales Development Representative, tu es le premier point de contact et le premier maillon de notre chaîne commerciale. Ton rôle est stratégique : transformer l’intérêt d’un prospect en une opportunité commerciale réelle pour les Account Executives.

Il existe 600.000 copropriétés en France et chacune d’elle constitue une communauté à part entière, dont il nous faut comprendre le fonctionnement afin de les convaincre de nous rejoindre ! Nos prospects peuvent aussi bien être une petite copropriété de 3 lots en zone rurale, déjà autonome, qu’un grand ensemble immobilier de 300 logements en centre-ville, géré par un professionnel en face duquel nous présenterons une offre concurrente.

Tes missions en soutien de l'équipe Sales

En binôme avec nos commerciaux et sous la responsabilité de ton/ta manager, tu seras formé·e pour découvrir le métier de Sales Development Representative (SDR).

title: Alternance, Growth Marketing
descriptionHtml:
About Marble

Marble is a climate tech venture studio. We partner with scientists, engineers, and operators to create companies solving hard climate problems in the world's largest industries.

Our first 15 companies are building transformative products across energy, industry, agriculture, and climate resilience. 100% have been successful in raising follow-on to date. We are looking to partner with exceptional individuals to create our next venture.

About The Role

We are hiring a Growth Apprentice to join the Marble team and support our recruitment and marketing activities.

You will work directly with senior team members, Partners, and brilliant founders on a mission to turn the tide on the climate crisis. This role offers a unique opportunity to bridge the gap between developing cutting-edge climate technologies and effectively communicating their impact to our target audiences.

You will also gain exposure to the journey of building startups, including thesis development, venture building, and founder support.

Location: Paris.
Language: English fluency; French fluency is preferred.
Contract Type: Apprenticeship (Contrat d’Apprentissage).
Duration: 12 months for the apprenticeship
Start date: October, 2026

Responsibilities

The Growth Marketing apprenticeship is focused on running a 360° marketing process for Marble:

  • Campaign Execution: Plan, launch, and monitor performance-driven marketing campaigns (organic and paid) across Google Ads, LinkedIn, and X to drive measurable user acquisition.

  • A/B Testing & Optimisation: Constantly test ad copy, landing pages, and creative assets to lower our Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) for both talent and portfolio interest.

  • Tracking & Conversions: Implement and manage audience tags and tracking pixels across all platforms to maximise conversion rates and ensure accurate data attribution.

  • Data & KPI Dashboards: Analyse marketing performance data and maintain comprehensive KPI dashboards to track campaign effectiveness and generate actionable insights.

  • Outbound Talent Sourcing: Optimise Marble’s talent pipeline by building targeted lists to strengthen outreach and ensuring seamless data coordination between outbound marketing efforts and CRM systems.

  • PR & Brand Visibility: Support press outreach, pitch media angles to tech and business publications, and integrate PR efforts into broader growth campaigns to amplify brand reach.

Requirements

This is an exciting opportunity for a tech-savvy, creative individual passionate about climate tech and startup ecosystems:

  • Currently enrolled in a degree or certification program eligible for an apprenticeship (Contrat d’Apprentissage)

  • You are fluent in English. French is preferred but not mandatory.

  • You have 5+ hours of screen time.

  • Solid understanding of paid media platforms, including Google Ads, LinkedIn, and X, with experience in campaign setup, targeting, and optimisation.

  • Experience running campaigns and SEO optimisation across Hootsuite, Ahrefs, and similar platforms.

  • You can write high-converting ad copy, PR pitch, or a witty, viral social media hook, adjusting your voice seamlessly.

  • You are experienced in making complex ideas accessible through independent projects (running your own science communication initiatives, creating educational content, managing technical documentation). You know how to maintain brand consistency while experimenting with different content formats.

  • You thrive in fast-paced environments (startups, agencies, research labs, NGOs, etc.) where you've demonstrated a quick adoption of new tools and processes and adapted to new platforms and workflows.

Your ability to learn on the job is more important than ticking every single box. However, we would especially love to hear from you if this sounds like you:

  • You are passionate about climate tech, startups, and venture capital (VC). You are familiar with some climate deep tech startups.

  • You know what it takes to market things well and can execute end‑to‑end: from ideation to design, ads, and launch.

  • You move quickly and proactively. You're quick to recognise when things aren't on track and seamlessly transition into problem-solving mode.

  • You are highly organised, able to juggle competing priorities.

  • You have impeccable attention to detail and excellent written and verbal communication. When it comes to representing Marble, your communications, both written and spoken, are top-notch.

  • You can quickly understand and transform complex technical concepts into engaging content forms. You have worked with tools like Canva, Figma, CapCut, etc.

  • You are AI-savvy and comfortable experimenting with the latest AI tools. You know how to use tools like Hootsuite, Ahrefs, Claude, etc., have a good understanding of prompting, and keep up with the latest developments in AI.

What We Offer

  • A monthly compensation aligned with French legal standards

  • Office located at Station F in Paris. Flexible remote days are possible

  • 1 week of vacation

  • Meal vouchers (Swile), 50% transport refund

  • Exposure to our network of top founders, investors, and advisors

  • Working with the brightest, most driven individuals you’ll meet

  • Rapid learning curve and personal development

How To Apply

You will be asked for:

  • Your LinkedIn profile + a CV (please make sure to include your portfolio within the CV)

  • A few short questions about you (your evaluation as a candidate will be dependent on your portfolio)

We believe that a diverse group of minds is key to solving the climate crisis. We encourage women and people of colour to apply. Studies have shown that under-represented candidates are less likely to apply for an opportunity unless they feel they meet every single qualification. We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive and mission-driven cohort. If you’re excited about the programme but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with what you read on our website, we encourage you to apply anyways!

Our proprietary MIMO-over-copper technology powers a high-performance, chiplet-based AI memory fabric that is both scalable and energy-efficient. Unlike traditional interconnects, our solution reduces power consumption signiﬁcantly while preserving high bandwidth and ultra-low latency — unlocking unprecedented efficiency for AI training and inference at scale.

 

Kandou’s architecture is not just an incremental improvement — it’s a foundational shift in how AI hardware is built for the future.

We believe the world’s largest companies should move at the speed of their ideas, not the speed of the decade-old systems they run on. Today they don’t.

Every process change and every new product line runs into SAP systems layered with decades of custom code and complexity no human mind can fully comprehend. New requirements take months to ship, system migrations cost $100M+ and years of pain.

We’re building the AI operating system that absorbs this complexity and gives enterprises back their speed and ambition. Major enterprises already trust us with their most critical systems, we’ve closed game-changing SI partnerships, and just raised a $60M Series A.

We’re a small, talent-dense team doing our life’s work out of London and NYC. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here shapes the company and how the world’s largest companies operate. We sponsor visas and are convinced diverse teams build better products, so we especially encourage underrepresented groups in tech to reach out.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Every great enterprise software company has a moment when analysts stop treating it as a vendor to watch and start treating it as the one that defines the category. We’re building toward that moment, and we want you to lead us there.

This is a rare chance to build an analyst relations function from the ground up. There’s no legacy playbook and no inherited programme. You decide what world-class looks like and build it with the full backing of the founders. You’ll have a seat at the table on narrative, product and go-to-market from day one, and your work will show up directly in the deals we win and the category we help define.

You'll be the first dedicated AR hire and the person who shapes how the world's most influential technology analysts see Conduct, and by extension how the CIOs and boards who rely on them see us. You'll have a seat at the table on narrative, product, and go-to-market from day one, and your work will show up directly in the deals we win and the category we help define.

descriptionHtml:
Real ownership. Real impact. Build from day one.

Are you an ambitious graduate ready to tackle complex, real-world challenges at the intersection of data, strategy and tech? 

The Future Leaders Graduate Program – Business Analytics at Picnic is a one-year launchpad for exceptional talents. From day one, you join a business team, own a business topic, and become an expert in your field.

At Picnic, we’re building the future of grocery. Using cutting-edge technology and data-driven innovation, we challenge the status quo and build the world’s smartest, most customer-focused supermarket.
We move fast, think big, and turn bold ideas into tangible impact.

Tricks of the trade

  • Lead with ambition: Bring your relentless determination, creativity, and grit. Take the driver’s seat and redefine the grocery shopping experience for millions. You will be expected to think independently, move fast, and deliver results.
  • Steep learning curve: Your growth comes from owning real problems, testing your ideas, learning from your mistakes and starting again. You'll blend hands-on training with immediate execution, you’ll move at a pace that accelerates your growth like nowhere else.
  • Solve real-life puzzles: Spot opportunities, use tools at the forefront of technology, and own the outcome end to end. Not just making slides, but building the solution yourself.
  • Innovate across borders: You’ll collaborate with teams across the Netherlands, Germany, and France, tackling challenges that redefine how Picnic operates at a European scale.
  • High-performance environment: You’ll work alongside some of the best teams in analytics and tech, people who set a high bar and expect you to do the same.

From learning to leading

Throughout this one-year program, you’ll own business-critical projects from start to finish right from the get-go, supported by mentorship, learning sessions, and regular feedback.

You’ll strengthen your leadership skills in project management, storytelling, stakeholder communication, and giving and receiving feedback, while sharpening your technical skills in Python, SQL, Excel, and PowerPoint.

As your scope grows, so does your responsibility. You might scale your initial project or take on new challenges within the same domain. Either way, there’s always a new challenge to lead and an opportunity to make an impact. That’s why every journey is unique: there’s no standardized path through the program, just continuous opportunities to grow and lead.

Where you’ll make an impact

From day one, you’ll be embedded in a business team, taking ownership in one of the following domains:

  • Consumer - Drive growth through pricing, supplier strategy, and our market strategy. Think: Shaping our successful market entry into new cities. Your decisions shape how millions of customers experience Picnic. 
  • Logistics - Build the backbone of Picnics operations. Think: robotic fulfilment, demand forecasting, route optimization across Europe and much more

Your superpowers

You don't wait for permission. You see a problem, build the solution, and bring people with you, before anyone asks. You've probably already started something: a project, a product, a business, an initiative that didn't exist until you made it happen.

More specifically, you:

  • Are about to graduate (or recently graduated) a Masters in a quantitative field: e.g., mathematics, econometrics, engineering, or similar
  • Have experience in high-performance environments: consulting, fast-growth startups, or competitive internships and know what it means to raise the bar
  • Show an entrepreneurial mindset: you build, improve, and take ownership without being asked
  • Think like a builder: hands-on, curious, and driven to challenge the status quo with practical solutions
  • You have already gained basic knowledge in PowerPoint, Python, SQL, Excel or alternative coding languages 
  • EU citizenship or valid EU working permit required.

Many strong candidates (particularly women) talk themselves out of applying because they don't tick every box. If this excites you and you believe you have what it takes, apply. We only hire when we find the right match. That’s why our selection process is intentionally highly selective.

Why Picnic?

  • Grow as we grow. We’re scaling quickly across countries and millions of customers and this is just the start. Grow your impact as we grow; we invest in your path but the driver's seat is always yours
  • Work with other innovators. Work with a driven, energetic team that builds, wins, and celebrates together (think of legendary Friday drinks, our Ski trip and our parties)
  • Kickstart your career. Earn a competitive salary and step into a program designed to launch your long-term future at Picnic

Picnic Perks 

🏆 Rewarding Impact from Day One

You’ll receive an attractive compensation package, designed to reward your ambition, drive, and the direct impact you’ll make from your very first project.

🍎Learning & development 

Our Future Leaders Graduate Program - Business Analytics is designed to offer you a steep learning curve by taking business ownership and end-to-end responsibility early on. You’ll get to learn by doing, while mentored by our Picnic leaders that had a similar journey like you. Next to that, you’ll benefit from other opportunities like Lepaya training for polishing soft skills or Picnic Tech Academy training in case you want to learn new skills other than what you already do in this program. We also offer free access to trained psychologists via our OpenUp partner, and German language classes if you’d like to get your experience in Germany to the next level. 

🗺️Relocation

If you’re moving from another country to join Picnic we make it as smooth as possible for you. We’ll cover your flight costs and a first month's accommodation. 

 🥗Fresh Lunch, coffee, and snacks 

Our offices are equipped with fully-fledged coffee bars and a kitchen. We get delicious fresh and warm lunches every day so you can keep your energy up.

⛳All the rest 

At Picnic you get 30 holidays, we cover your travel expenses and offer a pension plan. We subsidise your Deutschlandticket and with the Lease-a-Bike you can get to work sustainably and healthily. And your phone and laptop are on us, of course.

FAQ

Do I need a quantitative background? It's a strong advantage, but not a hard requirement. If your internships and projects demonstrate real hands-on ownership and data-driven thinking, we'll consider your application. You do need a Master's degree, basic knowledge of Python or SQL, and relevant work experience.

Does the program include rotations? No, intentionally. We believe depth creates ownership, and ownership creates impact. Rather than rotating across teams, you’ll go deep in one area, build real expertise, and gradually expand your scope as your impact grows. If you have topic preferences, tell us during the process.

In what language should I apply? English. Please include your CV and Master's degree transcript or any other relevant test scores (e.g., GMAT)

What are the long-term opportunities after the program? This program is a fast track into a high-impact career at Picnic, it’s an entry point for a long-term future, not a two-year stopover. 

Career paths here are as varied as the people on them. Some grow vertically, building deep expertise and a team around them as their project expands. Others move laterally - from Commercial to Fulfilment, Distribution to Customer, or wherever their strengths and ambitions take them. What they share is real ownership, real impact, and a career they shaped themselves.

title: Android-Entwickler als Scrum Master (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Entwickle Android-Software, die Menschen in Bewegung bringt

Du möchtest Android-Apps entwickeln und sehen, wie dein Code in einem echten Produkt zum Einsatz kommt? Bei AUGLETICS entwickelst du Software für smarte Rudergeräte und unsere App. Du kannst neue Funktionen direkt ausprobieren und gemeinsam mit dem Team verbessern – vom ersten Prototyp bis zur zuverlässigen Anwendung.

Wir entwickeln und produzieren in Königs Wusterhausen bei Berlin. Unser Unternehmen hat rund 25 Mitarbeitende; im Softwareteam arbeitest du mit vier bis fünf Personen und direkt mit unserem CTO Christopher Klabunde. Wir haben viele Ideen und suchen jemanden, der mitdenkt, gerne programmiert und Wert auf gute Ergebnisse legt.

Das entwickelst du bei uns

  • Android-Funktionen für Gerät und App: Du entwickelst neue Features, verbesserst bestehende Abläufe und arbeitest an einer verständlichen, zuverlässigen Bedienung.

  • Das Zusammenspiel im Blick: Du arbeitest an Schnittstellen zwischen App, Gerätesoftware und Backend und hilfst, Datenflüsse und Fehlerfälle sauber zu lösen.

  • Ideen praktisch erproben: Du setzt Prototypen um, probierst sie am Rudergerät aus und entwickelst gute Ansätze mit dem Team weiter.

  • Qualität von Anfang an: Du schreibst nachvollziehbaren Code, beteiligst dich an Reviews und Tests und behebst Fehler nachhaltig.

  • KI sinnvoll einsetzen: Du nutzt KI-gestützte Entwicklungswerkzeuge für Ideen, Code, Tests und Fehleranalyse. Du verstehst und prüfst die Ergebnisse, bevor sie ins Produkt gelangen.

Deine Rolle als Scrum Master

Du verbindest deine technische Arbeit mit der Verantwortung dafür, dass unsere Projekte gemeinsam vorankommen. Als Scrum Master koordinierst du die Zusammenarbeit im Softwareteam und mit externen Entwicklungsagenturen. Du arbeitest eng mit CTO Christopher Klabunde zusammen; disziplinarische Personalführung gehört nicht zur Rolle.

  • Du bringst interne Entwicklung und externe Partner in eine gemeinsame Planung und sorgst für klare Zuständigkeiten, nächste Schritte und nachvollziehbare Abnahmekriterien.

  • Du bereitest agile Abstimmungen vor und moderierst sie, zum Beispiel Sprint Planning, kurze tägliche Abstimmungen, Reviews und Retrospektiven – passend zu unseren Projekten.

  • Du behältst Abhängigkeiten, Termine und offene Entscheidungen im Blick, sprichst Hindernisse früh an und hilfst dem Team, sie zu lösen.

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass Ergebnisse zusammengeführt, gemeinsam getestet und für einen verlässlichen Release vorbereitet werden.

Wenn du bereits Scrum-Master- oder Projektkoordinationserfahrung hast, kannst du sie direkt einbringen. Wenn du neu in der Rolle bist, wachsen wir mit dir hinein: Chris und das Team unterstützen dich dabei. Eine Scrum-Master-Zertifizierung ist ein Plus, aber keine Voraussetzung.

Das bringst du mit

  • Programmiergrundlagen und Lust auf native Android-Entwicklung mit Kotlin oder Java. Praktische Android-Erfahrung ist willkommen; wenn du dich neu in Android einarbeitest, interessieren uns dein bisheriger Lernweg und deine Motivation.

  • Du kannst erklären, wie du technische Aufgaben angehst. Eigene Apps, Lernprojekte, Hochschulprojekte, Praktika und Werkstudententätigkeiten zählen genauso wie berufliche Erfahrung.

  • Ein gutes Verständnis von Programmiergrundlagen und Interesse daran, verständliche, wartbare und getestete Software zu entwickeln.

  • Offenheit für KI-unterstützte App-Entwicklung. Wenn du solche Werkzeuge bereits ausprobiert hast, interessiert uns, was gut funktioniert hat und wie du die Ergebnisse geprüft hast.

  • Eigeninitiative, Freude an Zusammenarbeit und Lust, dich in ein bestehendes Produkt einzuarbeiten und schrittweise Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

  • Gutes Englisch in Wort und Schrift ist für den technischen Austausch im Team erforderlich. Deutschkenntnisse sind ein großer Vorteil, aber keine Voraussetzung.

  • Bereitschaft, regelmäßig in Königs Wusterhausen vor Ort zu arbeiten, um Funktionen am Gerät zu entwickeln und mit dem Team abzustimmen.

Ein Studium der Informatik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung, eine passende Ausbildung oder vergleichbare Kenntnisse sind eine gute Grundlage.

Mit Erfahrung oder am Anfang: Wir wollen dich kennenlernen

Du hast schon mehrere Jahre Erfahrung in diesem Bereich? Super – bring deine Ideen und deinen Blick von außen ein. Du stehst noch am Anfang oder hast bisher keine Berufserfahrung in diesem Bereich? Auch das ist in Ordnung. Wenn du für unser Produkt brennst, technische Grundlagen mitbringst und dich schnell in neue Themen einarbeitest, möchten wir dich kennenlernen.

In beiden Fällen ist es unsere Aufgabe, dich gut ins Team zu integrieren und dir Wissen, Werkzeuge und Unterstützung für einen erfolgreichen Start bereitzustellen. Gemeinsam mit Chris und dem Team lernst du unser Produkt und unsere Abläufe kennen. Aufgaben und Verantwortung stimmen wir auf deinen Erfahrungsstand ab und entwickeln sie mit dir weiter.

Zusätzliche Pluspunkte

  • Erfahrung mit Firebase als Backend für Apps, zum Beispiel bei Benutzeranmeldung, Datenspeicherung oder serverseitiger Logik.

  • Erfahrung in der iOS-Entwicklung, idealerweise mit Swift oder SwiftUI.

  • Kenntnisse in Git, automatisierten Tests, CI/CD oder der Anbindung von APIs und Geräten.

Darauf kannst du dich freuen

  • Ein eigenes Produkt, das du direkt ausprobieren kannst, und sichtbaren Einfluss auf das Training unserer Kunden.

  • Ein kleines Softwareteam, direkte Zusammenarbeit mit CTO Christopher Klabunde und kurze Wege zwischen Idee, Entwicklung und Test.

  • Raum für eigene Ideen und fachliche Entwicklung – mit Aufgaben, die zu deinem Erfahrungsstand passen und mit dir wachsen.

  • Unbefristete Vollzeitstelle mit 40 Stunden pro Woche und 28 Urlaubstagen im Jahr.

  • 50.000 bis 65.000 € brutto pro Jahr, abhängig von deinen relevanten Fähigkeiten und Erfahrungen.

  • Arbeitsplatz Zur Heide 10 in Königs Wusterhausen bei Berlin. Ein bis zwei Tage Homeoffice pro Woche sind nach Absprache möglich.

Dein Arbeitsplatz bei Berlin

Unser Standort ist Zur Heide 10 in Königs Wusterhausen. Der Bahnhof Königs Wusterhausen ist mit der S-Bahn S46 und Regionalzügen direkt an Berlin angebunden. Die Strecke vom Bahnhof zu uns lässt sich mit dem Fahrrad zurücklegen. Vor Ort entwickelst und testest du direkt am Produkt; ein bis zwei Tage Homeoffice pro Woche sind nach Absprache möglich.

Einfach bewerben

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf auf Deutsch oder Englisch. Ein klassisches Anschreiben brauchst du nicht. Ein GitHub-Link oder eine App ist willkommen, aber keine Voraussetzung.

Zum Einstieg lernen wir uns in einem kurzen Onlinegespräch kennen. Danach schauen wir gemeinsam auf deine bisherigen Erfahrungen, deinen Lernweg und die Aufgaben bei AUGLETICS.

English-speaking applicants are welcome. English is required; German is a strong plus. You will develop Android software for our connected rowing machines and app, working closely with our CTO and a small team. Early-career developers with practical projects are welcome. Based in Königs Wusterhausen near Berlin, with one to two home-office days per week by agreement.

title: Anthropic Research Resident
descriptionHtml:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

The Anthropic Residency is our paid, fixed-term research program, with placements lasting between six weeks and six months. We are looking for people who have led ambitious work in a variety of technical fields and want to transition to full-time work focused on making sure AI systems are safe and beneficial for all of humanity. If you are a professor in a quantitative discipline, a technical founder or a staff-level engineer and want to transition to work on transformative AI, we want to hear from you. Background in machine learning is not required.

What to expect

  • A concrete, scoped project matched to your background, with direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers
  • Access to Claude models and GPU compute
  • Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community

Interview process

The interview process will include an initial application, recruiter screen, technical assessment, research discussion and a reference check.

Applications for this round close on November 22, 2026 (11:59 PM PT). We expect to make offers in January 2027.

You may be a good fit if you

  • Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole
  • Are excited to transition into working on empirical AI research full-time
  • Have led ambitious work in a variety of technical fields (professor in a quantitative discipline, a technical founder or a staff-level engineer)
  • Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments
  • Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Strong candidates may also

  • Have experience authoring research papers in machine learning, NLP, or AI safety
  • Have experience with LLMs, reinforcement learning or Kubernetes clusters and complex shared codebases

Mentors and research areas

Potential Anthropic mentors include:

  • Sara Price: leads the Alignment Training team; background in data science
  • Ethan Perez: leads the Alignment Science team; background in machine learning
  • Evan Hubinger: leads the Alignment Stress-Testing team; formerly at The Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)
  • Samuel Marks: leads the Scalable Oversight team; background in mathematics
  • Elana Simon: researches the interpretability of language models and biological models; background in biomedical informatics
  • Belinda Li: researches how language models represent the world, users, and themselves; background in natural language processing (PhD, MIT)
  • Jack Lindsey: leads the Model Psychology team; background in theoretical neuroscience
  • Nicholas Carlini: researches adversarial machine learning and AI security; previously at DeepMind and Google Brain
  • Jascha Sohl-Dickstein: works at the intersection of safety and pretraining; background in physics and neuroscience, formerly Principal Scientist at Google Brain

Residents will work on empirical research questions in collaboration with Anthropic's research teams. Areas we are particularly interested in include:

AI safety & alignment

  • Scalable Oversight: Developing techniques to keep highly capable models helpful and honest, even as they surpass human-level intelligence in various domains.
  • Adversarial Robustness and AI Control: Creating methods to ensure advanced AI systems remain safe and harmless in unfamiliar or adversarial scenarios.
  • Model Organisms: Creating model organisms of misalignment to improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise.
  • Model Internals and Interpretability: Advancing our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures.
  • Safeguards Research: Developing robust defenses against adversarial attacks, comprehensive evaluation frameworks for model safety, and automated systems to detect and mitigate potential risks before deployment.
  • AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations.

AI security & frontier red-teaming

  • Stress-testing frontier models to understand the full extent of their current capabilities in fields such as cybersecurity, robotics or cryptography.

ML systems & reinforcement learning

  • Improving how frontier models are trained and building the infrastructure behind that research, from model architecture, optimizers and training data to accelerator simulators, hardware backends and RL environment pipelines.

For a fuller picture of the questions we care about, see our Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions and recent publications from our Alignment, Interpretability and Frontier Red teams.

Logistics

  • Duration: Placements are six weeks, three months or six months, depending on team fit and candidate preferences. Other lengths between three and six months are possible by exception.
  • Location: This application is for a remote UK position, with the option to work from our London office. However, we prefer that Residents work from our San Francisco office, where most of our research staff is based, but remote participation is possible, especially for shorter placements. Most full-time research roles at Anthropic require relocation to San Francisco. Remote participants need to be based in a country where Anthropic can hire.
  • Commitment: Full-time role for the duration of the residency.
  • Compensation: £265,000 to £375,000/year pro-rated for the duration of the residency + benefits
  • Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas for placements of three months or longer. For six-week placements we encourage remote participation from a country where Anthropic can hire.

Applicants may also be considered for the Anthropic Fellows Program.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:£265,000—£375,000 GBP

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

descriptionHtml:

We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Role Overview

As a Junior Application Security Analyst in the Information Security team, you will help secure Checkout.com’s software applications throughout the Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC). You will work closely with developers and product teams to integrate security early in the development process, identify and oversee the remediation of vulnerabilities, and ensure adherence to secure coding practices and application security standards. This role focuses on practical, hands-on security support while also growing your expertise in application security.

 

Key Responsibilities

SSDLC & Secure Coding

  • Assist in integrating security controls into the SSDLC.

  • Support the creation and maintenance of secure coding guidelines (e.g., OWASP Top 10, CERT Secure Coding Standards).

Application Security Testing

  • Run a Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Software Composition Analysis (SCA) scans.

  • Conduct API security testing.

  • Support CI/CD pipelines to keep secure and effective integration.

Threat Modeling & Application Security Analysis

  • Participate in threat modeling sessions.

  • Document identified threats, assess risks and provide mitigation recommendations.

  • Assist in code and system reviews to analyse security in company’s products.

Vulnerability Management

  • Triage and prioritise vulnerabilities from automated scans.

  • Track, verify and ensure security flaws remediation.

  • Assist to automate an AppSec pipelines

Collaboration & Awareness

  • Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate security into product design and improve existing systems.

  • Help deliver training and awareness on SSDLC best practices and secure coding.

  • Contribute to security documentations.

Required Skills & Experience

  • 1–3 years in application security, secure software development, or related IT/security role.

  • Understand basic network technologies and protocols (HTTP, TCP/IP, DNS and the OSI model).

  • Understanding of common software vulnerabilities and their mitigations.

  • Basic programming experience in a popular language (e.g., Python, JavaScript, Golang).

  • Understanding of CI/CD pipelines and DevSecOps principles.

  • Basic understanding of cloud technologies (AWS, GCP or Azure) and GitHub security features.

  • Strong attention to detail in documentation and assessments.

Preferred

  • Familiarity with SAST/DAST/SCA tools and API security testing platforms.

  • Exposure to cloud-native application security (AWS, Azure, GCP).

  • Understanding of container security (Docker, Kubernetes).

  • Experience of participating in Capture The Flag (CTF) competitions.

Key Competencies

  • Eager to learn and expand technical skills in application security.

  • Effective communicator with both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Collaborative and proactive problem solver.

  • Ability to prioritise work.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

title: Applied AI Architect, OpenAI for Government
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The OpenAI for Government AI Architect team partners with public sector organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with government agencies, public institutions, and partner organizations serving the government to identify where AI can advance critical missions, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, Global Affairs, and specialist delivery teams to help public sector customers adopt advanced AI responsibly and effectively.

About the Role

As an AI Architect, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will shape each customer's AI strategy and guide their journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable mission impact.

You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate mission priorities into a focused use-case portfolio, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable customer value. The Account Director leads the overall account strategy and relationship, while you lead the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production impact.

You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, and partners to provide deeper expertise and execute work where needed. This role calls for strong public sector fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy and hands-on technical conversations.

This role is based in Munich or London. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of public sector customers and pre-sales prospects.

  • Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, and expansion opportunities.

  • Lead discovery with agency leaders, mission owners, executives, and technical teams to identify, qualify, and prioritize use cases tied to meaningful mission and operational outcomes.

  • Develop clear Applied AI Architectures spanning models, applications, data, integration, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, and deployment.

  • Guide customers through technical evaluations, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, and proofs of value, building confidence in both the solution and its path to production.

  • Help customers navigate the security, compliance, governance, and deployment requirements that shape AI adoption in the public sector.

  • Maintain a focused use-case portfolio with clear decision criteria, ownership, blockers, success measures, delivery needs, and adoption plans.

  • Develop trusted relationships and technical champions across CIOs, CTOs, CISOs, Chief Data and AI Officers, program leaders, engineering teams, and other customer stakeholders.

  • Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, security, product and domain specialists, partners, and other delivery teams.

  • Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged.

  • Track adoption, usage, account health, production readiness, and measurable mission impact, intervening early when risks threaten value realization.

  • Apply public sector and mission expertise to recognize repeatable patterns, sharpen customer priorities, and identify relevant expansion opportunities.

  • Share customer insights with Product, Engineering, and Research, translating field learnings into better products, architecture guidance, and reusable practices.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, solutions engineering, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical customer success.

  • Have guided complex organizations from technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable impact.

  • Have experience working with government agencies, public institutions, or government contractors and understand how mission priorities, security, compliance, governance, and procurement considerations shape technology adoption.

  • Build credibility with senior technical and government leaders while communicating equally well with hands-on engineers and program teams.

  • Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, data integration, identity, security, and privacy.

  • Understand modern AI systems, frontier models, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, and enterprise AI workflows.

  • Can prototype, explain technical tradeoffs, and work confidently with APIs, SDKs, and languages such as Python or JavaScript.

  • Exercise sound judgment about when to go deep personally, when to involve specialists, and how to establish clear handoffs and ownership.

  • Have experience developing technical account plans, prioritizing complex customer portfolios, and connecting adoption to measurable outcomes.

  • Bring meaningful expertise in a relevant public sector mission or customer segment.

descriptionHtml:
About Nomos

Europe pays more than twice as much for electricity as the US or Asia. To reach competitive price levels, Europe has to lean on solar and deliver the flexibility that makes this feasible. Nomos is building a full-stack power company to unlock that flexibility by connecting millions of homes to Europe’s energy markets.

At Nomos, we care about our craft and take full responsibility for what we build. We hire for spikes, not an absence of weaknesses, and look for exceptional ability backed by a record of achievement. This has brought together IMO and IOI medalists, former founders and Olympic athletes in a team whose individual strengths reinforce one another.

 

What you’ll do

We’re building an energy company from first principles. That means rethinking the operational work behind it: which processes we need, how they run, and what agents can take on. You’ll build the AI systems that let Nomos serve more customers without scaling manual work at the same rate.

  • Work directly with customers and internal teams to understand their workflows and find where AI can make the biggest difference.

  • Build agents and integrations that handle real operational work, from customer onboarding to communication with energy market participants.

  • Own what you ship: design, development, testing, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance.

 

Exciting challenges

  • Rethink how an energy company operates. Building from scratch gives us the freedom to question processes that established suppliers take for granted. You’ll decide how software, agents, and people work together and turn that into systems the company depends on every day.

  • Put the newest AI capabilities to work in production. Nomos is built around AI. You’ll have access to new models and tools as they become available, with generous spending limits to experiment. The engineering challenge is making them dependable at scale: testing behaviour, handling exceptions, and knowing when a person needs to step in.

 

Who you are

  • You’ve shipped and operated production software. You understand how systems fit together, how they fail, and how to keep them working as usage grows.

  • You have hands-on experience building with AI. You can connect models to tools and data, evaluate their behaviour, and make sound decisions about where agents are useful.

descriptionHtml:
About Us

Engelhart was founded in 2013 by BTG Pactual Group as a commodities trading company. Our business model is “asset light” and highly diversified – giving us the ability to adapt effectively and nimbly to changing market conditions. We have assembled successful multidisciplinary teams, leveraging advanced fundamental analysis with deep quantitative and weather research capabilities.  Our activities are underpinned by strong risk management practices and by powerful technology and operational excellence. We have exceptional teams with diverse global backgrounds and decades of experience, and are driven by a highly collaborative culture, across products and competencies.

In 2024, Engelhart acquired Trailstone, a global energy trading and technology company. The acquisition provides us with new expertise, analytics and proprietary technology which is being used to provide risk management and optimisation services to help maximise the value of our clients’ renewable power. The acquisition also expanded Engelhart’s capabilities into physical natural gas across North America, a critical fuel to support the energy transition.

Our talented and experienced individuals work together according to its four company values: Performance, Agility, Collaboration, Entrepreneurship.

About the Role

As a member of the Tech Data, AI & UX team allocated to European & Asian Power Trading in Berlin, you will build the services, infrastructure, and AI & data platforms that power the business, enabling teams to improve their data-driven decisions and connect innovative products.

As part of this Joint Venture, the Applied AI Engineer will help to evolve ECTP’s AI & Agentic platforms – a strategic, firm-wide initiative led by the Tech Data, AI & UX team. The role provides hands-on exposure to the cutting edge of enterprise AI, working alongside experienced data engineer, architects and quant developers in a live, production-grade environment.

You will work closely with trading desk and Technology teams to build core agentic infrastructure, integrate tooling via AWS Lambda and MCP servers, develop agent skills, and configure knowledge bases across user, chat, agent, and application contexts. You will explore and evaluate open-source and proprietary connectors within the rapidly evolving LLM and Generative AI ecosystem, and help roll out individual productivity tools such as Microsoft Copilot and Claude Code. All solutions will be hosted securely within Engelhart’s internal network, with models deployed in a dedicated VPC and governed access to firm data, with a strong preference for AWS-native and Bedrock-based architectures.

This will be a full-time role, owning the following responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with the trading desk to supercharge their research capabilities and data-driven insights by extending Engelhart's core AI and agentic platform to address new trading desk requirements.
  • Assist in the set-up and configuration of core agentic AI infrastructure, including orchestration layers, agent runtimes, and supporting services, deployed securely within Engelhart’s AWS VPC.
  • Build and maintain agent tooling integrations via AWS Lambda functions and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, enabling agents to interact with firm data, APIs, and internal systems.
  • Develop agent skills and configure knowledge bases, including document stores, vector databases (e.g. Postgres with pgvector, AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases), and retrieval pipelines for user, chat, agent, and application contexts.
  • Research, evaluate, and help integrate open-source and proprietary accelerators, connectors, and frameworks (e.g. LangChain, LlamaIndex, n8n, etc) into the platform, assessing fitness for purpose in a regulated, IP-sensitive environment.
  • Support the deployment and end-user adoption of individual AI productivity tools, including Microsoft Copilot and Claude Code, ensuring secure configuration and appropriate access controls within Engelhart’s internal network.
  • Contribute to technical documentation, architecture diagrams, and internal knowledge sharing on AI tooling, design decisions, and implementation patterns to support team learning and continuity.
  • Collaborate with engineers, data scientists, and business stakeholders to iteratively test and improve agentic workflows, gathering feedback and translating it into technical improvements.

About You

This person will be a technically minded and genuinely curious person who is excited about the transformative potential of AI and wants to go beyond surface-level tooling – you want to understand how things work and help build them. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, energised by fast-moving technology landscapes, and take pride in writing clean, well-structured code. You thrive in collaborative environments and are motivated by the opportunity to contribute to something that has real, visible impact within a live business setting.

The following education, experiences and skills are essential for application:

  • Background in Computer Science, Software Engineering, AI, Data Science, or related technical undergraduate degree.
  • A genuine passion for AI, Large Language Models, and Generative AI. Not just as a user, but with curiosity about how they work and how to build with them.
  • Proficient in Python, with hands-on experience writing scripts, working with APIs, or building small applications – whether through coursework, personal projects, or hackathons.
  • Familiarity with cloud concepts or services (preference for AWS), containerisation (Docker), or REST APIs – even if only at an introductory or project level.
  • A proactive, self-directed learning style – able to research unfamiliar technologies, synthesise documentation, and form a view on trade-offs with limited guidance.
  • Good communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical colleagues, and to work effectively in a small, fast-moving team.
  • A collaborative, team-oriented mindset, with the confidence to contribute ideas, ask questions, and engage actively with engineers, data scientists, and business users.
  • An organised approach to work, with attention to detail, a strong sense of ownership, and the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity and rapid change, with the resilience to iterate quickly, adapt to new findings, and thrive in a technology landscape that evolves week to week.

In addition, the following criteria is not required, but highly desirable for this role:

  • Foundational knowledge of energy trading markets, including core concepts like balancing mechanism operations, Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), and Virtual Power Plants (VPPs).
  • Prior exposure to LLM frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or similar; experience with vector databases (e.g. pgvector, Pinecone, Chroma); or familiarity with AWS Bedrock, SageMaker, or equivalent managed AI services.
  • Experience with version control (Git) and basic understanding of CI/CD pipelines or infrastructure-as-code (e.g. AWS CloudFormation, CDK).
  • Understanding of prompt engineering techniques, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), or multi-agent system design patterns.
  • Participation in AI/ML hackathons, open-source contributions, personal projects involving LLMs or automation, or active engagement with the AI development community (e.g. Hugging Face, GitHub, LangChain forums).
  • Portuguese as a second language.

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and participation in Engelhart’s discretionary bonus plan.
  • 28 days of annual holiday entitlement plus Berlin public holidays.
  • €3,000 per year contribution to a private pension scheme on your behalf.
  • €20 monthly subsidy towards BVG tickets.
  • €25 monthly subsidy towards ClassPass membership.
  • A subsidy for German language courses to help you immerse yourself in the local culture.
  • A sociable working environment with an open, international culture.

title: AppSec Staff Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Location: Bristol, UK (hybrid, three days a week in the office)
Level: Staff Engineer (TL2)
Team: Security Engineering, within the Cyber Security squad
Salary: £105,600 – £132,000 + discretionary bonus
Contract: Permanent
Reporting to: Senior Software Engineering Manager

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.


About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.


What you’ll do

You’ll join the Security Engineering team, working alongside our cyber security leadership, architecture team and technical leaders across engineering. Our mission is to equip teams to build and innovate while upholding security best practice and protecting client data in the highly regulated energy sector.

  • Integrate security tooling and use AI to prevent, detect and respond to emerging threats

  • Work with senior technical leadership to shape our technical strategy and solutions architecture, so security, risk and compliance feed into technical decisions

  • Help product teams deliver secure systems quickly by building a strong security culture through mentoring, design reviews and training

  • Give product and engineering teams practical guidance on identifying, prioritising and mitigating systemic risks and vulnerabilities

  • Lead the evolution of our security best practice across application development and the wider SDLC, supporting teams with expert advice and automation

  • Influence technical and non-technical stakeholders across Kaluza and client teams

  • Mentor and coach security and software engineers to balance risk with speed and quality

  • Build relationships with third-party security vendors and industry bodies to keep us at the forefront of emerging practices, tooling and standards


What you’ll bring

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Extensive experience mentoring engineers and collaborating closely (e.g. pairing, swarming)

  • Deep understanding of software security flaws and web application security best practice (OWASP Top 10, CWE/SANS Top 25)

  • Extensive knowledge of CI/CD and DevOps principles, and their security considerations

  • Experience applying AI in your own work and helping others build it safely into how they develop

  • Scripting skills and first-hand experience of software development at scale

  • Working knowledge of Okta or equivalent, to enable workforce identity and enforce access management policies

  • Awareness of AWS and/or GCP security best practice, and some experience with infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform)

  • Experience applying architectural and software design patterns in a complex environment

You’ll also be:

  • A pragmatic, risk-based decision-maker who weighs the technical and commercial consequences of your choices

  • Skilled at influencing upwards and outwards, with great communication skills

  • Able to set a clear vision for large-scale technical direction and align multiple teams behind it

  • Keen to drive compliance and NFR improvements that balance information security and commercial goals

  • Committed to a culture of learning and improvement, and willing to challenge engineering leadership to support it

Skills (SFIA): We use the SFIA framework to assess and develop our security engineers. Levels run from 1 to 7.

Essential:

  • Level 6: Systems design

  • Level 5: Information security, specialist advice, systems development lifecycle, solution architecture, emerging technology monitoring

  • Level 4: Information assurance, information and data compliance

Desirable: Identity and access management (Level 5), software development (Level 6), learning delivery (Level 3), and information assurance stepping up to Level 5


Our values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.


Our perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday [plus/including bank holidays], plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app


Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you. If you need any adjustments during the process, just let us know.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn, or read our Applicant Data Protection Policy.

title: Architecture Modeling Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Meet Arago and the Aragonians

Arago’s mission is to re-engineer the foundations of computing from first principles.

The explosive growth of AI is pushing the industry to rethink how processors are built. Arago is meeting that challenge with a proprietary technology that fuses optical and CMOS technologies to deliver an order-of-magnitude increase in performance.

Arago is the fastest, and currently the only, company to have built such a processor. It's backed by leading deep-tech investors and some of the most respected figures in semiconductors and computing, including the CEO of Arm, the founder of macOS who worked directly with Steve Jobs at Apple, an Nvidia Fellow, the Head of Optics at Google, and many other industry leaders.

Our work is guided by three clear values: do great things, move with high velocity, and operate as one unit. We work in a demanding environment where constant learning, ownership, and execution are expected, and where exceptional people have the opportunity to do their life’s work.

 

What you’ll do

As Architecture Modeling Engineer you will own performance modeling and workload analysis for Arago's optical AI accelerator, working across hardware and software teams to evaluate design choices, shape the programming model, and optimize key compute kernels. This role turns workload requirements into architecture decisions and, ultimately, high-performance software on silicon.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Strong mathematical background, particularly in linear algebra, probability, numerical methods, and quantitative performance analysis.

  • Strong knowledge of computer architecture, including compute pipelines, memory hierarchies, interconnects, and parallel execution.

  • Strong C/C++ and Python programming skills.

  • Experience analyzing and optimizing performance-critical kernels or low-level compute workloads.

  • Good understanding of AI/ML workloads, tensor operations, data movement, and common execution patterns.

  • Ability to work across hardware and software teams and translate workload behavior into architecture and software requirements.

  • Language: English at a proficient level.

Responsibilities

  • Develop fast, flexible performance models to evaluate AI accelerator architecture choices and guide early design decisions.

  • Work closely with the software team to characterize key AI workloads, kernels, dataflows, and system bottlenecks.

  • Work closely with hardware architects to model compute, memory, interconnect, and scheduling behavior across proposed architectures.

  • Drive rapid performance studies and trade-off analyses across throughput, latency, utilization, bandwidth, and efficiency.

  • Help define and validate the programming model and workload mapping strategy for the accelerator.

  • Following architecture definition, work hands-on with the software team to optimize compute kernels and key workloads for the target hardware.

  • Build lightweight simulation, profiling, and analysis tools that support fast iteration from architecture exploration through software optimization.

Nice to have

  • Strong industry knowledge about AI hardware, GPUs, memory generations, rack-scale computing.

  • Experience building performance models, simulators, or analytical models for CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, or other accelerators.

  • Experience with profiling, benchmarking, and identifying hardware or software performance bottlenecks.

  • Experience in novel computing architectures: analog computing, in-memory computing, heterogeneous systems.

Pay and benefits

  • Competitive cash compensation, with final package based on location, experience, and the pay of team members in similar positions.

  • Meaningful stock option plan offered (included in the majority of full time offers).

  • Healthcare coverage (including family-friendly options), pension contributions, professional development support, and 25 days of PTO, in addition to public holidays.

  • Ownership of a key technical domain, with significant vertical and/or horizontal growth opportunities, based on performance and individual drive.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of AI at Arago.
