  • Identify opportunities to integrate emerging technologies and data-driven tools to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and elevate fan outcomes.

Ownership & Execution (Determined & Relentless Mindset)

  • Own the strategic roadmap, budget, and resource planning for the Fan Services customer service organization, aligning headcount, technology, and vendor/BPO investment to business goals.
  • Drive performance management across the team with a disciplined focus on financial targets and third-party SLAs, ensuring accountability at every level of the organization.
  • Thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, demonstrating the ability to manage competing priorities with urgency and composure while delivering results at scale.
  • Communicate clearly and confidently in writing, speaking, and digital formats to senior-level and C-level audiences, translating operational complexity into strategic insight.

AI & DIGITAL CAPABILITY

We are building a future-ready organization. This role is expected to:

  • Apply AI and technology to improve efficiency, quality, and outcomes
  • Use data and digital tools to inform decisions and enhance performance
  • Demonstrate curiosity and adaptability in adopting new technologies and ways of working
  • Contribute to a culture of innovation and continuous improvement

CAPABILITIES & EXPERIENCE YOU BRING

Required Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of customer operations experience, including deep expertise in first and second line contact management and managing own and 3PL operations.
  • 7+ years of people leadership experience, including demonstrated success leading leaders and managers across on-premises, hybrid, and remote environments.
  • Experience and understanding of omni-channel operations and the e-commerce space.
  • Advanced communication skills in writing, speaking, and digital formats, with the ability to deliver comfortably to senior-level and C-level audiences.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office suite, including foundational experience with Excel and pivot tables; knowledgeable user of CRM technologies, Conversation-Analytics Software, Contact Center Technologies, Customer Review Tools, and order management tools such as EDI, DAX, and Cloud Reporting.

Education:

Bachelor's degree in business, communications, management, or a related field.

At Fanatics, we operate with a BOLD mindset - We Build Championship Teams, we’re Obsessed with Fans, we embrace a Limitless Entrepreneurial Spirit, and we approach every challenge with a Determined and Relentless Mindset. Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. descriptionHtml:
Who is Sonar?

Sonar enables organizations to ship agentic code with confidence. Code creation is abundant, but confidence is scarce. Our core platform, SonarQube, verifies over 750 billion lines of code every day, delivering agentic verification and governance for all code. Trusted by more than 7 million developers and 75% of the Fortune 100, including teams at Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com, Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company, Sonar enables organizations to reduce outages, improve security, and lower the cost and risk of agentic software development.

Founded in Geneva and now headquartered in Austin, Texas, Sonar has a global team working across offices and hubs, including Silicon Valley, London, Bochum, Barcelona, Singapore, Tokyo, and the Washington, D.C. area. At Sonar, we’re enabling enterprises to build agentic software factories that can move quickly while maintaining the control, consistency and evidence required to ship with confidence.


Position description

Sonar is scaling its go-to-market engine across Sales, Customer Success, and post-sales teams in every region. As the company grows, the field needs operating changes that are consistent, measurable, and adopted, not a collection of regional fixes. This role exists to design, land, and measure those changes.

As Director, Global Field Operations, you will sit in Revenue Operations as an individual contributor at Principal level, dedicated 100% to global field operations initiatives. You will not carry a regional support remit. You will own the portfolio of initiatives that change how the global field plans, sells, forecasts, and retains customers, from problem definition through rollout to measured business impact. You will be judged on outcomes such as conversion, pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy, productivity, and retention, not on the volume of activity delivered.

  • Own a portfolio of global field initiatives end to end: problem definition, business case, design, rollout, and post-launch review. Prioritise on expected impact and effort, and stop or pivot initiatives that are not moving their target metric.

  • Build and run change plans: stakeholder mapping, communication cadence, interlock with enablement, adoption tracking, and feedback loops. Explain the why behind each change in the language of the audience, from reps and front-line managers to the CRO and ELT.

  • Stay close to the field through deal reviews, pipeline inspection, and field sessions. Collect feedback continuously, adapt the approach quickly, and close the loop with the people who gave it.

  • Align Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Enablement, Finance, and Systems on priorities, sequencing, and ownership, often without direct authority. Balance regional needs against global standards.

  • Standardise global processes and operating cadence (forecast, pipeline inspection, QBRs) for scalability and repeatability.

  • Provide narrative and analysis for QBRs, leadership meetings, and strategic discussions, linking initiative results to ARR, NRR, and GRR.


    • Experience & Qualifications

  • Bring 5+ years in sales operations, field operations, revenue operations, or a related function in B2B SaaS. We welcome current ICs, and managers willing to move into an IC role for the medium term (1+ years).

  • Have led process, tooling, or organisational changes that the field adopted, with proven change management and communication skills at every level up to executive.

  • Have field credibility: you have worked directly with Sales Leaders and sellers, and both trust you.

  • Take feedback well and pivot quickly without losing sight of the outcome.

  • Build strong relationships and influence across the GTM organisation without relying on direct authority.

  • Combine business, strategy, and analytical capability, including forecasting, pipeline, and productivity analysis, and be able to articulate trends in churn, expansion, ARR, NRR, GRR, LTV, and CAC.

title: Director, International Expansion — CEO Office
descriptionHtml:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the team

The CEO Office partners directly with Airwallex's executive leadership on the company's most important priorities. We work across regions and functions to shape the company's direction, solve complex problems, and turn ambitious ideas into reality.

International expansion is a core strategic priority for Airwallex. As we continue to build a truly global financial platform, we are expanding into new markets, securing regulatory licences, deepening our local financial infrastructure, and bringing new products to customers around the world.

We operate at the intersection of strategy, regulation, product, and execution, working closely with leaders across Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, Finance, and Operations. The team combines strategic thinking with an entrepreneurial, hands-on approach to building and scaling our international presence.

What you'll do

As Director, International Expansion, you will lead Airwallex's expansion into new markets globally, shaping where and how we grow and building the regulatory, product, and operational foundations to succeed.

You will own a portfolio of market-entry initiatives end to end, from evaluating opportunities and defining entry strategies through licensing, product localisation, operational readiness, and commercial launch.

Reporting to the CEO's Chief of Staff, you will lead a lean team and work directly with senior executives to influence strategic decisions, mobilise cross-functional teams, and overcome the complex challenges of entering new markets.

This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who combines strategic judgment, an entrepreneurial mindset, and the ability to translate ambitious plans into tangible outcomes. You will build and lead the expansion function while remaining directly involved in the most strategically important and complex market-entry initiatives.

Responsibilities

  • Lead global expansion strategy: Own the strategy and execution of Airwallex's expansion into new markets globally. Evaluate and prioritise market opportunities, define entry strategies, and recommend where and how Airwallex should invest to establish and scale its presence.

  • Own market entry end to end: Lead expansion initiatives from initial market assessment through regulatory authorisation, entity establishment, product readiness, and operational launch. Take accountability for delivering market entries and navigating the strategic and execution challenges along the way.

  • Define regulatory and operating models: Work closely with Legal, Compliance, Risk, and Finance to determine the optimal licensing, legal entity, and operating structures for each market. Translate regulatory requirements into practical, scalable business models that support Airwallex's long-term ambitions.

  • Influence product and infrastructure strategy: Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to shape local product capabilities, payment infrastructure, and market-specific roadmaps. Identify opportunities to deepen Airwallex's presence through new licences, direct payment-system access, and expanded product offerings.

  • Lead a high-performing team: Manage and develop a lean team, setting clear priorities, providing strategic guidance, and driving accountability across multiple markets. Personally lead the highest-priority or most complex initiatives while building the team's capabilities.

  • Drive executive alignment and investment decisions: Work directly with the CEO's Chief of Staff and senior executives to shape expansion priorities, resolve critical trade-offs, secure resources, and drive timely decisions. Present clear recommendations on market opportunities, regulatory strategy, investment requirements, and launch readiness.

  • Build external relationships: Partner with local regulators, financial institutions, payment networks, advisers, and other strategic stakeholders to support regulatory approvals, establish local capabilities, and unlock new market opportunities.

  • Build a scalable expansion engine: Develop repeatable frameworks, tools, and operating processes that enable Airwallex to expand faster and more efficiently. Leverage AI and automation to improve regulatory intelligence, market analysis, execution tracking, and cross-functional coordination.

  • Drive broader CEO Office priorities: Support or lead high-impact strategic initiatives beyond international expansion, working across the business to solve complex problems, shape company-level decisions, and drive execution on critical priorities.

Who you are

Minimum qualifications:

  • Intellectually curious, resilient, and hungry to win. You thrive on solving difficult problems, challenge conventional thinking, learn quickly, and have the drive and persistence to turn ambitious goals into results.

  • Significant experience in strategy, international expansion, business operations, or related roles, ideally in fintech, payments, banking, or other high-growth technology businesses.

  • Strong strategic and commercial judgment, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, evaluate complex trade-offs, and translate big-picture thinking into practical execution.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead teams and complex cross-functional initiatives, influence senior stakeholders, and drive outcomes in fast-paced environments.

  • Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to simplify complexity, make sound decisions, and engage effectively with executive leadership.

  • Entrepreneurial, hands-on mindset with a strong sense of ownership and willingness to get into the details to make things happen.

Preferred qualifications:

title: Director, International Tax
descriptionHtml:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths. 
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory. 

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Director, International Tax 

We are looking for an Director, International Tax to build and own the international tax function at Quince. This is the first dedicated tax hire in the company, and it arrives at the moment we need it most: Quince is entering Europe, Mexico, Australia, and numerous other countries on an aggressive timeline, and every one of those markets brings tax questions we do not currently have an in-house answer to.

Entity structure. Permanent establishment. VAT and GST registration. Withholding tax. Transfer pricing. Customs and import duty treatment. Local filing obligations we may not know exist until we have already tripped over them. The International Tax Director is the person who knows where those blind spots are before we walk into them, and who tells us what we need to do about them while it is still a decision rather than a problem.

The role reports directly to the VP of Accounting and functions as their right hand on anything tax — the person who can answer any tax question, or knows exactly how to go get the answer. This role is also the first call for the Head of International on any tax question tied to a new market, and a close partner to Legal, People Ops, and Supply Chain as the international footprint is built.

Responsibilities

  •     Serve as the tax lead on every new-market launch — assess the tax profile of a market before we enter, flag what will and won't work, and define the registrations, filings, and structural decisions required to operate compliantly from day one.
  •     Build and maintain a market-entry tax playbook and a global filing calendar, so the tenth country launch is materially faster and cleaner than the first.
  •     Advise on legal entity structure and the tax consequences of each option — branch vs. subsidiary, holding structure, where IP and inventory sit, and how intercompany flows are designed — partnering with Legal on entity timing and sequencing.
  •     Identify and manage permanent establishment risk created by employees, contractors, EOR arrangements, warehouses, third-party logistics providers, and local agents, including the tax implications of transitioning employees from EOR to local entity.
  •     Own transfer pricing end to end: intercompany agreements, pricing methodology, master file and local file documentation, country-by-country reporting where applicable, and defense of the position under audit.
  •     Own indirect tax globally — EU VAT (including OSS/IOSS, distance-selling rules, import VAT, and reverse charge), UK VAT, Mexican IVA, Australian GST and low-value imported goods rules, and the considerably more complex South American regimes — covering registration, filing, recoverability, and the operational setup behind each.

Qualifications

  •     Deep international tax capability is essential given the scope of this role — cross-border structuring, transfer pricing, treaty analysis, permanent establishment, and indirect tax across multiple regimes.
  •     Working knowledge of US federal and state taxation, including ASC 740, is a plus rather than a requirement. Our US provision and returns are prepared by an external firm; what we need is someone who can manage that firm credibly, review its work, and recognize when an answer doesn't hold up.
  •     Genuine indirect tax depth, or a demonstrated ability to research an unfamiliar country's VAT/GST regime from scratch and return with a defensible, documented answer. Knowing how to find the right answer in a new jurisdiction matters more here than having memorized any one of them.
  •     Demonstrated ability to stand up tax infrastructure where none exists, and to apply rigorous technical judgment to ambiguous, fast-moving, and incompletely specified situations.
  •     Comfortable being the only tax person in the company. This role will not be hiring a team for at least 12–18 months, and in the meantime you are both the strategist and the person doing the work.
  •     Proactive risk identifier. The most valuable thing you will do in this role is raise the issue nobody else knew to ask about.
  •     Skilled at translating complex technical tax positions into clear business language that non-tax partners can act on with confidence.
  •     Collaborative partner with a positive, solutions-oriented mindset; able to build trust quickly with Accounting, Legal, People Ops, Supply Chain, and the International team.
  •     Agile and adaptable; comfortable building and evolving processes as the international footprint matures, without being constrained by legacy approaches.
  •     Entrepreneurial mindset; equally comfortable setting global tax strategy and rolling up their sleeves to file a return.
  •     Proactive problem-solver and self-starter; energized by ambiguity and motivated to find the right answer even when no playbook exists.

Preferred:

  •     Substantial international tax experience specifically — this is the center of the role, not an adjacent skill.
  •     Demonstrated experience supporting a company through multi-country international expansion, including entity setup, indirect tax registration, and cross-border structuring.
  •     Experience supporting direct-to-consumer, retail, e-commerce, or another goods-based business with a physical supply chain strongly preferred, including exposure to customs and import duty matters.
  •     Experience selecting and managing external tax advisors across multiple jurisdictions.
  •     Practical experience with tax engines (Avalara, Vertex, or similar) and ERP tax configuration preferred.

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. 

Quince is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete your application or to perform the essential functions of a role at Quince, please let us know by completing this accommodation form. We review all requests individually and will work with you to determine appropriate accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Quince will conduct background checks in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Security Advisory: Beware of Frauds

At Quince, we're dedicated to recruiting top talent who share our drive for innovation. To safeguard candidates, Quince emphasizes legitimate recruitment practices. Initial communication is primarily via official Quince email addresses and LinkedIn; beware of deviations. Personal data and sensitive information will not be solicited during the application phase. Interviews are conducted via phone, in person, or through the approved platforms Google Meets or Zoom—never via messaging apps or other calling services. Your mission: build a category-defining brand and a world-class, AI-enabled creative organization to bring it to life.


What you’ll own

Brand creative direction

  • Strong benchmarking instincts and a clear point of view on differentiation and creative excellence.

    • You’ll Thrive in This Role If You

title: Director of Cloud Infrastructure & Security
descriptionHtml:
Vestiaire Collective is the leading global platform for desirable pre-loved fashion and a pioneer in transforming how people consume fashion. Our mission is simple: make circular fashion the norm, not the exception.
Through technology, expertise, and a highly engaged global community, we enable millions of people to buy and sell fashion in a more sustainable way. Founded in Paris in 2009, Vestiaire Collective is now a globally scaled marketplace with offices in Paris, London, Berlin, New York, Singapore, and Ho Chi Minh City, and logistics hubs across Europe, Asia, and the US. Today, we are a team of around 600 people from over 50 nationalities, united by a shared ambition: to drive meaningful change in the fashion industry. Our values, Activism, Transparency, Dedication, Greatness, and Collective, shape how we build, collaborate, and grow every day.

About the Role:

Vestiaire Collective runs a global marketplace on AWS and GCP — Kubernetes, Kafka, Terraform, Vault, Cloudflare, Datadog, a large PHP application under active modernisation, a series of microservices in different tech stacks (Goland, PHP, Node) and a fast-growing surface of AI-powered services.

As Director of Cloud Infrastructure and Security, you will lead a small team of six senior individual contributors across Cloud Infrastructure (DevOps/SRE) and Security. This is a hands-on Director role: alongside setting the strategy and roadmap, you will work directly with the team on architecture, technical decisions, incidents and delivery. You will be accountable, alongside Product Development teams, for the reliability, cost-efficiency and security posture of everything we run in production.

What you will do:

Leadership across two teams

  • Directly lead, develop and retain a small team of six (6) experienced engineers across Cloud Infrastructure and Security. This is a player-coach role without multiple management layers, so you will remain close to the team’s technical work and day-to-day priorities.

  • Define a joint roadmap for both teams, aligned to business priorities and risk appetite, and make explicit calls on what we will not do.

  • Establish clear KPIs, SLOs and risk metrics, and report regularly to leadership on reliability, cost and security posture.

  • Set the operating model: what product teams self-serve behind guardrails versus what your teams own centrally.

  • Foster a culture where reliability and security are shared accountabilities, not tickets thrown over a wall, including establishing a Security Champions model across engineering.

Cloud infrastructure, reliability and platform

  • Own our AWS and GCP footprint end to end: EKS, networking, secrets (Vault), data stores (RDS/Aurora, MSK, ElastiCache, MongoDB Atlas, OpenSearch) and the edge (Cloudflare).

  • Establish real reliability engineering practice: SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, and a business continuity plan.

  • Drive infrastructure-as-code maturity: Automating Terraform change application, advancing our move to GitOps (ArgoCD), and enforcing guardrails at creation time with policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) so provisioning is safe, self-serve and reviewable.

  • Consolidate observability into a single source of truth for metrics, logs and traces.

  • Improve developer experience and delivery throughput: CI/CD (Jenkins, GitHub Actions), paved roads, test environments on demand, and delivery metrics that hold up.

  • Own FinOps: infrastructure cost per unit of business value, cost accountability pushed back to each team, and continued run-rate reduction. Cost discipline is a first-class objective.

  • Support the modernisation of our core platform: Tech migrations, runtime and framework upgrades, and continuous database and Kubernetes upgrades.

  • Attack toil systematically: automate the recurring requests, and hand safe self-service back to product teams rather than absorbing the work.

  • Grow the foundations for AI-augmented engineering and operations

Security

  • Own security strategy and posture across cloud, application, identity, detection and response, building and improving the governance: risk register, published roadmap, remediation SLAs, and a recurring reporting cadence for leadership.

  • Strengthen cloud security posture management (CNAPP) and secure-by-default configurations across all environments.

  • Improve Embedding security into the SDLC and CI/CD: establish full static-analysis and dependency-scanning coverage with clear criteria for when critical findings block a release.

  • Mature vulnerability management, penetration testing and our bug bounty program into one prioritised program with SLAs and aging reports that measurably reduce risk.

  • Advance identity and access management toward least privilege and zero trust: automated provisioning from groups, and periodic access reviews.

  • Mature logging, detection and incident response, closing SIEM coverage gaps

  • Set guardrails for safe AI adoption (shadow AI outside approved paths, data and prompt leakage, prompt injection, model abuse) and defend against AI-enabled fraud and phishing.

  • Ensure compliance with GDPR, PCI DSS v4, NIS2, and CIS v8, including a maintained, reusable evidence library rather than evidence gathered on request.

  • Collaboration with legal and finance teams on compliance and forensic investigation topics

  • Manage third-party and supply-chain risk with vendor tiering and a recurring review cadence.

  • Own the security-built services your team already runs (back-office authentication and ACL, banning/fraud tooling, phone verification) and decide what to keep, hand over or retire.

  • Own endpoint security and partner closely with Corporate IT on device and identity coverage.

  • Keep security awareness and training relevant to a threat landscape that now includes AI-enabled social engineering.

Who you are:

  • 8+ years with a Significant experience in Infrastructure, Platform Engineering, DevOps, SRE or Cloud Security, including experience leading engineers.

  • You may currently be an Engineering Manager, Senior Engineering Manager or Head of who is ready to broaden your scope and step into a first Director role.

  • Strong practical experience with public cloud, ideally AWS, Kubernetes and Infrastructure-as-Code, with the willingness to remain close to architecture, incidents and technical delivery.

  • Track record establishing reliability practice at scale — SLOs, incident management, on-call, capacity planning, disaster recovery.

  • Demonstrable cloud cost optimisation / FinOps results at meaningful scale.

  • Strong grounding in cloud and application security fundamentals — IAM, network security, secrets management, CSPM, OWASP Top 10 — and the judgement to know when to hire the depth you don't have.

  • Working knowledge of compliance frameworks (GDPR, DORA, PCI DSS, NIS2) and how to turn requirements into practical controls.

  • Experience leading through incidents and security events under pressure.

  • Excellent communication skills: able to make a technical trade-off legible to a CFO and a risk decision legible to an engineer.

  • Comfortable operating with a lean team — ruthless prioritisation, automation over headcount, pragmatism over perfection.

Our Tech Stack includes:

  • AWS cloud (primary), GCP, Kubernetes, Vault, Cloudflare, Datadog, ArgoCD, Okta. Applications are built on top of PHP 8, Golang and Node.js, using MariaDB, MongoDB and Kafka.

What We Offer

  • Purpose-driven work at scale
    Join a company reshaping the fashion industry towards circularity, you directly contributes to reducing waste and extending the life of luxury items.
  • High-impact scope & ownership
    Work on products used globally, where your decisions have immediate, measurable impact on millions of users across 70+ countries.
  • A truly international environment
    Collaborate with a diverse team of 50+ nationalities across Paris, London, Berlin, New York, Singapore, and Ho Chi Minh City.
  • Career acceleration in a fast-moving scale-up
    Take ownership early, grow fast, and shape your path, as an expert or a future leader.
  • Learning & growth as a priority
    Dedicated budget, continuous feedback culture, and opportunities to work on cutting-edge topics (AI, marketplace dynamics, scalability, etc.).
  • Flexible ways of working
    Hybrid model (typically 2 days remote per week), with trust and autonomy at the core of how we operate.
  • Give back through action
    2 paid days per year to support a cause of your choice and actively contribute to positive impact beyond your day-to-day role.
  • Competitive compensation & benefits
    Including bonus, health coverage, lunch vouchers, Gym-Pass, and additional legal perks depending on your location.

Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds including women, people with disabilities, and other marginalized communities, are less likely to apply unless they meet 100% of the criteria.

At Vestiaire Collective, we believe diversity drives better decisions, stronger products, and more meaningful impact.
If this role excites you but your experience doesn’t align perfectly, we still encourage you to apply, your perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

Vestiaire Collective is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

PS: We take candidate experience seriously, and your safety too !

  • Ask for payment or banking information at any stage of the process

descriptionHtml:
About BJAK

BJAK is Southeast Asia’s largest digital insurance platform, expanding financial access through automation, data, and digital scale. As we grow across markets, we are committed to building a platform that is safe, compliant, and trusted.

We are hiring a Director of Compliance and Risk (UK) to lead regulatory strategy, risk governance, and compliance operations for our UK market entry and expansion alongside the CEO. This role is expected to hold the SMF16 (Compliance Oversight) Senior Management Function once approved, and will act as our primary point of contact with the FCA.

This is a build role: you'll be creating frameworks, policies, and controls from scratch rather than inheriting an existing function.

 

Why This Role Matters

The Director of Compliance and Risk (UK) will:

  • Design and enforce compliance frameworks that enable safe scaling of digital financial services.

  • Ensure BJAK operates in accordance with UK regulatory standards, especially FCA requirements.

  • Protect consumers through transparent, fair, and ethical practices.

  • Establish BJAK as a trusted partner with regulators, partners, and industry stakeholders.

  • Build compliance capability and culture across the company.

 

What You Will Do

Regulatory Leadership & Strategy

  • Develop and maintain compliance frameworks aligned with UK regulatory requirements.

  • Lead regulatory readiness for market entry, licensing, and ongoing supervision.

  • Serve as the primary contact with the FCA and relevant UK bodies.

  • Interpret regulatory changes and guide business strategy accordingly.

 

Risk Governance & Compliance Operations

  • Build policies and controls covering AML, KYC, data privacy, consumer duty, distribution, and claims-related compliance.

  • Conduct risk assessments and implement remediation plans for identified gaps.

  • Establish monitoring, testing, and reporting processes for ongoing compliance.

  • Ensure internal audits, compliance reviews, and control testing are operationalised.

 

Consumer Protection & Business Integrity

  • Embed fairness, transparency, and responsible selling throughout the organisation.

  • Oversee product compliance, marketing reviews, pricing governance, and distribution oversight.

  • Implement complaint handling frameworks aligned with regulatory standards.

 

Cross-Functional Support & Training

  • Partner with product, operations, legal, marketing, and commercial teams to ensure compliant execution.

  • Provide guidance on regulatory implications of new products, partnerships, or distribution models.

  • Deliver training to ensure teams understand and execute compliance responsibilities.

 

You Will Thrive in This Role If You

  • See compliance as a strategic enabler, not a blocker.

  • Operate with high integrity, sound judgment, and strong attention to detail.

  • Communicate clearly and influence leaders using data and logic.

  • Enjoy building frameworks and scaling systems from early-stage to mature environments.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, evolving settings where regulation meets innovation.

 

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of compliance, risk, or regulatory experience within financial services, insurance, insurtech, or fintech.

  • Deep understanding of UK regulatory frameworks, including FCA rules and consumer duty requirements.

  • Experience in compliance for digital platforms, distribution, or insurance products (preferred).

  • Proven ability to design policies, conduct risk assessments, and manage complex compliance programs.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including dealing with regulators.

 

Bonus (Nice to Have)

  • Experience in start-up or high-growth environments.

  • Previous SMF experience.

  • Background in insurtech, digital distribution, or online marketplaces.

  • Knowledge of GDPR, AML, sanctions, or cross-border compliance.

 

Location Requirement

  • This role is based in the UK. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our London office at least 3 days per week.

 

Why Join Us

  • Shape compliance for a fast-growing international fintech-insurtech platform.

  • Build frameworks that enable safe, inclusive financial access at scale.

  • Work closely with leadership and regulators to drive responsible innovation.

  • Competitive compensation with long-term growth and international career opportunities.


Compensations Range

  • We offer a highly competitive package, ranging from £100,000 to £150,000, reflecting both experience and suitability for this pivotal role.

title: Director of Cybersecurity & IT
descriptionHtml:
Hi, we’re Back Market.

We’re here to help make tech reliable, affordable, and better than new. We're a global marketplace for refurbished devices, helping lower our collective environmental impact by providing trustworthy, affordable tech with 92% less carbon emissions than new.

Yep, you read that right. Turns out refurbished tech is way better for the planet than new. In fact, With every device purchased on Back Market, our positive impact on the planet grows. From our Customer Care representatives to our software engineer, every individual at Back Market cuts the planet — and consumers — a break. Our mission is simple: to do more with what we already have.

Are you ready to join us?

Back Market is looking for a Director of Cybersecurity & IT to define and lead the next phase of our security and technology operations maturity. Reporting to the VP of Platform Engineering, you will be a strategic leader at the intersection of cybersecurity, IT, risk, compliance, and business growth.

You will lead a multi-disciplinary organization through its existing functional managers, creating the clarity, operating rhythm, and investment focus needed to protect Back Market while enabling the company to move quickly. The scope includes cybersecurity strategy and risk management, security operations, governance and compliance, IT operations, IT support, and the corporate technology foundations that keep our people productive and our business resilient.

 

This is a director-level role, not a super-sized operational manager role. You will not be expected to personally own every process or make every technical decision. Your impact will come from setting direction, developing leaders, aligning stakeholders, making sound investment choices, and ensuring that the organization delivers measurable outcomes. You will be the senior voice who makes cybersecurity and IT understandable, actionable, and connected to the business.

 

To know more about our engineering teams:

  • A video of our VP Platform: https://youtu.be/zvTlw4BNNdc

  • Our company purpose: http://bit.ly/3OsScpl

  • Our engineering blog: https://bit.ly/3ASJNID

How we work with the existing teams 💚

 

The Director sets direction, creates clarity, secures resources, removes organizational obstacles, develops leaders, and ensures that the overall portfolio delivers against agreed outcomes. The functional managers and senior experts retain ownership of day-to-day execution, technical practices, operational processes, and delivery within their domains. The Director creates the conditions for those leaders to succeed and makes sure their work adds up to a coherent company-wide strategy.

Your next missions 👇

 

Set the strategy, roadmap, and investment priorities

  • Define and evolve a multi-year Cybersecurity & IT strategy aligned with Back Market's business goals, risk appetite, technology strategy, and growth plans

  • Translate that strategy into a focused portfolio of initiatives, with clear outcomes, sequencing, ownership, dependencies, and measures of success

  • Own the operating rhythm for the full scope: planning, budgeting, program tracking, KPI and SLA reporting, risk reviews, and executive communication

  • Make pragmatic investment and prioritization recommendations, balancing resilience, customer trust, regulatory expectations, employee experience, and engineering velocity

  • Establish the governance forums and decision mechanisms needed to keep priorities clear and accountability visible

 

Lead and grow a high-performing leadership organization

  • Lead through the managers and senior individual contributors responsible for Security Operations, Governance Risk & Compliance, IT Operations Engineering, IT Support, and relevant security engineering or product security capabilities

  • Coach, challenge, and develop your leaders, helping them grow their scope, judgment, influence, and ability to build strong teams of their own

  • Create clear career paths, succession plans, and development opportunities across the organization

  • Build a high-trust environment where teams have genuine ownership, collaborate across boundaries, and are encouraged to improve how work gets done

  • Attract and retain exceptional talent, define what great leadership and execution look like, and continuously raise the bar without creating unnecessary bureaucracy

  • Ensure that responsibilities, decision rights, and interfaces between the teams are explicit, understood, and respected

 

Turn cybersecurity into a business enabler

  • Act as a trusted advisor to the VP of Engineering, CTO, Executive Committee, and senior leaders across the business

  • Explain complex security, IT, and risk topics in clear business language, including the trade-offs, options, costs, and consequences of different decisions

  • Engage with Heads of and cross-functional streams across Back Market to advocate for security and resilience in all areas of the business

  • Build alignment rather than relying on authority, and help teams adopt secure and resilient ways of working because they understand the rationale and value

  • Partner with Finance and senior technology leadership on investment cases, budget stewardship, vendor strategy, and the value delivered by the portfolio

 

Steer enterprise cyber risk and trust

  • Own the cyber risk management process at the strategic level, using the GRC framework as the foundation for security decisions and prioritization

  • Ensure that material risks, control gaps, exceptions, and remediation plans are visible, understood, and actively managed

  • Escalate critical risks when they exceed the organization's risk appetite or require executive arbitration

  • Support security compliance efforts across the organization, ensuring alignment and buy-in from peers and key stakeholders across ISO 27001, PCI DSS, GDPR, NIS2, and contractual partner requirements

  • Partner with the VP Legal and DPO on the company's data privacy strategy, ensuring privacy and security requirements are considered early in business, product, and technology decisions

  • Represent Back Market's security maturity and risk posture to investors, auditors, regulators, strategic partners, and major customers

  • Serve as the senior escalation point for major or complex security incidents, ensuring the right executive communication, decision-making, learning, and follow-through without displacing the operational ownership of the incident response teams

 

Enable secure products and resilient technology

  • Partner with Engineering, Product, and other Bureau of Technology directors to ensure security requirements are integrated into product and feature development from the beginning

  • Sponsor and evolve Product Security and secure software development lifecycle practices, including security-by-design, threat modeling, appropriate testing, and pragmatic guardrails

  • Ensure the security roadmap addresses the most important risks across cloud infrastructure, corporate systems, identity and access, endpoints, applications, data, and third-party services

  • Set the expectations for Security Operations across threat intelligence, vulnerability management, security monitoring, incident readiness, risk assessment and project design reviews, fraud support, AI security, and associated SLA and KPI tracking

  • Ensure IT Operations and IT Support provide a reliable, scalable, and high-quality experience for Back Makers across our global offices and remote workforce

  • Champion automation, standardization, and engineering-led approaches that reduce manual work and improve reliability, while leaving day-to-day technical ownership with the appropriate functional teams

 

Build security culture and external credibility

  • Foster a security-aware culture through clear communication about the evolving threat landscape, key initiatives, practical expectations, and the role every Back Maker plays in protecting the company

  • Sponsor awareness, education, and Security Champion programs that make secure behavior accessible and relevant to different audiences

  • Represent Back Market in relevant security communities, industry groups, partner forums, and regulatory conversations

  • Build trusted relationships with strategic technology partners, auditors, insurers, and external security providers

  • Help Back Market demonstrate that strong security, responsible technology, and business agility reinforce one another


You could be a good fit if you've:

  • A proven track record of building, scaling, and developing organizations that span multiple security and/or IT domains

  • 12 to 15+ years of experience across cybersecurity, information security, IT, or related technology leadership roles, including at least 5 years leading managers and multi-team organizations

  • Experience operating as a strategic partner to a CTO, VP Engineering, executive committee, or equivalent senior leadership group

  • Proven expertise and a solid grasp of the domains listed below: security operations, cyber risk and governance, compliance and assurance, security architecture, product security, cloud security, IT operations, or corporate technology

  • Demonstrated ability to turn business strategy and risk appetite into a practical security and IT roadmap, investment plan, and operating model

  • Experience communicating security and technology risk to executive, board-level, investor, partner, audit, and non-technical audiences

  • A mature, risk-based approach. You understand that perfect security does not exist, and that good leadership means making explicit, informed trade-offs and focusing resources where they have the greatest impact

  • Experience leading through managers and senior experts, with a genuine passion for developing people, building leadership capability, and creating meaningful career paths

  • Strong understanding of modern cloud, SaaS, identity, endpoint, application, data, and infrastructure security concepts, even if you are not the deepest technical expert in every domain

  • Experience with security-by-design, secure software development lifecycle practices, and effective partnership with Engineering and Product teams

  • Excellent written and verbal communication in English, with the ability to make complex topics clear, concrete, and compelling. French is a plus

  • The judgment, calm, and influence required to operate effectively in ambiguity, during incidents, and across competing stakeholder priorities

  • Genuine excitement about Back Market's mission and the belief that cybersecurity and IT are essential enablers of sustainable growth

    Nice to have

  • A recognized certification such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, CCSP, or an equivalent professional qualification

  • Experience with ISO 27001, PCI DSS, GDPR, NIS2, or other relevant European regulatory and assurance frameworks

  • Experience with GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, modern cloud-native security tooling, or SaaS-first environments

  • Experience in marketplace, e-commerce, fintech, or another business with meaningful customer, partner, or regulatory trust requirements

  • Experience with AI security, fraud prevention, third-party risk, or software supply chain security

  • Experience working in a fast-growing, international organization with distributed

    1. Phone call with Marie, Technical Talent Acquisition Partner - 45 min

    2. Deep-dive interview on Leadership and management with your future manager, the VP of Engineering - 60 min

    3. Meeting a peer Engineering Director and an Engineering Manager - 60 min

    4. Technical interview with Cybersec and IT team - 45 min

    5. Stakeholder interview with cross-functional partners, including the CTO and relevant Security and IT leaders - 60 min

WHY SHOULD YOU JOIN US ? ✌🏼

At Back Market, we’re committed to hiring and supporting diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives — it’s one of the reasons we’re such a high-scoring certified B Corp company (93.2).

At Back Market, we strive to create a workplace that embodies the world we’re trying to change. We’ve embedded our diversity, equity, and inclusion principles into our DNA — from dedicated staff to employee resource groups to our company values.

We know that the perfect background for a role doesn’t mean the perfect fit — we encourage you to apply for a role even if you think you may not have all the qualifications.

title: Director of Engineering - Risk and Compliance
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

We’reCheckout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

Role overview | Context

Checkout.com built its name serving the world's largest enterprises. We're now growing into many more types of customer: businesses of every size, including self-serve, startups integrating straight from our docs, and platforms (software companies, payfacs and marketplaces) that onboard thousands of sellers through our APIs. As our product range grows, that takes us from thousands of customers to millions.

At that scale, the decision about who we work with, and on what terms, can't be a manual review at the end of a sales process. It has to be a product. It decides how quickly a good business goes live, how much it costs us to serve them, and how confident our regulators and scheme partners are in us. We're looking for a senior Engineering leader to own that decision.

This team decides which businesses we can work with and on what terms. It covers business verification, screening, underwriting, ongoing monitoring and financial crime. It's a shared platform that serves every one of our businesses. Its users are our customers (directly, or through the platforms they sign up with) and, internally, our Risk, Compliance and Financial Crime teams and the analysts who run reviews and investigations.

Much of what we have today was built segment by segment and market by market, for a smaller number of large customers. The next chapter is one opinionated, configurable decisioning platform. Enterprise, platform and SMB customers should all run on the same foundations, with the right depth of checks and the right terms for each. That way a new product, segment or market doesn't mean rebuilding our controls, and this team isn't on the critical path for every launch.

Role overview | Risk, Verification & Compliance

The remit covers:

  • Risk decisioning: underwriting, risk tiering, exposure limits, reserves and settlement terms, and when to restrict or offboard, re-assessed across the customer lifecycle.

  • Business verification: company, ownership, document, bank account and website checks, run once for every segment.

  • Financial crime: sanctions and PEP screening, AML and transaction monitoring, and the controls, audit trails and reporting behind our regulatory obligations.

  • Decisioning platform: the shared infrastructure that runs these checks automatically for every market and customer type.

You'll partner closely with the teams that own onboarding and identity verification.

Role overview | Remit and Responsibilities

You'll be comfortable building and scaling critical platforms in a regulated environment, where correctness, auditability and availability matter as much as speed. You'll balance two goals that are often in tension: making it fast and easy for good businesses to work with us, and keeping bad actors out and the business compliant.

This is a change role. You'll assess what we have, set a clear direction, and move us from segment-specific, analyst-led processes to an automated decisioning platform, without pausing the business while you do it. You'll do this in close partnership with Product, Risk, Compliance, Financial Crime and Legal, and with the leaders of the businesses that depend on the platform.

You'll directly lead an established team of engineers and managers of varying seniorities. Amongst other duties, you'll have impact across:

  • Setting the technical vision and strategy for Risk, Verification & Compliance. That includes deciding what we build once and share, and what each segment, product or market configures.

  • Building a decisioning platform that automates the decisions that don't need a human, safely, and sends the rest to the right analyst with the context they need. Our automation rate sets our cost to onboard and to serve.

  • Making risk dynamic across the customer lifecycle. New businesses start on terms that match the signals we see: limits, reserves and settlement speed. Those terms relax automatically as the business trades well, and we act quickly when the signals change. This starts with simple rules and evolves into machine learning.

  • Making decisions explainable, so that customers, partners and our own analysts understand why a decision was made and what happens next.

  • Giving Risk and Compliance the dials. Acceptance criteria, early-life controls and policy should be configuration that can be changed, tested and measured by cohort, not a code change.

  • Keeping our financial crime controls ahead of growth. Screening and monitoring have to scale from large enterprises to a very large base of smaller businesses, through new channels, payment methods and products.

  • Leading the design and delivery of verification, screening, underwriting and monitoring systems that are accurate, auditable and highly available.

  • Representing Engineering in regulatory, audit, scheme and partner conversations where needed.

  • Managing and developing a high-performing team of individual contributor (IC) Engineers and Engineering Managers, providing guidance, support and career development.

  • Striving for best practice on hiring, coaching and enablement, and being a magnet for top talent.

Role overview | Desired Background, Core Competencies

The ideal candidate for the role will bring:

  • Experience leading multi-level engineering organisations (EMs and ICs) through growth and change, with a track record of developing leaders, not just hiring them.

  • A record of transforming critical platforms while the business kept running: multi-year re-architecture, migrations, or consolidating several systems into one.

  • Experience building and operating mission-critical decisioning or rules platforms at scale. Ideally these served several customer segments, products or markets from a shared foundation.

  • Experience in a regulated environment (financial services, payments or similar), where compliance, auditability and risk are part of the engineering problem.

  • Deep technical understanding of cloud-native, distributed and data-heavy systems, including how to run ML models safely in production.

  • Exceptional collaboration skills, with a proven ability to partner with senior cross-functional stakeholders, particularly in Risk, Compliance, Financial Crime and Legal, and to make clear trade-offs in a complex stakeholder landscape.

  • Ideally, domain knowledge in KYB, AML and financial crime, underwriting, fraud or merchant risk. Experience with self-serve or high-volume onboarding, or with platforms and their sub-merchants, is a strong plus.

  • Humility, low ego and an ideal ambassador for our mission, values and operating principles.

If you feel that you don't meet all the requirements but think you might still be right for the role, please consider continuing in the process. We're always keen to build relationships with leaders who resonate with our mission and values.

 

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

descriptionHtml:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

WHY JOIN US

  • The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.
  • You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms.
  • We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Flight Control Systems team at Stark is responsible for safety-critical architectures, control laws, and integrated flight software across autonomous defense platforms. Working closely with systems engineering, aerodynamics, and software teams, we bridge theoretical control theory and field-tested hardware deployment. Our mission is to ensure robust, high-performance, and resilient flight behavior in highly dynamic and contested environments.

YOUR MISSION

As Director of Flight Control Systems (FCS), reporting directly to our VP of Hardware, you will lead the end-to-end development, verification, and qualification of next-generation flight control architectures. You will define the technical roadmap, build and mentor an elite team of control and software engineers, and oversee safety-critical flight law implementation from initial modeling to flight testing.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AT STARK

  • Lead and scale the Flight Control Systems team, setting engineering standards, performance goals, and development roadmaps.
  • Drive the architectural design of fly-by-wire flight control software, sensor fusion algorithms, and actuation control loops.
  • Oversee Model-in-the-Loop (MIL), Software-in-the-Loop (SIL), and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing and verification frameworks.
  • Collaborate with systems engineering and flight test crews to validate control system performance during flight test campaigns.
  • Ensure compliance with safety-critical aerospace and defense standards (e.g., DO-178C, DO-254, or military flight clearance frameworks).
  • Interface with internal cross-functional leadership and external partners to align system requirements with platform capabilities.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION

  • Degree in Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Control Theory, or a related technical field.
  • Proven leadership experience managing engineering teams in flight control systems or safety-critical aerospace development.
  • Deep expertise in flight dynamics, control laws development (PID, LQR, H-infinity, adaptive control), and MATLAB/Simulink modeling.
  • Hands-on background in auto-code generation, embedded C/C++ development, and flight software integration.
  • Track record of taking flight control systems from initial concept through ground and flight testing.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience with autonomous defense platforms or unmanned aerial systems (UAS).
  • Familiarity with military certification processes and flight test safety protocols.
  • Knowledge of modern software development practices (CI/CD, automated testing, Git).

title: Director of International Product
descriptionHtml:
About Lyra
Lyra Health is the leading provider of mental health solutions for employers supporting more than 20 million people globally. The company has delivered 13 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 20 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness and cost efficiency. Extensive peer-reviewed research confirms Lyra’s transformative care model helps people recover twice as fast and results in a 26% annual reduction in overall healthcare claims costs. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions.

Lyra is looking for a visionary and strategic Director, International Product to lead and scale our global mental health offerings. As Lyra grows around the world, you’ll shape how we deliver high-quality, culturally relevant care to members, providers, and employers in every market we serve.

You’ll serve as the connective tissue between our global commercial ambitions and technical execution, guiding multiple simultaneous initiatives and building a platform-first, repeatable engine for international growth. Working alongside senior leadership, you’ll own the strategic vision, delivery, and performance of the international product suite.

The leaders who thrive in this role pair high standards with real care for the people around them. They build strong relationships across the organization, earn influence through trust and clarity, and bring steady, energizing leadership to their teams, especially when the path ahead is uncertain


What You'll Do:
  • Global Product Vision & Strategy: Define the multi-year vision and roadmap for Lyra’s international product suite, grounded in market analysis, competitive insight, and firsthand understanding of the members, providers, and clients we serve in each region. Synthesize global market signals into a clear point of view on where to invest for the greatest impact for global employers.
  • Product Scope & Ownership: Hold full lifecycle responsibility for the scoping, development, and delivery of member experiences and the underlying platform infrastructure across four major product lines: International Lyra Workforce Mental Health (WFMH), Global Lyra Wellbeing, 10 Local Lyra Wellbeing products, and other product surface areas as needed.
  • Platform-First Scale: Lead the evolution of our international offerings onto a unified global platform, with automated workflows that make each new client launch faster and more repeatable than the last. Champion the localization of core capabilities, including billing, eligibility, and provider management, so they flex gracefully across markets.
  • Roadmap Stewardship: Balance the needs of today’s clients with durable, long-term platform investments. Make clear, well-reasoned tradeoffs, explain the “why” behind them in a way that brings people along, and have the conviction to say “not yet” when that’s what best serves members and the business.
  • Leadership & Team Development: Build and lead the International Product team. Hire and grow exceptional people, including leaders whose strengths go beyond your own, and invest in their development through candid, caring feedback and meaningful ownership. Your success is measured by how well your team thrives: clearing the path, providing context, and creating the conditions for others to do their best work.
  • Business Ownership & Resourcing: Create and manage the annual budget for International Product. Assess resourcing needs and build compelling business cases to secure the investment needed to reach ambitious growth targets.
  • Cost-to-Serve & Performance Insight: Partner with the Data organization to build a single, trusted view of international performance, giving leadership clear visibility into margins, ROI, and utilization. Define and track the product metrics that measure success, and identify opportunities to streamline and automate so global products are built for long-term profitability.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Serve as the central connector across Product, Engineering, Data, Operations, Clinical Governance, Legal, and Compliance. Build trusted relationships across regions and time zones, including in our local operations work toward win-win outcomes amid competing priorities, and ensure clinical quality and local regulatory requirements are built into the product lifecycle from the start.
  • Go-To-Market Partnership: Act as a trusted partner to Go-To-Market and Client Services teams. Serve as the product voice in high-stakes, C-level client conversations and complex RFPs, bringing the technical and clinical confidence that helps Lyra win and retain large-scale global contracts.
  • AI-Enabled Product Excellence: Maintain a high bar for product craft and apply AI with purpose, both in our products, where it can meaningfully expand access and improve care, and in how we work. Model how AI can accelerate research, synthesis, planning, and execution, and help your team adopt tools and practices that drive efficiency, effectiveness, and happiness.

    • What You'll Bring:
  • Experience: Several years in product management, strategy, or technical operations.
  • Leadership: Several years of people leadership, with a track record of building strong teams and coaching talent to grow beyond their current roles.
  • Global Product Expertise: Experience launching and scaling products across multiple countries, including localizing for language, culture, and care norms, and navigating regional privacy and regulatory frameworks (e.g., GDPR, data residency). A natural instinct to design for local context, informed by real cultural fluency.
  • Platform & Enterprise Architecture: Deep understanding of bringing multiple systems together onto a unified global platform and reducing the effort required for each new client launch.
  • Commercial & Financial Acumen: Advanced skills in multivariable planning, budget ownership, and resource forecasting in a complex, matrixed environment. You think like a business owner and use data on product health, margin, ROI, and utilization to guide strategy.
  • Executive Influence & Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can distill complexity into a crisp narrative, write a document that drives a decision, and adapt your message for engineers, clinicians, and C-level executives alike. A demonstrated track record of influencing senior leaders and key external stakeholders through credibility and trust, along with strong negotiation skills.
  • High Performance under Complexity: Ability to analyze changing, multivariable situations and set objectives with high impact on company goals. You make sound calls with incomplete information, move comfortably between the details and the big picture, keep momentum when plans shift, and stay composed and solutions-oriented when headwinds arise.
  • Practical AI Fluency: Hands-on experience using AI to meaningfully accelerate your own work and your team’s, with the discernment to know where it adds real value.
  • Culture & Psychological Safety: A model of Lyra’s values who fosters psychological safety across the team, welcomes nuanced feedback, and makes it safe for team members to voice differing opinions. You hold strong opinions loosely, change your mind when the evidence warrants, and share credit freely.
  • Mission & People Focus: A passion for Lyra’s mission. Your curiosity and empathy come naturally: they show up in the questions you ask, the time you spend with members, providers, and clients, and the products you build as a result.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) required; MBA or equivalent professional experience preferred.

title: Director of Operations, Slate Development
descriptionHtml:
Scopely is looking for a Director, Slate Operations to join our Slate Development Group team in the UK remotely or in Barcelona, on a flexible hybrid model.

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play every day - whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily. 

Slate Operations keeps Scopely's game development slate moving. We oversee execution and cross-functional alignment across the games in development — connecting game teams and central teams so decisions get made once and stick, running the cadence that keeps everyone aligned, and clearing the path so teams can build.

What You'll Do:

We're looking for a Director, Slate Operations to own this end to end. There are two sides to it: keeping the Group running as an organization — its cadence, process, and the day-to-day support the Game Board, Head of Slate Development and leadership team rely on — and running program management for the Game Development Framework (GDF) so games move cleanly from concept to launch. You'll sit inside the Slate Development Group but work with every part of Scopely: game teams, divisional leadership, finance, strategy, and corporate development.

  • Be the operational point of contact for specific in-development games — running the GDF cadence and connecting game and central teams so decisions get made once and aren't re-litigated. The main goal is to be the end to end steward for game teams in the game development framework.
  • Deliver operational excellence within our internal team, shaping our service model, priorities, and ways of working. Evolve our capabilities as needs change.
  • Drive the cross-slate operating model so independent game teams reuse what already works instead of rebuilding it.
  • Bring structure to consequential decisions — organize the inputs, assumptions, and trade-offs early so the owners and the room can reach real alignment before committing.
  • Own a capstone project — one meaty area you drive end to end, for example: evolving the GDF, owning launch readiness, or operationalizing central partnerships, depending on where the need is. 
  • Keep investment decisions well-informed — track progress across games at different stages, and surface Greenlight Case, budget, staffing, and dependency status so leadership can challenge and decide.
  • Unblock teams through the development cycle, especially at launch readiness, by clearing operational issues with central partners (legal, IT, procurement, finance, logistics) so teams stay focused on the game. Partner with marketing, strategy, and divisional leadership so launches go out clean.
  • Give teams operational support — production perspective, process, facilitation, and help navigating the GDF.
  • Operationalize playtests and validation — help build and run research, playtest, and validation plans, and package the findings so vertical owners and leaders can form the recommendation.
  • Utilize the latest AI technologies to keep information flowing — the dashboards, status, and key dates people need to see, without the overhead.

What We’re Looking For: 

  • Bachelor's degree, MBA a plus — or the equivalent in experience.
  • 10+ years in program/project management across tech and direct-to-consumer businesses, at least 5 of them in games, working within or alongside a development team.
  • You know how games get made and sold — development, publishing, platforms, business models. You don't need to have shipped one yourself, but you get what game teams are up against.
  • You've supported senior execs in a fast-moving environment and you like the pace — taking initiative, juggling priorities, switching gears without losing the thread.
  • You can run a lot of projects at once, ideally a mix of R&D and live.
  • You're comfortable in ambiguity and good at creating clarity for other people. You make sound calls in the company's interest and know when to escalate.
  • You can hold your own with P&Ls and free-to-play KPIs.
  • You spot the process that's slowing people down and fix it — and you'll push back and start the right debate when it matters.
  • You build trust with all kinds of people at every level and don't flinch at the hard conversations — with the presence to grow into a partner to senior game leaders over time.
  • You write clearly and fast, and you can build a strong deck with cross-functional input.
  • Detail and organization come naturally to you.
  • Low ego, business outcomes first, open to feedback — and genuinely curious about every part of the business.
  • You play games and care about the industry.

About Scopely

Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.

Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.

Scopely has global operations and partners across four continents in more than a dozen countries worldwide. For more information, visit: https://www.scopely.com/. 

Notice to Candidates: Scopely will never request payment or financial information during the application or hiring process. Please apply only through our official website and verify that all Talent Partner communications come from an email address ending in @scopely.com.

Should you have any questions or encounter any fraudulent requests/emails/websites, please immediately contact ----- Our job applicant privacy policies are available here: California Privacy Notice and EEA/UK Privacy Notice.

Employment at Scopely is based solely on a person's merit and qualifications. Scopely does not discriminate against any employee or applicant because of race, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding), or any other basis protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.

descriptionHtml:
🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us. 

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

📍London / UK Remote | 💰 £140,000 - £165,000 + Equity + Benefits ✨
