descriptionHtml:
About Virtual Identity

 

Virtual Identity (VI) is a digital agency built on Human-Centered Business Growth: combining empathy for people with insight from data to drive real digital success. With around 140 colleagues across Freiburg, Munich, Vienna, and Porto (and remote), we cover the full spectrum from Consulting and UX Research to UX/UI Design, Software Development, and Digital Marketing — always learning in close collaboration with our clients.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer at VI, you sit at the intersection of client, product, and engineering. You're not building in isolation from a backlog handed down by someone else — you go into deep, sustained virtual immersion with the client, understand their real operational problems, and ship working software that solves them, fast. You prototype, integrate, and iterate directly with the people who will use what you build, then help harden it into something production-ready with our delivery teams.

You also bring a well-founded understanding of agentic engineering — not just using AI coding assistants, but genuinely understanding how agents plan, use tools, and fail, and applying that thinking to how you build, integrate, and automate in the field.

This role suits someone who's equally comfortable in a client workshop, a codebase, and a data pipeline — and who gets energy from ambiguity rather than needing it resolved before starting.

 

What you will do:

  • Embed with client teams to observe workflows, diagnose bottlenecks, and identify where custom software can create outsized impact.

  • Rapidly prototype and deploy solutions — internal tools, integrations, automations, data pipelines — directly in the client's environment.

  • Translate messy, real-world requirements into working code without waiting for a fully specified brief.

  • Own the full loop: build, deploy, get feedback from actual users within days, iterate.

  • Use agentic engineering practices — not just AI-assisted coding, but designing workflows, automations, and integrations that leverage agents as a core part of the solution, where it genuinely helps the client.

  • Work closely with VI's UX, consulting, and cloud-native engineering teams to transition prototypes into scalable, supportable production systems.

  • Navigate client infrastructure, security constraints, and existing systems (cloud platforms, APIs, legacy tools) pragmatically.

  • Act as a trusted technical voice in client conversations — you can whiteboard an architecture and defend it in the same meeting.

  • Travel to client sites as needed (frequency depends on engagement).

    What we expect:

  • Strong full-stack or cloud-native engineering experience, with a track record of shipping real software, not just prototypes that die in a demo.

  • Comfort working directly with non-technical stakeholders and translating their problems into technical solutions on the fly.

  • Solid grounding in at least one modern backend stack and one frontend stack, plus working knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).

  • Experience with APIs, data integration, and automation — you can connect systems that were never designed to talk to each other.

  • Real, well-founded knowledge of agentic engineering — you understand the underlying concepts (agent planning, tool use, context management, orchestration, evaluation), not just the tool names, and you've applied that thinking to real work, not side projects.

  • A bias toward action: you'd rather build a rough version and test it with real users than perfect a spec.

  • Strong communication skills — you can explain a technical trade-off to a client stakeholder without jargon.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and shifting priorities; forward deployed work is inherently unstructured.

  • Willingness to travel to client sites.

  • Experience in an agency, consultancy, or client-facing technical role (nice to have).

  • Familiarity with UX research or design collaboration workflows (nice to have).

  • Exposure to enterprise integration patterns or legacy system modernization (nice to have).

  • Hands-on experience building or deploying agentic systems for a client, not just personal productivity use (nice to have).

  • A relevant degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field — but we care more about what you've built (nice to have).

What you can expect from us

 

Exciting projects with well-known brands, a team of motivated colleagues who genuinely enjoy working together, and continuous learning through our VI Academy. Whether you're based in one of our offices or working fully remote, we give you the room to grow — professionally and personally.

 

Sound like your kind of place? We'd love to hear from you.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About SANOVIO

SANOVIO makes buying and selling medical supplies easier. On our AI platform, hospitals, purchasing groups and suppliers work together in one place instead of juggling emails, Excel lists and disconnected systems. Hospitals can buy together, and suppliers reach that bundled demand more easily.

Our software, SANOVIO aOS, uses AI agents to take over the tedious work: cleaning up product data, comparing requests and offers, bundling demand and keeping orders on track. It connects to the systems our customers already use.

When needed, SANOVIO Fulfillment also takes care of the physical side: finding manufacturers worldwide, quality checks, financing, warehousing and delivery. The goal is simple: less admin work, and more time and money for patient care.

About the Role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you are the bridge between our customers and our product, on both sides of the platform: healthcare providers and purchasing groups on one side, suppliers on the other. At its core, this role is about talking to customers. You work directly with procurement, logistics and IT teams, understand how they really work and make SANOVIO work inside their world: you connect our platform to their ERP, materials management and supplier systems, untangle their data and processes, and ship the solutions that make them successful.

This role is for builders who are just as comfortable in a customer workshop as in a code editor. Whether you studied business informatics, industrial engineering, computer science or mathematics, or bring experience in technical product management, product engineering or software engineering with a strong design sense: what matters is that you love solving messy real-world problems end to end. We hire for skills, not for degrees.

Tasks

  • Talking to our customers every day: leading workshops with procurement managers, IT departments and suppliers, and being a trusted partner for our customers

  • Owning customer implementations end to end, from kickoff and process analysis to go-live and continuous improvement

  • Analyzing and redesigning procurement processes on both sides, from requisition and ordering at healthcare providers to order handling at suppliers, and uncovering optimization potential

  • Designing, building and running integrations between SANOVIO and our customers' ERP systems (such as SAP), materials management and supplier systems

  • Onboarding and harmonizing customer data (e.g. article master data, catalogs, order histories) and building robust data pipelines and mappings

  • Configuring and extending our AI agents for customer-specific workflows such as data matching and order automation

  • Prototyping and shipping customer-facing workflows, tools and dashboards with a strong focus on usability for non-technical users

  • Bringing customer insights back into the product and turning recurring solutions into product features together with our engineering team and the founders

Communication and customer focus

  • You enjoy talking to customers: you listen carefully, ask the right questions and explain technical topics in plain language

  • Native-level German and very good English, so you can confidently lead conversations and workshops with our customers

  • Confident with all kinds of stakeholders, from procurement managers to IT departments

  • Willing to work on-site in Munich and to travel regularly to customers in Germany and Switzerland

General Profile

  • Degree in Business Informatics (Wirtschaftsinformatik), Industrial Engineering (Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen), Computer Science, Mathematics or a similar field. Skills matter more to us than your degree, so equivalent hands-on experience counts just as much

  • Strong process understanding: you enjoy mapping, analyzing and improving business processes such as procure-to-pay or supply chain

  • High ownership, structured problem-solving and the drive to deliver fast in ambiguous environments

  • This is a junior role: a great fit if you're a recent graduate or have up to five years of professional experience. Internships and working student jobs count too

Technical skillset

  • First hands-on experience with system integrations and interfaces (e.g. REST APIs, webhooks, EDI or file-based interfaces), whether from work, internships or university projects

  • Solid coding skills (e.g. TypeScript/JavaScript or Python) and good SQL and data skills

  • Product and design affinity: you care about UX and can turn complex workflows into simple, intuitive interfaces. Experience with Figma or building UIs is a plus

Bonus if you

  • Worked at a startup or software company focused on SAP/ERP, integration platforms, process mining or procurement software (internships and working student jobs count too)

  • Have first experience as a Technical PM, Product Engineer, Solutions or Implementation Engineer, or ERP consultant

  • Have built with LLMs or AI agents, e.g. for data extraction or matching

  • Bring domain knowledge in healthcare, hospitals, procurement or supply chain

  • Can share a portfolio, GitHub or case studies of projects you shipped

Benefits

  • A steep learning curve: you learn integration work, process consulting and product building at the same time, working closely with the founders

  • Real ownership and direct impact on how we work with our customers

  • Great central office in Munich with regular team events and dinners

  • Monthly wellness budget

  • Access to the AI and productivity tools you need

  • Regular customer visits across Germany and Switzerland

  • Compensation package including cash, performance bonus and shares

About the interview process

Step 1: Intro call

Casual intro call to get to know each other, introduce SANOVIO and talk about your experience.

Step 2: Case study

A practical case based on a real-world challenge from our platform, for example how you would connect a hospital or a supplier to SANOVIO and redesign its ordering process. You'll present your approach to the team, just like you would to a customer.

Step 3: Personal fit

Meet one of our co-founders to get a feel for our culture and working style.

Step 4: Offer & reference checks

If we see a great fit, you will get an offer, including a competitive compensation package. We'll also ask for two to three references.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
descriptionHtml:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Auterion, you will play a pivotal role in the successful development, integration and deployment of Auterion-powered drone systems. 

In this role, you will collaborate closely with the production, hardware engineering, and firmware/software teams, as well as operations, ensuring that every platform transitions smoothly from an airframe concept into a fully validated flying robot ready for deployment. You will serve as the primary technical interface for partners, work closely with them to understand their technical requirements, configure and adapt existing solutions, contribute to core software development, and ensure successful implementation. 

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with customer collaboration and system-level problem solving, bridging the gap between hardware, firmware, and real-world flight performance. 

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Operate in a highly hands-on environment with evolving system requirements, rapidly iterating across hardware and software integration challenges.
  • Manage software releases and perform firmware flashing and configuration using PX4 or adjacent autopilot ecosystems, including sensor calibration, ESC tuning, and system bring-up.
  • Provide deep avionics and airframe expertise, including autopilot tuning, sensor and payload integration, power systems and airworthiness considerations.
  • Work independently to troubleshoot integration and flight-readiness issues while collaborating cross-functionally with hardware engineering, firmware/software teams, operations, and QC engineering to escalate complex challenges when required.
  • Act as the primary technical authority in customer engagements, translating mission requirements into concrete system architectures and demonstrable solutions built on AuterionOS and Skynode.
  • Participate in flight testing activities to validate platform stability, safety, and mission performance, resolving technical issues often directly in the field during customer trials and demonstrations.
  • Contribute to technical documentation and continuous improvement of engineering processes.
  • Feed customer and market requirements back into product and engineering teams to influence the roadmap of the Auterion stack.

Qualifications and Skills

  • Degree in Software, Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace or Robotics Engineering, or a related field
  • Working proficiency in C/C++ and Python: you can read, debug and patch existing code and write small tools and scripts
  • Comfortable in Linux environments, including the command line, logs, Docker and basic networking (IP, TCP/UDP)
  • Hands-on hardware-software integration: system bring-up, wiring and connectors, and embedded interfaces (UART, CAN, I2C, SPI) at a practical level
  • Structured troubleshooting: you can isolate whether a problem is software, hardware, configuration or RF, often under time pressure in the field
  • Strong communicator: you can explain technical issues clearly to customers and operators, and report findings back to engineering in a way they can act on
  • Willing to travel and work on-site with customers, including at test ranges and in field environments
  • EU citizenship (required for security clearance and customer requirements)

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with PX4 or ArduPilot, MAVLink, QGroundControl or mission planning tools
  • UAV flight testing and validation in operational environments
  • Experience with datalinks and radio systems
  • Previous customer-facing or field engineering role, especially with defense or government customers
  • German language skills

Benefits

  • Flexible working hours
  • Stock Options
  • Generous holiday allowance
  • Pension plan 
  • Extended social security package 
  • Enhanced maternity & paternity leave
  • Wellpass membership 

About Auterion

We are building the leading software platform for AI-powered autonomous systems for enterprise and government customers. Our team is supporting the most important missions and solving the most challenging problems.

At Auterion, we bring together the sharpest minds who love to solve the hardest problems. Join a vibrant team built on innovation, openness, and excellence, where you’ll be empowered to develop ideas, collaborate across all levels, and make an impact that matters.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
descriptionHtml:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer in the customer organisation, you are the technical spearhead of monday.com's AI transformation motion for our most strategic customers. You will carry a portfolio of 1 to 2 strategic accounts, deeply embedded with C-level and technical teams to architect, build, and ship AI solutions in production, and you will be accountable for the business outcomes those engagements promised, not just the build.

This is part of a growing motion, and you will be joining a team that’s already working on active deployments.

Please note this is a hybrid position of 3 days/week in our Paris office.

About the Role

Enterprises don't struggle to access AI capability; they struggle to deploy it. Your job is closing that gap for a small portfolio of monday.com's highest-value customers. You will advise executives on AI-driven operational change, design and ship the systems that make it real, and feed what you learn back into the product with evidence, not anecdotes.

You will work with: monday AI agents, MCP-based integrations into customer systems, vibe apps, and production workflows. You will take these from discovery through architecture, build, rollout, and measurable adoption.

This is an autonomous, high-visibility role that shapes both customer outcomes and the future of forward-deployed engineering at monday.com.

What You'll Do

Strategic transformation. Embed with C-level stakeholders across your accounts to architect end-to-end AI solutions and scalable workflows that solve complex, mission-critical business pains. You own the narrative from pilot to full production rollout.

Outcome ownership. Your success metric is the business result the engagement committed to: adoption, workflow throughput, measurable ROI. You define the success criteria with the customer up front and you own getting there.

Build and ship. Design sophisticated platform configurations, build monday agents and vibe apps, wire MCP integrations into customer systems, and prototype custom scripts where the platform ends. Your leverage is architecture and judgment; your credibility is that you can build it yourself.

Eval-driven product feedback. Instrument your deployments, run evals against real customer workflows, and translate what you find into PRDs and roadmap input that changes what we build. You are a sensor for the product org, with data behind every claim.

Cross-functional leadership. Partner with Sales and CS as the technical authority on account strategy. Productize what you learn: patterns, agents, and assets from one account become reusable machinery for the whole motion.

What we promise

This role has been built with a direct line into the product roadmap, a mandate to productize rather than repeat, and outcome-based success criteria agreed before the build starts.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years building applications from scratch using TypeScript/Node.js/React, with full-stack depth

  • Experience leading hands-on projects end-to-end in a production environment, preferably client-facing

  • Background in Solution Architecture or Software Engineering with a strong grasp of AI/LLM systems: agent architectures, MCP or comparable tool-use protocols, evals, and prompt-to-production workflows

  • Experience navigating C-suite relationships and influencing executive decisions in ambiguous environments

  • Track record of turning one-off delivery work into reusable assets, product requirements, or repeatable playbooks

  • Entrepreneurial, fast-moving, and focused on long-term impact over immediate fixes

title: Forward Deployed Engineering Lead
descriptionHtml:
TL;DR - We’re looking for an exceptional Forward Deployed Engineering Lead to help build the future of AI-powered software creation. You’ll build and lead an exceptional FDE team in your location, while working alongside our other FDE leaders to shape how the function operates globally. You’ll remain deeply hands-on — working directly with our most ambitious customers, writing production code, and building alongside your team.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

 

What makes this role special?

You will:

• Build and lead the FDE team in your location

• Join a small group of FDE leaders defining how the function operates and scales globally

• Stay deeply hands-on — personally building and shipping alongside your team

• Partner with customers building never-seen-before AI systems

• Set a high technical bar across architecture, engineering, and execution

• Turn patterns from real deployments into core product and platform improvements

• Influence our product direction, technical roadmap, and how FDE works at Lovable

 

If you want to build an exceptional engineering team without stepping away from building yourself — this is that role.

 

What we’re looking for

• 12+ years across software engineering, technical architecture, and customer-facing engineering

• Experience leading and developing high-performing technical teams

• A track record of remaining deeply hands-on as your leadership scope has grown

• Strong full-stack engineering fundamentals across modern frontend and backend development

• Strong architectural thinking and familiarity with distributed systems

• Experience owning complex technical engagements end-to-end

• Exceptional product intuition and ability to work directly with users

• Ability to move comfortably between writing code, making architectural decisions, leading engineers, and working with senior customer stakeholders

• High agency and comfort operating in high-ambiguity, high-velocity environments

 

Bonus if you’ve:

• Built a team or technical function from zero

• Worked on agentic AI systems or built with LLMs in production

• Led zero-to-one product development

• Worked in a founding or early-stage startup environment

• Worked across high-growth startups, big tech, consulting, or enterprise AI

 

What you’ll do

In one sentence: build the team that deploys intelligence into the real world — and deploy it alongside them.

• Recruit, develop, and lead an exceptional team of Forward Deployed Engineers

• Work directly with customers to understand their workflows, needs, and hardest technical problems

• Personally design, prototype, and implement solutions alongside your team

• Own and guide projects from idea → architecture → shipping → iteration

• Set the technical bar through architecture decisions, code reviews, and hands-on engineering

• Translate insights from customer deployments into foundational platform improvements

• Partner with other FDE leads to shape standards, playbooks, and how the function scales globally

• Contribute to core product strategy, technical decisions, and cultural foundations

 

Our Tech Stack

We choose tools that empower both humans and AI:

• Frontend: React, TypeScript

• Backend: Golang & Rust

• Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, multiple LLM providers

• Tooling: GitHub Actions, OTEL, Grafana, Terraform, and more

• Always evolving with what works best

 

How we hire

1. Fill out a short form and hop on a brief intro call with our recruiting team

2. A technical leadership interview — how you build teams, set standards, and make technical decisions

3. Show us how you approach hard technical problems

4. Show us something you’ve built that makes you proud

5. Conversations with the leaders you’d work most closely with, followed by a final discussion

 

About your application

• Please submit your application in English — it’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join

• We treat all candidates equally — if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal

title: Forward Deployed Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:

Location: London, United Kingdom - Hybrid 

Recruiter: Dina Hussain

Role Overview

As a Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) Manager, you will lead a high-performing delivery team of 8+ Individual Contributors (ICs) to build and productionize solutions for customers' data and AI challenges using the Databricks platform. You are responsible for ensuring high-quality technical execution, driving professional services business outcomes, and nurturing elite engineering talent while remaining close to the technology and execution.

Scope of Impact & Leveling Criteria

  • Typically manages an elite engineering team of 8+ Individual Contributors. Handles delivery across direct accounts and navigates technical and scoping alignment with Engagement Managers and client stakeholders.
  • Focuses internally on building team capabilities and externally on account execution. Mandates high standards for Greenhouse scorecards and interview calibrations, ensuring clear pass/fail hiring signals.

Key Responsibilities & Core Behaviors

  • Connect your team’s day-to-day work to real customer outcomes and business impact. Build excitement about Databricks by sharing customer wins and delivery successes, making each individual feel motivated and appreciated.
  • Reinforce your team’s top delivery priorities. Help your team focus on high-impact technical work, redirecting effort away from low-value tasks and removing blockers that slow execution. Use delivery data and PS KPIs to confirm focus areas.
  • Hire strong PS talent using structured interviews and practical delivery scenarios. Ensure team takes 2–4 protected hours a week for continuous technical learning and experimentation. Understand your team’s strengths and growth areas to provide regular coaching, and handle underperformance early with clear feedback and accountability.

Review delivery plans and architectures utilizing practical knowledge of the Databricks platform and cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP).   • Leadership Skills: Proven ability to manage technical project delivery, timelines, scoping, conflict resolution, and executive customer relationships from technical ICs up to Director level.

More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. title: Forward Deployed Finance Engineer, Private Credit
descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey's Finance Engineering team is the investment-side counterpart to our Legal Engineering team: former investment professionals who bring real deal experience to Harvey's prospects and customers. Forward Deployed Finance Engineers lead discovery, demos, pilots, trainings, onboarding, and custom builds alongside our AEs and CSMs. They translate real investment work into Harvey solutions, serving as the trust layer across the entire customer lifecycle, from the first pilot to the most complex, custom-built workflow.

Finance Engineers work on Harvey Deals, a new product built off of Harvey's acquisition of Benchmark. Harvey Deals is where investment teams run their deals — screening, underwriting, diligence, and committee materials — built in the firm's own templates and formats, with every figure traceable back to the document it came from. Harvey works with 150+ asset management firms and analyzes 178M+ documents each month; the Finance Engineering team is how that capability meets the way deal teams actually work.

Finance Engineers understand how investors think and work, and use that expertise to design, build, and refine solutions that hold up under live deal pressure. In doing so, they don't just drive adoption; they shape Harvey's product roadmap, ensuring every release is grounded in what investment teams actually need. It's a team built to make Harvey the platform investment teams can trust with their most important work.

This role is the first Finance Engineer dedicated to private credit. You will build the credit playbook — demo library, workflow templates, use cases — while running live pilots, and lead the credit practice as the team grows.

You may be asked to travel around 2–3+ times per month. Travel is always for a significant business need and typically is for 1–3 days at a time.

What You'll Do

Forward Deployed Finance Engineers on the private credit team are former credit investors who left the desk to help build the future of how credit gets underwritten. Working closely with Account Executives, they engage with direct lenders, opportunistic and specialty finance managers, BDC managers, and insurer credit arms throughout the pre-sales process and stay with them well past it — leading pilots on live opportunities, guiding lenders through what's possible with AI, and sitting down with credit teams to build screening, underwriting, and credit committee workflows in the firm's own templates and formats.

The work is the work they did on the desk: lender presentation and CIM review; QoE read-throughs and data pack analysis; cash flow and leverage modeling; sizing and structuring; covenant and credit agreement review; credit memo drafting; and comps. It continues post-close into compliance certificate review, covenant tracking, amendment and waiver analysis, and quarterly portfolio reporting, so value compounds after the first deal. Along the way, Finance Engineers bring credit-team feedback back into the product, helping shape the future of Harvey.

What You Have

  • 6+ years on the investment or underwriting team at a direct lender, private credit fund, BDC manager, or insurer private credit arm, with demonstrated ownership of live deal work: screening, underwriting, diligence workstreams, modeling, structuring, and drafting credit committee materials. Asset-based and specialty finance backgrounds are welcome. Leveraged finance, restructuring advisory, or rating-agency experience before the principal side is welcome, but principal-side deal execution is required.

  • Strong command of the documents and data that drive a credit decision — lender presentation and CIM, QoE and data pack, model, credit agreement and intercreditor, compliance certificates — and an instinct for where the numbers and the paper disagree.

  • Advanced Excel and financial modeling, comfort with prompting and agentic AI workflows, and a builder's instinct for turning a repeated manual process into a repeatable automation. Python, SQL, or experience building internal tools is a plus.

  • Executive presence and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish credibility from analysts and associates through to partners and credit committee members.

  • Outstanding communication and presentation skills — comfortable leading a live demo, facilitating a workshop, or holding your own in a technical conversation about a covenant package or an underwriting assumption.

  • Deep curiosity about AI's potential to transform investment work, paired with a practical, solutions-oriented mindset and bias toward action.

  • Track record partnering with senior stakeholders to drive results, with curiosity for testing approaches and optimizing for customer outcomes.

  • Customer-facing or commercial experience (LP or investor relations, capital formation, banking coverage, business development) and/or hands-on experience using AI tools in an investment setting are pluses.

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Internship
descriptionHtml:
Le poste

Les Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSE) travaillent directement avec les clients afin de comprendre rapidement leurs problèmes les plus importants et ainsi concevoir et implémenter des solutions qui vont utiliser leurs données afin de résoudre ces problématiques. Nos clients s’appuient sur les plateformes de Palantir pour certaines de leurs opérations les plus critiques, et les projets débutent souvent par une question ouverte, par exemple : « Comment évaluer le risque d’incendie de forêt et, par conséquent, comment optimiser le réseau électrique ? » ou « Comment évaluer rapidement notre chaîne d’approvisionnement alimentaire et l’adapter afin d’apporter à temps une aide vitale ? » En tant que FDSE, vous appliquez votre capacité à résoudre les problèmes, votre créativité et vos compétences techniques pour aider les organisations à exploiter au mieux leurs données et avoir ainsi un impact réel sur le monde. Vous avez l’opportunité d’obtenir des informations rares et de contribuer à certaines des industries et institutions les plus importantes au monde.

Responsabilités principales

En tant que stagiaire chez FDSE, vos responsabilités s’apparentent à celles que l’on trouve dans une petite start-up, tout en bénéficiant des ressources, de la stabilité et de l’accompagnement d’une entreprise technologique bien établie. Vous travaillerez en petites équipes avec une supervision minimale et serez responsable de l’exécution de bout en bout de projets à enjeux élevés. Votre journée peut consister à discuter de l’architecture avec d’autres ingénieurs, à gérer des données à grande échelle, à coder une application web personnalisée, à discuter avec l’équipe dirigeante du client ou à établir une stratégie pour votre équipe.

Les stagiaires FDSE sont traités exactement comme des ingénieurs à temps plein, et bénéficient d’une grande liberté et d’une grande autonomie dans leur travail. Ils assument la responsabilité des projets et des résultats réels sur lesquels nos clients comptent.

Nos principes:
  • Impact : nous gérons des projets significatifs et enthousiasmants qui rendent le monde meilleur.
  • Responsabilité : nous menons nos projets du début à la fin, en surmontant tous les obstacles que nous pourrions rencontrer. Nous nous faisons mutuellement confiance afin de gérer efficacement le temps et les priorités et donner aux individus l’espace nécessaire pour réfléchir par eux-mêmes.
  • Collaboration : nous travaillons en interne avec des personnes d’horizons variés, tels que d’autres FDSE, des équipes Produits et des Deployment Strategists. Nous travaillons également en externe avec nos clients, souvent sur site, afin de comprendre et de répondre à leurs problèmes.
  • Développement : nous pensons que l’apprentissage par l’expérience est l’une des meilleures écoles et nous nous encourageons nous-mêmes tout comme nos pairs à rechercher de nouveaux défis et de nouvelles opportunités de croissance, ainsi qu’à trouver de nouvelles façons d’innover et de partager les connaissances.
Le profil recherché
  • Propension et intérêt à se déplacer sur les sites client en fonction des besoins. Capacité de passer 25 à 50 % du temps en déplacement de préférence, mais les exigences peuvent varier selon l’équipe et l’emplacement.
  • Capacité démontrée à apprendre continuellement, à travailler de manière autonome et à prendre des décisions avec un minimum de direction.
  • Capacité à collaborer avec des équipes de personnes techniques et non techniques, et à être à l’aise pour travailler dans un environnement en évolution constante avec des objectifs dynamiques et des itérations avec les utilisateurs.
  • Volonté de résoudre de façon créative les problèmes techniques liés aux structures de données, aux systèmes de stockage, à l’infrastructure cloud, aux frameworks front-end et à d’autres outils techniques.
  • Intérêt à travailler avec des données à grande échelle et à les utiliser pour résoudre des problèmes opérationnels importants.
Les exigences
  • Expérience en ingénierie, de préférence dans des domaines tels que l’informatique, les mathématiques, le Software Engineering, la physique et la science des données.
  • Maîtrise de langages de programmation tels que Python, Java, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript ou similaire.
  • Vous devez prévoir d’obtenir votre diplôme en 2027. Il doit s’agir de votre dernier stage avant d’obtenir votre diplôme.
Pour postuler, veuillez soumettre ce qui suit :
  • Un CV à jour
  • Des réponses réfléchies à nos questions de candidature
Date limite de l’offre

Afin de renforcer la transparence de notre processus de recrutement, nous aimerions vous faire part de nos attentes concernant la date limite de l’offre. En postulant à ce poste, vous vous engagez à confirmer votre décision dans les deux semaines suivant la réception de votre offre écrite.

La vie chez Palantir

Nous tenons à ce que chaque Palantirien(ne) atteigne son meilleur potentiel, c’est pourquoi nous célébrons les forces, les compétences et les intérêts des individus, de votre premier entretien à votre croissance à long terme, plutôt que de nous appuyer sur les échelles de carrière traditionnelles. L’attention portée aux besoins de notre communauté nous permet d’optimiser nos possibilités de croissance et contribue à garantir de nombreuses voies de réussite chez Palantir. Promouvoir la santé et le bien-être dans tous les domaines de la vie des Palantiriens n’est que l’une des façons dont nous investissons dans notre communauté. Apprenez-en davantage sur la vie chez Palantir et notez que nos offres peuvent varier selon les régions.

Conformément aux valeurs et à la culture de Palantir, nous estimons que les employés sont « meilleurs ensemble » et que le travail en présentiel permet d’obtenir des résultats plus créatifs. En conséquence, nous encourageons les employés à travailler depuis nos bureaux pour favoriser la connectivité et l’innovation. De nombreuses équipes proposent des options hybrides (télétravail un jour ou deux par semaine), ce qui permet à nos employés de trouver le bon compromis pour leur productivité personnelle. En fonction des besoins de l’entreprise, il existe quelques postes qui permettent de travailler « à distance » de manière exceptionnelle. Si vous postulez à l’un de ces postes, vous devez travailler depuis la ville et/ou le pays dans lequel vous êtes employé(e). Si le poste précise « sur site », vous devez travailler depuis un bureau.

Si vous souhaitez donner aux organisations les plus importantes au monde les moyens d’agir, votre place est ici. Palantir valorise l’excellence, d’où qu’elle vienne. Nous nous engageons à rendre le processus de candidature et d’embauche accessible à tous et offrirons des aménagements raisonnables aux personnes vivant en situation de handicap. Si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement pour le processus de candidature ou d’embauche, veuillez et nous indiquer comment nous pouvons vous aider.

Attention : il ne vous sera jamais demandé d’envoyer un paiement ou de partager des données financières pour participer à notre processus d’entretien. Si vous pensez avoir été contacté par un escroc, nous vous conseillons de cesser toute communication avec la personne et d’envisager de la signaler aux autorités compétentes, telles que l’Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) du FBI aux États-Unis.

A World-Changing Company

Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. You’ll work in small teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of high stakes projects. Your day might span discussing architecture with fellow engineers, wrangling massive-scale data, coding a custom web app, speaking with customer executives, or establishing strategy for your team.

FDSE Interns are treated just like full time engineers, with significant freedom and ownership over their work. Interns take responsibility for real world projects and outcomes that our customers rely on.

Our Principles:

What We Require

Life at Palantir

We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Who we're looking for

  • A strong software engineer. You have solid fundamentals and the technical depth to design and build complex production systems

  • An autonomous builder. You operate with limited guidance, create structure from ambiguity, and drive problems through to production

  • A versatile product engineer. You’re comfortable working across the stack and moving between hands-on engineering, product thinking, and conversations with the people using what you build

     

Experience requirements

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience with strong CS fundamentals

  • Experience building production software across the stack, from product-facing applications and APIs to backend services and data workflows

  • Strong system design judgment and experience making architecture decisions for complex software

  • Strong coding skills in a modern language; Python is a plus

  • Evidence of owning technical problems end to end, from design through production

  • Strong product judgment, technical communication, and stakeholder management

  • Experience working directly with users, customers, or external engineering teams is a plus

  • Bonus: experience in a high-growth startup, developer platform, or ML/data product environment

     

Why Encord

  • Competitive salary, commission, and meaningful equity in a high-growth startup

  • Clear, accelerated growth opportunities as the company scales rapidly

  • Strong in-person culture: 4 days/week

  • Daily team lunches & dinners

  • Annual learning & development budget

  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage

  • US employees: 18 paid vacation days plus US public holidays

  • UK employees: 25 paid vacation days plus UK public holidays

  • Frequent travel opportunities across the U.S., London, and Europe

  • Bi-annual company offsites & monthly socials

 

Operating principles

 

High agency

You see something broken, you fix it or find the person who can. We celebrate the people who solve 90% of a problem before anyone asks.

Build with care & urgency

We bear-hug the customer. Former founders and people from fast-moving, high-stakes environments thrive here.

Self-aware & hungry

We stay warm, self-aware, and genuinely hungry. We elevate our peers, and ego doesn't last long.

Invent in real time

We move toward the ambiguity. We’re pragmatic, resourceful, energized by the fact that there's no playbook.

 

If you're looking to do the most meaningful work of your career alongside people who push you to be better, we'd love to meet you.

  • Du verantwortest ein eigenes, abgegrenztes Thema, bei dem die Geschäftsführung nicht mehr nachfasst.

  • Die Bereichsleitungen sprechen dich direkt an, wenn sie eine Analyse brauchen.

Wohin sich die Stelle entwickelt:

Du siehst in wenigen Monaten, wie ein wachsendes Unternehmen entscheidet, und nimmst eine Arbeitsweise mit, die in jeder späteren Rolle trägt. Wer überzeugt, bleibt im Gespräch.

Das bringst du mit

Erfahrung & Track Record

  • Ein fortgeschrittener Bachelor oder Master mit sehr guten Leistungen: Wirtschaftswissenschaften, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Jura, Naturwissenschaften oder ein Fach, in dem du nachweislich herausgestochen bist.

  • Erste Praxis in einem anspruchsvollen Umfeld ist ein Plus: Beratung, Investment Banking, Private Equity, Scale-up, Founders Office oder eine eigene Gründung.

  • Profile, die nicht in dieses Raster passen, aber Denkschärfe und Umsetzungskraft mitbringen, sind ausdrücklich eingeladen. Wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett.

Skills & Arbeitsweise

  • Du schreibst klar und knapp. Zwei gute Seiten schlagen bei uns zwanzig vollständige.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug für Recherche, Analyse und Drafting. Repetitive Aufgaben sind für dich ein Anlass zur Automatisierung.

  • Bei einer offen formulierten Aufgabe machst du deine Annahmen explizit, schlägst eine Richtung ein und justierst unterwegs.

Mindset & Persönlichkeit

  • Du verträgst die direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung: schnelle Iteration, hohe Eigenständigkeit und auch Aufgaben, die nicht im Lebenslauf glänzen.

  • Du bringst die Demut mit, von Praktikern zu lernen. Die Steuerberaterin mit 20 Jahren Erfahrung weiß Dinge über ihr Mandat, die in keinem Modell stehen.

  • Du hast den Anspruch, in allem, was du ablieferst, den höchsten Standard zu setzen, nicht weil jemand es kontrolliert, sondern weil Mittelmaß dich persönlich stört.

Was du bei uns nicht finden wirst

  • Keine Konzern-Strategieabteilung. Was du schreibst, geht in eine Entscheidung, die diese Woche fällt.

  • Keinen Elfenbeinturm. Eine Empfehlung ohne Verantwortung für die Umsetzung ist hier keine Lieferung.

  • Kein Praktikum mit Rotationsplan. Du bekommst eigene Themen und damit auch die Konsequenzen deiner Entscheidungen.

  • Keine Zuarbeit für eine Zwischenebene. Du trägst deine Ergebnisse selbst vor der Geschäftsführung vor.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

title: Founding Account Executive (Italian Speaker)
descriptionHtml:
About Sona

Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.

Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here (https://www.sona.ai/careers).

About the Role

We're hiring a Founding Account Executive to win Sona's first customers in Italy and open the market for us. This is a senior, seller-first role, and you'll run every conversation with prospects in Italian, from the first call to the close.

Our expansion into Europe is starting now and ramps up through 2027 across key markets. Italy is one of them, and you'll own the go-to-market launch there. Colleagues across Sona will be running the product, operations and other launch activities, so your focus is winning customers, building partnerships and creating the collateral to sell. With no sales team in market yet, you'll work with less support than a typical AE, and the team around you will grow as the market does.


Day to day, you'll decide which Retail and Hospitality accounts to go after, from mid-market through to enterprise, and run consultative sales conversations yourself. You'll also build what a new market needs, including partnerships and Italian-language collateral. The platform is already localised for Italy, and you'll have product and solutions support.

It's early, and the ground will shift as we learn what works. If you want a structured environment with lots of support around you, this won't be the right fit. If you want to shape how Sona sells in Italy from the start, it could be exactly that. The role is office-based in London, with travel to Italy as needed.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the go-to-market launch in Italy and win Sona's first customers, taking each deal from first conversation to close.

  • Build your own pipeline across Retail and Hospitality, from mid-market to enterprise.

  • Run strategic, consultative sales conversations in Italian.

  • Build and run partnerships that open doors in the Italian market.

  • Create the collateral Sona needs to sell in Italy.

  • Work with Sona's Strategy and Expansion Lead on where to focus and how to approach the market.

  • Feed what you learn from the market back to our Commercial and Product teams.

  • Travel to Italy as the role requires.

Requirements

  • You're a native Italian speaker, comfortable selling and negotiating in Italian, with fluent English for working with colleagues in London.

  • You have a senior Account Executive track record of winning new business, ideally across mid-market and enterprise deals.

  • You have a founder mentality. You take ownership, make decisions with limited information, and are happy building without a playbook.

  • You're strategic and consultative in how you sell, and you work well independently with less support than most AEs get.

  • You're comfortable creating partnerships and collateral from scratch.

  • You're based in London, or able to be, and happy to travel to Italy as the role needs.

  • Strongly preferred: Spanish, French or German as an additional language. It doesn't replace Italian.

Benefits

  • Salary: £80,000 - £120,000 base depending on experience, with OTE of £160,000 - £240,000

  • Office-based in our London office, with travel to Italy as the role requires

  • Share options

  • 35 days annual leave (25 days standard plus 10 flexible public holiday days)

  • Extra day of leave for every year of service

  • Pension contributions matched up to 5%

  • Comprehensive health insurance

  • Enhanced parental leave & pay

  • Salary sacrifice childcare scheme (Workplace Nursery)

  • Annual all expenses paid team retreats

  • The latest Macbook and equipment budget for your home office

  • Professional development budget

  • Unlimited free books

Plato is building the AI OS for litigation lawyers.

With AI, the legal industry is on the verge of a major transformation. Litigation lawyers are overwhelmed by complex and repetitive tasks: complex damage calculations, thousands of documents to review, days spent drafting legal documents, and more.

Our mission: Build the leading AI OS for litigation lawyers, enabling professionals to work 5x faster, by putting their whole firm on autopilot.

Plato already supports more than 30 law firms and 1 major insurance company’s legal team, who use our solution daily to manage hundreds of active cases.

Founded in January 2026 by Ben (CEO) and Alexandre (CTO), we are backed by Hexa (formerly eFounders), Europe’s leading startup studio. Hexa has launched over 35 companies, including unicorns such as Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, collectively generating more than €230M in ARR and raising over €750M in funding.

Your job is not to do AI research for the sake of research. You’ll experiment with models and approaches, understand what works, and turn the best solutions into reliable production systems.

You'll work on problems such as building agentic workflows, making sense complex legal documents, designing autonomous long-running agents, and improving the quality and reliability of AI-generated outputs.

  • Evaluate and improve agent outcomes through testing, evals and iteration

  • Build the backend services and infrastructure needed to run AI reliably at scale

Shape the product

  • Work directly with the founders and users to understand real-world problems

  • Move quickly from problem → experiment → production (think days, not weeks)

🤩 This role is for you if

We're looking for a strong software or AI engineer with 2+ years of experience who wants to build real-world AI products at the forefront of the agentic stack.

You like working close to founders and users, making pragmatic technical decisions, and shipping software that actually runs in production.

  • Are autonomous and pragmatic, comfortable navigating early-stage ambiguity and shipping fast

Our stack is designed to support AI-first workflows and production reliability.

Meet Siena

Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.

It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on.

The team

We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.

We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.

If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.

The Role

Siena is about to launch several products in quick succession, and we're not looking for someone to execute a brief well. We're looking for the person whose taste the rest of the company gets measured against: someone who can't look at a landing page without having an opinion, who'd rather kill a launch than ship something mediocre, and who has owned creative direction before, not just contributed to it.

This is a craft title, not a headcount title. You'll ship personally for the first year and set the bar for everyone who comes after, building toward a small internal agency (two to three people across design, motion, and content) that can brief, position, and launch without outside help.

What You'll Do

  • Own narrative and positioning across every launch. Design as strategy, not decoration

  • Own every artifact that goes to market: landing pages, launch video, decks, social

  • Own the design system, from v3 onward

  • Set the bar, full stop. If it ships under the Siena name, you made it or you signed off on it

Who You Are

The Bar: If you're missing any of these, this isn't the role for you.

  • Taste, above everything, with specific, defended opinions about what's good and why

  • A track record of owning creative direction, not just contributing to it. Agency or in-house, brand refresh or full launch, you've been the person whose call was final, not the one waiting on notes

  • AI as a working tool, not a threat to your taste. You've already built something with AI (an app, a prototype, a mockup) and want to get technical enough to ship a landing page yourself within a year. Anti-AI is disqualifying

Strong Signal: Not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one.

  • Narrative thinking: you already have a point of view on how a brand like Siena should be positioned, not just how it should look

  • Range that travels. Your background doesn't have to be SaaS. Fashion, art, consumer brand, editorial: what matters is whether your taste holds up somewhere new

  • A pattern of shipping in chaos, not around it. Multiple launches in flight, feedback that moves in hours not weeks

Nice to Have: Bonus, not required.

  • Experience building or scaling a small internal creative team

  • Motion or video production skills alongside visual design

  • Direct, founder-facing creative leadership experience at another startup

Not a Fit If:

  • You need a creative director above you setting the vision, or a team to delegate to on day one

  • Your best work happens on a slow, considered, one-project-at-a-time pace

  • Too much scrutiny too fast doesn't sound exciting, it sounds exhausting

Why Siena?

Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.

Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.

A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.

A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.

Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build.

Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we.

AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.

Our values

The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback - both giving and receiving it - because they care more about getting things right than being polite.

They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward.

Our approach to AI

The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.

Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows.

At Siena, we're not just looking for people who can do a job. We're looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that's you, we look forward to your application.

How we hire

We use AI-assisted screening tools as part of our hiring process. All decisions are made by humans. You can request a human-only review at Siena provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

title: Founding Customer Success Manager, SME & Growth
descriptionHtml:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the team

Airwallex is revolutionizing global banking, and the EMEA Growth team is key to driving growth and retention of our growing long tail of customers.

Our work spans Airwallex’s core solutions, including Payments, Business Accounts, Spend and APIs, combining a scalable, customer-first approach with the pace and ambition of a high-growth fintech. As a team, we are driven by a desire to make a positive impact and are constantly innovating to find new ways to support the success of our SME/ Mid Market customers.

This role will work with our commercial team on our SME/MM clients through the implementation, go-live and servicing phases. You will work cross functionally, engaging with many teams across the Airwallex family including sales, solutions engineering, account management and operations. Furthermore, you are a technology-minded, fintech enthusiast who is driven by learning the ins and outs of our platform so that you are equipped with the knowledge to solve complex problems. We are looking for someone who has a passion for building relationships, creating amazing customer experiences, and managing the onboarding and customer activation process.

Our UK team is growing, we are currently 110+ employees, working in a hybrid work environment with 3 days per week required in our London Office @wells&more - GPE, Fitzrovia.

title: Founding implementation strategist [ERP + AI]
descriptionHtml:
TL;DR

  • We're building the SAP/NetSuite of the AI era for mid-sized companies in the real-world economy, starting with their supply chain operations (buy, sell, stock, produce)

  • Founding deployment strategist: you deploy two things into real factories, in the same project, the ERP that runs their operations, and the AI agents that work inside it. Every client goes from signed contract to go-live on the date we promised, running on Piston, with agents already doing part of the work

  • A rare shape: someone who has led client projects that landed in industrial companies, who is genuinely AI-native, and who will write the deployment playbook for the team and our system integrator partners

  • €3M Pre-seed (Top-tier VCs)

What this role is (and isn't)

Most ERP deployments are people moving data around for a year. Incumbents quote six figures for it, and the client gets the same software they had, just newer. Ours run in eight to twelve weeks and deliver two things at once: a new ERP that runs buying, selling, stock and production, and AI agents inside it that read the orders, recompute the production load, prepare the purchases, and ask a human only when it matters.

This is not a product or a sales role, you are a deployment strategist. In one project, you replace a company's ERP and you put AI agents to work inside it.

Why now

Since day one, the founders have run every deployment themselves. Clients are now coming in faster than we can handle, and we need someone to own deployments. You work directly with Eric, CEO, who also leads product. That puts you as close as it gets to what success means at Piston: the success of our clients.

What you'll do

  • Deploy the ERP, with AI. The client's sales, purchasing, stock and production move onto Piston: data migrated from their old ERP and their Excel files, configuration built from their own documents, training, go-live. AI does the heavy lifting, you do the judgment.

  • Put the first AI agents live, during the ERP deployment. You decide what each agent does on its own, what it hands to a human for approval, and you make sure it's still running three months later.

  • Write the deployment playbook. Every go-live feeds a playbook that our next deployment hires and our system integrator partners will follow.

  • Map where the client's time goes. On site, you find the work that eats people's days: re-keying orders, chasing suppliers, rebuilding the same Excel every month. That map is the backlog of the next agents.

  • Teach humans to work with agents. The people you deploy with have never supervised software that acts on its own. You show them how to trust it, check it and correct it.

  • Hold the date and the budget. You size each deployment before the contract and protect that budget.

  • Use the tools engineers build for you. Our engineers build the tools that let you deploy on your own: AI-assisted data migration from the client's old ERP and Excel files, and a builder for screens and agents. You tell them what slows you down, they make it disappear.

  • Agentify your own work. On top of the tools our engineers build, you create your own agents for the deployment itself: configuration checks, test scenarios, training material, status reports. Every manual step you repeat twice becomes an agent for the next deployment.

What you bring

You bring the energy to deploy AI at scale in industrial companies. You learn fast from discovery, and you're as comfortable with founders and leadership teams as with operators on the shop floor.

Must have

  • Customer-facing project experience. Two years or more managing client projects in an industrial environment, typically in consulting (operations, supply chain, transformation). You've held deadlines, managed stakeholders, and delivered.

  • AI-native, for real. You use LLMs every day, and you've built things with them: automations, agents, prompts that run in production (Claude, GPT, n8n, Make, scripts, whatever works). You know what an agent can do alone, where it breaks, and where a human must stay in the loop.

  • Listening before configuring. You translate what people say into what the system and the agents must do, and you notice when the two don't match.

  • At ease in front of clients: Plant directors, finance, shop-floor operators. You can hold a room, and say no in it.

  • A full load, gladly. Around 150 project days a year, several deployments running at once.

  • Fluent English and French, both required. Our first clients work in French, our team writes in English, and you may support our deployments in the United States.

Nice to have

  • You've automated a real operations process end to end, with measurable hours saved

  • You've already taken a complex B2B software live

  • Comfortable with AI

  • You've worked around manufacturing or food operations: lots, BOMs, production orders, campaigns

  • Seed / Series A experience, where nobody's job description holds for long

Talent beats checklists. If you're intrigued, apply anyway.

How we'll measure success

  • ERP go-lives on the date we promised

  • Days spent against the plan we sold

  • Agents still running three months after launch, and the hours of work they take off the client's hands

What you'll get

  • World-class peers

  • The first hire of our deployment team: you write the playbook that future hires and our system integrator partners will follow, and you grow with the team it builds

  • A front-row seat on how AI agents change the way real companies operate

  • Regular company offsite (2–4 times per year) in great locations

  • Ideal equipment and setup

  • Remote-first (France), about 20% of your time on client sites

Process

We value efficiency and clarity. The entire process takes no more than 2 weeks:

  1. 30-minute intro call with Florian (CRO)

  2. 60-minute deployment deep dive with Eric (CEO)

  3. 30-min cultural-fit interview with Eugène (CTO)

  4. 2 days paid assessment, on a real client situation.

  5. Offer: If it's a match, we move fast.

Interested? Tell us about a client project you led, and something you automated with AI. A short, personal note goes a long way, AI-generated cover letters don't.

title: Founding Design Engineer | CodeSpeak
descriptionHtml:
Role: Founding Design Engineer (Senior / Staff)

Company: CodeSpeak

Location: London, on-site. Ideally you already live in London. Candidates based elsewhere are welcome to apply, and remote is possible for a very strong candidate, but UK-based candidates come first. Candidates with a Global Talent visa, granted or in process, are a good fit.

Job Type: Full-time

About CodeSpeak

Agents write more code every month. Human brains stay the same. CodeSpeak is building a program model that sits one level above code, so people can see how a program works and changes over time without reading much of it. The goal is to give control back to the developer: you think about architecture, and the routine goes away.

CodeSpeak was founded by Andrey Breslav, the creator of Kotlin, which millions of developers use daily. Around him is a team that has built the tools other engineers rely on, at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph, and Elastic. When it comes to program analysis and developer tooling, these are some of the best people in the world. CodeSpeak is backed by Accel and by funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, and funding covers several years.

Here is the open problem. The team has a fair idea of what the program model should look like. It does not yet know how to visualise it. As Founding Design Engineer you will decide how it looks, then build it and ship it. The core engineering team has just been hired, and nobody on it has design-engineering skills. You are the missing piece.

CodeSpeak is a UK company. It has no business in Russia and no ties to Russian companies. It is still testing which problems it can solve best, so priorities may shift.

What you are expected to do:

Design and delivery

  • Own how people interact with CodeSpeak: in the CLI, on the web and on any future platform.

  • Design the interfaces yourself. Build many prototypes, decide on the right UX and ship the result.

  • Harden the prototypes users liked, so they hold up on real data, with the same care for performance and product quality as for design.

  • Ship features to production without help from the rest of the team.

Product problems

CodeSpeak works with unusually complex information: developer intent, requirements, code, architecture, the relationships between them, how they change over time, contradictions and dependencies. The job is not to display it, but to help developers understand it, navigate it and act on it.

  • Find a way to visualise CodeSpeak's new, higher-level program model.

  • In your first 30 days, visualise the architecture of a codebase split into components. Go deeper from there: a single component, its diff and its code review.

  • Then interfaces that let developers navigate structured requirements and how they relate to each other, review requirements alongside code review, see how requirements map onto parts of the codebase, explore how intent, architecture and code change over time, browse agent sessions, find contradictions between requirements, and edit and reorganise requirements rather than only view them.

  • Web UI is the simplest and most obvious platform. Some of this will live in the console. VS Code plugins and other desktop frameworks may follow, and the final scope is still open.

Ways of working

  • Find tasks and clarify requirements without waiting for a brief. Nobody will micromanage you. Egor and Andrey give general direction.

  • Work directly with the founder and the engineering team to turn early ideas and hypotheses into intuitive, interactive product experiences.

  • Take part in design meetings, where many decisions are made on the spot.

  • Explain and defend your design decisions to Egor and Andrey. Both hold strong opinions, and both argue hard.

  • Argue for your tasks, and step back with good grace if the team disagrees.

What you need to succeed:

Craft

  • You can design an interface, prototype it and ship it to production on your own.

  • You have strong design taste, and your portfolio shows it: UX, interaction design, information architecture and visual hierarchy. For this role the portfolio is critical.

  • You make complex information or a complex data model easy to read. Think maps with metadata or dense dashboards, with non-trivial state. Tools that read and write count for more than infographics or landing pages.

  • You have solid computer science and software engineering fundamentals, plus TypeScript, and deep experience building production apps with modern UI frameworks such as React. At least 3 years of delivering production software.

  • You understand the problems of engineers, because engineers are CodeSpeak's users.

How you work

  • You can say why you made each design choice. "I'm an artist, I see it this way" will not work here.

  • You are curious and self-directed, and you care about making programming better. You gather requirements and find projects yourself.

  • You actively improve your own workflow with AI-powered coding tools.

  • You work hard and can be reached when a task needs it. The team has no weekend-work culture.

  • You think fast and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • You speak Russian, which is the team's working language. This is a priority, not a hard rule, and a strong candidate without Russian will still be considered.

Nice to have

  • A background as a frontend engineer with good taste. Engineers from SwiftUI, desktop, mobile or full-stack are welcome if they visualise complex things very well.

  • Experience with complex data visualisation.

  • Some sense of what an early-stage startup is like. A big-tech engineer who knows what they are joining can fit, and so can a former co-founder.

A technical degree is not required. Self-taught people and people with degrees in geology or biology have done well in roles like this.

What you get:

  • An unsolved problem with real room for your taste. The team is inventing a new way to represent programs, and you decide how it looks.

  • A boutique team of strong engineers, built carefully, who have built developer tools at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph and Elastic.

  • An ML team of four, led by Emeli Dral. She co-founded Evidently, an evals startup, and co-authored a very popular Coursera course for data scientists.

  • Day-to-day work with Egor, Andrey and the tech lead.

  • Backing from Accel and from funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, with funding for several years.

  • A UK contract with a pension and medical insurance.

  • Autonomy. You set your own tasks and nobody hovers over you.

  • Work in AI, a field most people want to be in.
