title: Medical Device Auditor
descriptionHtml:
We pull medical technology from the future to solve human health.

 

Scarlet is authorised to assess and certify medical devices. We combine clinical, technical and regulatory expertise with AI agents and software so rigorous certification can keep pace with product development at the world’s most ambitious technology companies, without lowering the safety bar.

Our customers have cut a year or more from their certification timelines for new AI-enabled medical devices and shortened product-update cycles from months to weeks. You’ll join a team building the infrastructure that makes these outcomes repeatable at scale.

About the role

As a Medical Device Auditor at Scarlet based out of either our London or Sweden office, you will audit medical device manufacturers’ quality management systems and produce clear conclusions that support certification decisions. You’ll receive training in Scarlet’s audit methods and tools. Your work will combine reviewing evidence with conversations about how manufacturers’ processes work in practice. Travel will be limited, though occasional trips may be required. You will help safe devices reach patients sooner.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and conduct QMS audits against ISO 13485, EU MDR and UK MDR requirements.

  • Review records and interview teams to assess whether their processes meet the requirements.

  • Review corrective actions and the evidence needed to close findings.

Required qualifications

  • At least four years’ experience in the medical device industry, including two years auditing or managing an ISO 13485 QMS.

  • Experience with software demonstrating knowledge of software design, validation, testing, debugging and interactions with its operating environment.

title: Medical Director
descriptionHtml:
Making preventive health the default for every human in Europe

The mission

At Lucis, we believe healthcare should be preventive, not reactive. We’re building the operating system for human longevity to help people add more healthy years to their lives.

The role

Lucis analyses 110+ biomarkers, builds personalised clinical protocols, and delivers them through an AI-powered preventive health product. We are live in France and opening the UK, Portugal and Spain.

This role exists to turn clinical judgement into the medical standards the company can run on.

We are hiring a Medical Director to own Lucis's clinical direction and medical safety system.

You will:

  • Decide what we test and why, and to what clinical standard the service runs

  • Set the risk posture and the governance model: who signs what, how incidents are handled, what Lucis can claim

  • Own the certification call and path: medical device classification, CE, ISO, or stay out of scope, and the argument behind it

  • Hire and lead the clinical operations and safety team.

  • Represent Lucis clinically with labs, insurers, institutional partners and regulators, alongside the CMO

About you

You're passionate about the future of human health and want your work to help people stay healthy for longer. You move quickly from idea to execution, take full ownership of what you build, and work best with talented people who care as much as you do.

You thrive in fast-moving environments, learn by doing, and value feedback as a way to continuously improve.

You'll fit in well if

title: Medior / Senior Data Analyst
descriptionHtml:

Met een advies waar klanten en collega’s echt iets mee kunnen. AI zet je daarbij vanzelfsprekend in, om sneller en slimmer tot de kern te komen.

Wij zijn Follo: een snelgroeiend, award-winning digital agency (ontstaan uit de fusie van vier topbureaus) waar data de basis is onder alles wat we doen. Als Medior Data Analist werk je zelfstandig voor een eigen set klanten en projecten, samen met onze Data & Analytics Consultants en de specialisten in Search en Social. Je levert niet alleen de cijfers, je vertelt ook wat ze betekenen en wat er moet gebeuren.

Wat je gaat doen

  • Je analyseert data uit onder andere GA4, advertentieplatformen en CRM- en e-commercesystemen en ontdekt zo trends, kansen en knelpunten.

  • Je zet AI actief in om sneller patronen te herkennen, hypotheses te toetsen, SQL te schrijven en grote datasets te doorgronden, zonder je kritische blik op de uitkomsten te verliezen.

  • Je presenteert je bevindingen aan klanten en collega’s en vertaalt ze naar heldere, commerciële aanbevelingen. Je komt zelf met verbetervoorstellen voor marketing, meetopzet en businessprocessen, en kijkt verder dan de vraag.

  • Je schrijft SQL in BigQuery en bouwt aan schone, herbruikbare datamodellen (bijvoorbeeld in Dataform), zodat databronnen goed gekoppeld zijn en iedereen met dezelfde definities werkt.

  • Je ontwikkelt en onderhoudt overzichtelijke dashboards en rapportages in onder andere Looker Studio, en bepaalt mee welke KPI’s er echt toe doen en hoe je die het best visualiseert.

  • Je bewaakt de betrouwbaarheid van data, signaleert afwijkingen en spoort de oorzaak op, of die nu in de tracking, de koppeling of het model zit.

  • Je maakt terugkerend werk slimmer met automatisering en AI, en deelt je kennis met het team.

Wat je van ons mag verwachten

  • Een salaris tussen de €3.250 en €5.000, afhankelijk van je ervaring.

  • Een ambitieus team waarin verantwoordelijkheid en samenwerken voorop staan.

  • 26 vakantiedagen per jaar, met de mogelijkheid om er 5 bij te kopen.

  • Een eenmalig thuiswerkbudget tot €1.000 om je thuiswerkplek goed in te richten.

  • Een goed geregeld pensioen, zonder eigen bijdrage.

  • De vrijheid om hybride te werken, zodat jij het best tot je recht komt.

  • Interne kennissessies, events en brainstorms, van AI en automatisering tot data deep-dives.


Dit ben jij

Je bent een analist met oog voor detail die het grotere plaatje blijft zien. Je werkt gestructureerd, bent nieuwsgierig en vindt het leuk om complexe data begrijpelijk te maken voor anderen. Daarnaast herken je jezelf in het volgende:

  • Je hebt minimaal 2 jaar relevante werkervaring als data analist of in een vergelijkbare rol.

  • Je bent communicatief sterk: je legt een analyse net zo makkelijk uit aan een marketing manager als aan een developer, en je durft met een onderbouwd advies te komen.

  • Je beheerst SQL goed; ervaring met BigQuery is een grote pré.

  • Je hebt ruime ervaring met dashboarding in Looker Studio, Power BI of een vergelijkbare tool.

  • Je kent GA4 en begrijpt hoe online marketingdata tot stand komt. Ervaring met Google Tag Manager is een pré.

  • Je gebruikt AI al in je dagelijkse analysewerk, of hebt de sterke ambitie om dat te doen.

  • Kennis van Python of ervaring met Dataform of dbt is mooi meegenomen.

Waarom Follo?

Bij Follo is data geen bijproduct van marketing, maar het fundament eronder. Van Search en Social tot Marketplaces en CRO: elke strategie begint bij betrouwbare data en scherpe inzichten. AI is bij ons geen buzzword, maar onderdeel van hoe we dagelijks werken. Minder handwerk, meer tijd voor analyse, advies en impact.

  • Data als fundament: met de FolloEngine, ons eigen platform voor data intelligence, datakwaliteit en automatisering, start je met een voorsprong.

  • AI in je dagelijkse werk: je werkt met de nieuwste tools en technieken, van AI-gedreven analyse tot geautomatiseerde workflows.

  • Sterke merken, echte vraagstukken: jouw analyses sturen de beslissingen van ambitieuze adverteerders.

Als stagiair werk je aan het verbeteren van processen binnen domeinen zoals sales, projecten in nieuwbouw en finance. Je analyseert hoe processen vandaag werken en vertaalt dit naar slimme oplossingen met behulp van Power BI en Power Automate. Heras is een vooraanstaand Europese totaalleverancier van permanente perimeter protection oplossingen. Wij opereren vanuit meer dan 24 landen en hebben meer dan 1100 hoogopgeleide experts in dienst. Opgericht in 1952, vervult en overtreft Heras de beveiligingsbehoeften van klanten in heel Europa. Wij hebben binnen Heras een informele, open en toegankelijke cultuur. We zijn trots op ons werk, producten en dienstverlening. We hebben een no-nonsense mentaliteit, tonen ondernemerschap, zijn energiek en werken allemaal gedisciplineerd volgens de drie kernwaarden; betrokkenheid, betrouwbaarheid en deskundigheid. Heras is gewaardeerd op een Ecovadis Zilveren Ster en dat plaatst ons bij de duurzaamste 15% bedrijven van Nederland. Onze doelstelling is streven naar Goud in de komende jaren en volledig CO2 neutraal zijn in 2050. Wil je hier meer over weten? https://www.heras.nl/over-heras/kwaliteit-en-veiligheid/

Bij Heras bieden wij jou een meewerkstage binnen een zeer dynamische omgeving waarbij elke dag anders is met veel variatie en afwisseling. Je draagt je steentje bij aan een veilige omgeving en helpt om onze samenleving te beschermen. Tenslotte zijn er volop mogelijkheden om jezelf te ontwikkelen en door te groeien. title: Member of Marketing Staff - Events Marketing Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Tessl is a fast-growing Series A startup based in London, founded by Guy Podjarny, who previously founded Snyk. We’ve raised more than $100 million from world-class investors, including Index Ventures, Accel, GV and Boldstart. In 2025, Tessl ranked #2 in Sifted’s B2B SaaS Rising 100 and #20 in its AI 100.

We’re building the context layer for AI coding agents and a platform for AI-native software development. As an early member of the team, you’ll help shape how we build and scale a company operating at the forefront of AI and software development.

About the Role

Events are one of the main ways Tessl builds real relationships with developers, customers, and partners. We're looking for a mid-level Events Marketing Specialist in New York to run our growing US events program on the ground: community meetups, developer chapters, conferences, partner and customer events, and larger Tessl-owned moments.

This is a hands-on execution role, with the opportunity to influence our events strategy as we grow our presence in the US. You'll take an agreed plan and make it real, and you'll be the person in the room making sure it runs. Most of the team sits outside the US, so you'll own your events with real autonomy, while sharing learnings and the impact of events on our growth goals with the wider team.

What You'll Do

Run US events end to end

  • Own operational delivery once strategy, objectives, and format are agreed: timelines, run-of-show, budgets, vendors, venues, catering, AV, signage, swag, and shipping

  • Be the primary owner on the ground, and troubleshoot calmly when something breaks an hour before doors open

  • Make Tessl events feel considered and consistent, not just staffed

Support the developer community program

  • Help chapter leaders across the US navigate venues, formats, logistics, swag, and promotion

  • Show up for priority community events and represent Tessl in the room

  • Build repeatable resources so local chapters get more self-sufficient over time

Coordinate conferences, partner and field events

  • Manage Tessl's presence at third-party conferences and developer events, and support commercial B2B activations with Sales and Partnerships: booths, sponsorships, side events, dinners, and co-hosted events

  • Keep both sides clear on responsibilities and deadlines on co-hosted events, and support larger programs like US roadshows alongside senior team members

Help fill the room

  • Work with Marketing, Community, and Sales so every event has a promotion plan and the assets to back it

  • Flag early when registrations track below target, and help identify the local communities and companies worth reaching (audience acquisition matters here, but this isn't primarily a demand generation role)

Keep everyone aligned

  • Maintain a single source of truth for each event so people know what's happening and what they own

  • Surface risks and blockers early with a proposed fix, and work smoothly across time zones with the UK-based Marketing and Community teams

What Good Looks Like

  • US events run smoothly without senior team members managing every operational detail

  • Plans are current and trusted, and everyone knows what's expected of them and when

  • Problems surface early, with solutions rather than surprises

  • Events feel polished and intentional on the ground

  • Our community program expands, with regular, well-attended meetups in key US cities

  • Chapter organisers feel well supported and grow more self-sufficient over time

  • Events contribute measurable value to our growth goals, generating sales opportunities and growing our community

  • Awareness of Tessl and AI Native Dev grows among developers and technical leaders in the US

What We're Looking For

We're looking for a strong operator and doer. You don't need to bring a new events strategy; you need to be very good at turning plans into reality.

Must have:

  • A few years running events, field marketing, or community events, from planning through to live delivery

  • Excellent organisation and project management, with real attention to detail across several events at once

  • A proactive communicator who keeps people informed rather than waiting to be asked

  • Good judgment and the confidence to make sensible calls independently

  • Experience managing external vendors, venues, and event partners

  • Happy to get hands-on: as comfortable talking through a plan with a senior stakeholder as tracking down a missing shipment before doors open

  • Comfortable in a fast-moving company and working with a distributed international team

Nice to have:

  • Experience with developer, technology, or startup community events

  • Experience supporting community chapters, ambassador programs, or meetup organisers

  • Both community-focused and commercial B2B/field event experience

  • Familiarity with the New York technology and developer scene

  • Some experience promoting events through community channels, email, social, or local outreach

Location and Travel

This role is based in New York, with regular travel across the US. You'll be Tessl's primary events operator on the ground, so you should be happy to travel when your presence will make an event materially better. We don't expect you at every Tessl event. You'll also work with the global Marketing and Events team at larger moments and team gatherings.

Salary and Benefits

Salary: We offer a competitive salary based on experience and skills, benchmarked against industry standards.

Application Process

  1. Introductory call

  2. Hiring manager deep dive

  3. Practical exercise

  4. Final conversation with leadership


We care deeply about the warm, inclusive environment we’re building at Tessl and we value diversity – we welcome applications from those typically underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this role but are not totally sure whether you’re the right person, do apply anyway!

Learn how we think and work

  • On Tessl, The AI Native Development Startup

  • Announcing skills on Tessl: the package manager for agent skills

  • Podcast Episode: The End of Fragmented Agent Context, Guy Podjarny Tessl CEO

title: Member of Technical Staff
descriptionHtml:
About Seamflow

Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files.

Where we are:

  • Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry

  • $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed, co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze.

  • Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists.

The team

Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further.

The role

A Product Engineer owns the surfaces people actually work in. A coordinator planning a month of inspections across a fleet of auditors. A reviewer signing off on a technical file. These are dense, stateful workflows where the interface carries real consequences, and where the person using it has done the job for twenty years and will know immediately if the software doesn't understand it.

You own product surface end to end: the interface, the backend that supports it, and the data model underneath. Every customer runs the work differently, so there's no template to fall back on. You decide what the right thing to build is, build it, and are the one who hears about it when it's wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week.

What we're looking for

We care far more about raw engineering strength than about matching a list of technologies. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in Rust, Go, Python, TypeScript, C++ or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, speed and standards are not.

What we're actually screening for:

  • You've built something hard and put it in front of real users. Not a prototype, not a course project. Something that ran, broke, and got fixed.

  • You build genuinely good interfaces, and you can go as deep on the backend as the feature requires.

  • You can hold a complicated workflow in your head and find the version of it that's simple enough to ship.

  • Speed with taste. You ship fast, and you're opinionated about what not to build.

  • You go to the source. You'll read the customer's actual documents, join the actual call, and look at hundreds of real outputs.

Signals we like, none of them required:

founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, early engineer at a startup with a serious engineering culture, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup, design sense you can defend, open source you genuinely maintain.

This is probably not for you if

  • You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch.

  • You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning.

  • You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane.

What you get

  • Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar

  • Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room

  • Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly

  • Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster

  • A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics

If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV.

title: Member of Technical Staff - Security Engineering
descriptionHtml:
About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

The role

We build the control chain that powers on, monitors, updates, and protects devices and racks across bare metal, RTOS, and embedded Linux. We also build the communication mechanisms that connect devices to each other and to the host. Security runs through all of it. A chain of trust from the hardware up to the rack management plane: the root of trust each controller boots from, the signed updates that reach the fleet safely, the identity that lets a device prove what it is, the authenticated channels the controllers and devices talk over, and the runtime protections that keep the host Linux kernel and the on-die firmware trustworthy long after boot. These are the layers that let operators rely on the hardware.

You’d be deeply involved in that security across the chain, making it real in software. You’ll work hand in hand with our architecture and hardware teams, bringing the software and system-level view: turning threat models into concrete mechanisms in bare metal, RTOS, and Linux, then designing, prototyping, and validating them. Some of the calls in this model are still open, and you’ll help shape them.

We want engineers who understand security from the inside out. You know how the root of trust, boot chain, key hierarchy, and secure interconnects actually work under the hood, not just how to switch them on. In this role, the security of your software solutions depends entirely on how well you understand the hardware beneath it. Some of the protections we rely on live in silicon, some in software, and part of the skill is knowing which belongs where. We’re looking for people who know both sides well enough to build the mechanisms that close whole classes of bugs by design.

We’re not heavy on levels here! Whether you’d call yourself senior, staff, principal, or lead, what matters is depth of security judgement, system-level experience, and working well with the engineers around you. If you’ve worked deep in the security of real systems and like to get your hands on the code and the systems around it, we’d like to hear from you.

What you’ll do:

  • Shape the security of the control chain (device, board, chassis, and rack controllers): threat models, trust boundaries, and a coherent secure-by-design approach across all platforms

  • Design and help build secure boot and the root of trust on each controller: verified/measured boot, signing and verification, anti-rollback, and locking down debug and privileged access in production

  • Secure the interconnects, between controllers and between devices and the host, with authentication, integrity, and additional protections where needed

  • Design and build the cryptographic mechanisms: key hierarchies, provisioning and storage, device identity, and remote attestation so the fleet can prove what it’s running

  • Make firmware updates safe end to end: signed images, rollback protection, staged rollout, and clean recovery, across every hop of the chain

  • Protect the running system, not just boot: harden the host Linux kernel and the on-die firmware

  • Work closely with hardware and the rest of the software team to build security into the product, running threat-model reviews, triaging vulnerabilities, and driving fixes to closure

What we’re looking for:

We expect you to know the fundamentals, and to have real, practical experience across several of these:

  • An adversarial mindset and sharp threat-modeling instincts: trust boundaries, assets, attacks, and honesty about residual risk

  • Hands-on experience with the core security primitives in software and in silicon: secure boot, root of trust, cryptography, and key management, including how they’re implemented and where they can fail

  • Secure protocol and channel design between components

  • Strong C and Rust, and the instinct for memory safety and defensive coding that low-level security work needs

  • Experience building, not just using, security mechanisms: a secure-boot chain, key hierarchy, or attestation flow you shaped

That’s the core. We get especially curious about your application when you also bring some of the following. Very few candidates tick every box here, and we don’t expect you to:

  • Attestation at boot and at runtime, and management-plane protocols (DICE, IETF RATS, SPDM, MCTP, PLDM; confidential-computing directions like TDISP)

  • Hardware building blocks and firmware/Linux hardening (HSM, TPM, secure element, Caliptra, secure debug; open firmware/boot projects, image minimisation)

  • Assurance and resistance (supply-chain security with SBOM and SLSA, fuzzing and testing, standards like NIST 800-series, Common Criteria, OCP incl. S.A.F.E., TCG/DMTF; physical and side-channel awareness)

  • AI/LLM-assisted security tooling, and RISC-V / GPU / ML-accelerator experience

What you’re signing up for:

This is a young company doing hard things, balanced across hardware and software. We’re building the software layer for a whole inference system as it takes shape, so you’ll often be securing systems ahead of the hardware: reasoning about a threat model against a specification first, then a simulator, then early boards. You’ll work with incomplete information and watch it get sharper with every iteration. That takes comfort with ambiguity and a bias for action. If that sounds daunting, this may not be the role. If it sounds like the fun part, we should talk.

Boundaries between areas are soft here. Security touches every layer, so you’ll work across bare metal, RTOS, and Linux, and alongside the architecture and hardware teams as much as the rest of the software team. That breadth is a good part of the job.

You’ll be there for first bring-up, the first secure boot that verifies, the first device that attests itself, the first clean end-to-end run. A piece of what you built will live in silicon and in every rack we ship.

We want a team that reflects the world it’s built for, and we welcome applicants from every background, including those whose path here hasn’t been a straight line. We care that you’re excited by this kind of work, that you bring security rigour, and that you make a team better.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role.

  • Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation

  • Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance.

  • Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment.

Fractile is seeking to increase the clock speed of global progress, one chip at a time. We’ve recently raised $220M from investors including Founders Fund and Accel and our most important work lies ahead. Join us!

 

Export controls

Our work involves technologies subject to UK, US and other international export control regulations. Certain roles may require additional eligibility checks to ensure compliance with applicable law. We'll be transparent about this throughout the hiring process.

title: Microsoft 365 Administrator (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Sie haben schon einmal einen gewachsenen Microsoft-365-Tenant aufgeräumt: Gruppen zusammengeführt, Rechte und Zugriffe neu geregelt und Richtlinien so aufgesetzt, dass alles verlässlich läuft? Und Sie möchten diese Verantwortung jetzt für ein Unternehmen mit Standorten in mehreren Ländern übernehmen?

Über unseren Mandanten

Unser Mandant ist ein international tätiger Industriezulieferer der Mobilitätsbranche mit Hauptsitz im Großraum Kassel. Das Unternehmen wächst auf einer sehr soliden Auftragsbasis, und die IT soll dieses Wachstum mit zuverlässigen Services begleiten.

Warum diese Rolle?

Die IT-Infrastruktur soll jetzt Schritt für Schritt sauber aufgestellt werden. Rollen, Gruppen und Gruppenrichtlinien sind über die Zeit entstanden und brauchen eine klare Ordnung. Zugleich soll der Tenant alle Standorte sauber abbilden, und der weitere Rollout von Microsoft 365 in die Organisation steht an.

  • Weil Sie Ihre Vorstellung eines sauberen Tenants einbringen und die Verantwortung dafür tragen.

  • Weil Sie die Roadmap für den weiteren Rollout von Anfang an prägen.

  • Weil am Ende ein Backend steht, auf das sich das Unternehmen beim Wachsen verlassen kann.

Das sind Ihre Aufgaben

  • Sie ordnen Rollen, Gruppen und Berechtigungen neu: Gruppen zusammenführen, Namenskonventionen festlegen, ein Rollenkonzept mit RBAC und Privileged Identity Management aufbauen, bei Bedarf mit Administrative Units je Land.

  • Sie verantworten Identitäten und Zugriffe in Entra ID, je nach Umgebung hybrid mit lokalem Active Directory, einschließlich Conditional Access und MFA.

  • Sie bereinigen bestehende Gruppenrichtlinien und überführen sie schrittweise nach Intune.

  • Sie bauen Intune als Plattform für die Geräteverwaltung aus: Autopilot, Softwareverteilung, Compliance-Richtlinien sowie Smartphones und Tablets.

  • Sie setzen Sicherheitsgrundlagen im Tenant um, darunter Defender-Basisschutz in Abstimmung mit dem externen SOC, und halten Lizenzen und Admin-Konten sauber.

  • Sie betreuen Exchange Online, Teams und SharePoint auf technischer Ebene.

  • Sie planen den weiteren Rollout von Microsoft 365 mit, bringen ihn in die Organisation und halten Standards schriftlich fest.

Zur Einordnung: Die Rolle verantwortet das technische Backend von Microsoft 365, also Tenant, Identitäten, Berechtigungen, Richtlinien und Sicherheit. Sie konzipieren und setzen selbst um. Dabei arbeiten Sie im Infrastruktur-Team eng mit den Kolleginnen und Kollegen an den Standorten in Europa und Nordamerika zusammen.

Das bringen Sie mit

  • Eine abgeschlossene IT-Ausbildung oder ein Studium mit IT-Bezug

  • Mehrere Jahre Praxis in der Administration von Microsoft 365 im Betrieb eines Unternehmens, idealerweise mit mehreren Standorten oder Ländern

  • Sicheren Umgang mit Entra ID, Conditional Access, Intune und Exchange Online sowie Erfahrung in der Migration von Gruppenrichtlinien

  • Automatisierung mit PowerShell und Microsoft Graph

  • Projekterfahrung und die Fähigkeit, ein Thema eigenständig zu strukturieren und zum Abschluss zu bringen

  • Sehr gutes Deutsch und gutes Englisch

  • Von Vorteil: Zertifizierungen wie MS-102, MD-102, SC-300 oder AZ-104 sowie Erfahrung mit Microsoft Defender

Das erwartet Sie

  • Eine Fachrolle mit voller Verantwortung für Ihr Thema, in einem Infrastruktur-Team mit erfahrener Führung, die Rückhalt gibt

  • Arbeitsplatz im Großraum Kassel: Die Rolle lebt vom direkten Austausch, deshalb arbeiten Sie überwiegend vor Ort

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und 30 Tage Urlaub

  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket, Bikeleasing und Weiterbildung

Interesse?

Wenn Sie sich in dieser Rolle wiederfinden, senden Sie uns Ihren Lebenslauf mit Gehaltsvorstellung und frühestem Eintrittstermin.

title: Microsoft 365 & Intune Administrator:in (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Wir sind das Rückgrat einiger Non-Profit-Organisationen in Berlin. Wir bauen verlässliche und sichere IT-Lösungen, damit sich Vereine, Stiftungen und NGOs auf das Wesentliche konzentrieren können: ihre Mission. Bei uns baust du IT, die trägt – statt Tickets abzuarbeiten.

Unsere Kund:innen sind Organisationen wie das Deutsche Kinderhilfswerk, die Technologiestiftung Berlin oder die Weltbank Group – Menschen, die mit ihrer Arbeit etwas verändern. Und du sorgst dafür, dass ihre IT verlässlich funktioniert.

Deine Rolle

Du bist bei uns die Person für Microsoft 365 und Intune. Du entscheidest, wie ein Tenant aufgesetzt ist, welche Richtlinien für Konten und Geräte gelten und wie die Daten vom alten Fileserver sauber in SharePoint landen. Bevor bei Kund:innen etwas umgebaut wird, planst du es – von der Bestandsaufnahme über das Zielbild bis zum Cut-over – und setzt es anschließend mit dem Team um. Unser IT-Support arbeitet nach deinen Standards und spiegelt dir, was im Alltag hakt.

Was du bei uns machst

Microsoft 365 & Entra ID

  • Tenants aufsetzen und aufräumen: Rollen, Lizenzen, Gruppen, Gastzugriffe und klare Namenskonventionen

  • Exchange Online betreuen: Postfächer, Verteiler, Mail-Flow, Spam- und Phishing-Schutz, SPF, DKIM und DMARC

  • SharePoint und Teams so strukturieren, dass Seiten, Bibliotheken und Berechtigungen auch in zwei Jahren noch verständlich sind

  • Identitäten absichern: MFA, Conditional Access, Notfallkonten und Rechtekonzepte in Entra ID

Intune & Endgeräte

  • Windows-Geräte über Intune verwalten: Konfigurations- und Compliance-Richtlinien, Updates und App-Rollouts

  • Geräte-Rollouts und Windows-11-Umstellungen planen und durchziehen, gern mit Autopilot

  • Microsoft Defender for Business einrichten und Meldungen bewerten

  • Apple-Geräte einbinden, wo Kund:innen gemischt arbeiten, über Intune und Apple Business Manager

Migrationen & Projekte

  • Bestandsaufnahmen bei Kund:innen durchführen und daraus ein Zielbild entwickeln: Wo soll die IT in ein bis zwei Jahren stehen?

  • Umzüge planen und umsetzen: vom Fileserver nach SharePoint, von Google Workspace zu Microsoft 365, von Tenant zu Tenant oder raus aus dem lokalen Active Directory

  • Den Plan selbst mit umsetzen: Testlauf, Cut-over am Wochenende, Rückfallebene und Nachbetreuung der Nutzer:innen

  • Konzepte so aufschreiben, dass Geschäftsführung und Vorstand entscheiden können: mit Varianten, Kosten und Risiken

  • Aufwände realistisch schätzen und Angebote gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung vorbereiten

Copilot, KI & Automatisierung

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot und andere KI-Tools bei Kund:innen einführen – mit aufgeräumten Berechtigungen, Vertraulichkeitsbezeichnungen und geklärtem Datenschutz

  • Wiederkehrendes automatisieren: PowerShell, Microsoft Graph oder Power Automate

Support & Schulung

  • Zweite Eskalationsstufe für alles rund um Microsoft 365 und Endgeräte – vor Ort in Berlin

  • Technische Entscheidungen verständlich begründen, auch gegenüber Geschäftsführungen ohne IT-Hintergrund

  • Kurze Security- und Anwendungsschulungen für Mitarbeitende unserer Kund:innen

Was du mitbringen solltest

  • Du arbeitest überwiegend vor Ort: im Büro in Schöneberg und ab und an bei unseren Kund:innen in Berlin, dazu bis zu 2 Tage Homeoffice pro Woche.

  • Ausbildung als Fachinformatiker:in Systemintegration oder mindestens zwei Jahre Praxis in der Administration

  • Fundierte Erfahrung mit Microsoft 365 auf Administrationsebene: Tenant-Struktur, Exchange Online, SharePoint/OneDrive, Teams, Entra ID

  • Praktische Erfahrung mit Intune: Richtlinien, Compliance, App-Rollouts – du definierst Standards, statt sie nur anzuwenden

  • Du denkst erst in Konzepten, dann in Klicks: Du hast schon eine Microsoft-365-Migration oder ein größeres Geräte-Rollout selbst geplant und durchgezogen und kannst das verständlich aufschreiben

  • Verantwortungsvoller Umgang mit KI: Du nutzt KI-Tools gern und prüfst ihre Ergebnisse, bevor sie bei Kund:innen landen. Du führst kein Skript aus, das du nicht verstehst, und gibst Kundendaten nur in freigegebene Tools

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse (mindestens C1-Niveau) sowie gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

  • Du erklärst Technik klar, freundlich und mit Geduld

Nice to have

  • Microsoft-Zertifizierungen wie MS-102, MD-102 oder SC-300

  • Erfahrung mit Autopilot, Defender for Business oder Microsoft Purview

  • Tenant-zu-Tenant-Migrationen oder das Ablösen von Entra ID Hybrid-Setups

  • Berührungspunkte mit Google Workspace oder Apple-Geräteverwaltung

  • Erfahrung mit Microsoft-Lizenzen für gemeinnützige Organisationen und Berührungspunkte mit Non-Profit, NGO oder Stiftung

Du fühlst dich eher in der ganzen Breite zu Hause, mit Netzwerk, Backup und Security? Dann schau dir auch unsere Stelle als IT-Administrator:in für Non-Profits an.

Was wir dir bieten

  • Gehalt: 48.000 – 68.000 € brutto/Jahr (je nach Erfahrung)

  • Vollzeit, 40 Stunden pro Woche

  • Arbeit mit Sinn: du unterstützt Organisationen, die gesellschaftlich etwas bewegen

  • Gestaltungsspielraum: Du entscheidest, wie unsere Microsoft-365-Standards aussehen – kein Konzern-Freigabeprozess

  • Kleines, wachsendes Team mit kurzen Wegen

  • KI-Tools im Arbeitsalltag: bereitgestellt und erwünscht, mit klaren Regeln

  • Einladendes Büro (guter Kaffee!) in Berlin-Schöneberg und 1–2 Homeoffice-Tage pro Woche für Konzepte, Doku und Skripte

  • Bezahlte Fortbildungen, etwa für Microsoft-Zertifizierungen

  • Regelmäßig gemeinsam raus – Teamreise in die Berge oder ans Meer

  • Deutschlandticket oder Gym-Mitgliedschaft, dazu 50 € Sachbezug im Monat

Bewirb dich und werde Teil unseres Teams - Begleite den Bau der modernsten und innovativsten Wind- und PV-Projekte in Deutschland!

Deine Aufgaben

  • Verwaltung von Benutzerkonten, Berechtigungen, Gruppen, Postfächern, Lizenzen, Rufnummern und Endgeräten sowie Begleitung von Mitarbeiterein- und -austritten

  • Administration und Betreuung von Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams inklusive Telefonie, SharePoint und OneDrive sowie Unterstützung unserer Mitarbeiter bei technischen Fragestellungen

title: Microsoft Fabric Analytics Engineer (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:

title: Microwave Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • Work on a civilisation-scale problem - Clean, baseload fusion energy is one of the few genuinely world-changing challenges, and every hire in Finance, People, or Legal directly accelerates the path to a working stellarator.

  • Grow as fast as the company does - With headcount set to roughly 5x in a few years and major technical milestones ahead on the path to our demo machine and first power plant, your role grows under you; today's hire is tomorrow's function lead.

  • Tackle problems that don't exist elsewhere - Fusion sits at a rare intersection of deep-tech R&D, industrial procurement, government relations, and venture financing, so non-tech functions face challenges no other workplace can offer.

YOUR IMPACT

As a microwave design engineer, you will help build the basis for the millimeter wave hardware acting as the spark plug that initiates a fusion plasma and raises its temperature to greater than 100 million degrees. You’ll join the Alpha Heating System team ready to drive the integrated RF and thermo-mechanical design of high-power components, and help build and test these components in the lab before installing them at scale on our net scientific gain Alpha stellarator.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Provide innovative solutions to complex RF engineering challenges by collaborating closely with physicists to ensure component designs meet the Alpha plasma physics and thermal-mechanical constraints.

  • Develop designs and evaluate vendor designs to determine an optimal path to efficiently deliver our power to the stellarator - driving down the denominator of input power that will limit fusion power plant gain Q=Pout/Pin - and drive down costs.

  • Draw from and contribute to our stellarator development process, interfacing your RF components with other stellarator systems.

  • Contribute to mechanical and thermal analysis and sensitivity studies for component viability under the loads and stresses imposed by the combination of vacuum, magnetic fields, temperatures, and MW-scale RF loads.

  • Interface with the Alpha project management teams to realize the delivery of RF components and meet the tight Proxima timelines.

WHO YOU ARE

  • A highly capable RF engineer with experience in millimeter waves and knowledge of the tools and best practices for design of these systems

  • Demonstrated familiarly with RF modeling codes - SURF3D, CST, COMSOL, GdfidL, openEMS, even self-developed python codes or ones plasma physics community hasn’t heard of - capable of performing modeling at 200 GHz frequencies

  • Experience validating first-of-a-kind designs with uncertain performance, working as part of a team on multi-scale and multi-physics simulations, testing, and prototyping.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts clearly and persuasively.

  • Experience with gyrotrons and associated components - transmission systems, launcher antennas, rf loads; experience with plasma physics is a plus.

  • Understanding of quasi optical propagation of millimeter waves; ray tracing and where it breaks down

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)


*This role sits at "L2-L3" of our framework, please inquire during the recruitment process for further information.

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

title: Mid-Level Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
At Ledgy, we’re on a mission to make Europe a powerhouse of entrepreneurship by building a modern, tech-driven equity management and financial reporting platform for private and public companies. In 2026, we aim to be the leading provider for European IPOs and reporting for share-based payments. We are a value-based company with a core focus on being humble, transparent, ambitious and impactful, all in order to delivery the best experience for our customers and end users.

We are proud to partner with some of the world’s leading investors. New Enterprise Associates led our $22m Series B round in 2022, with Philip Chopin joining Sequoia’s Luciana Lixandru on our board.

We were founded in Switzerland in 2017 and today we operate globally from offices in Zurich and London. We encourage diversity and are an international team coming from 26 different countries and speaking 25 different languages.

About the role

As a Mid-level Software Engineer at Ledgy, you’ll build reliable, scalable product experiences that help companies manage their equity with confidence. You’ll work closely with experienced engineers, product managers, and designers to turn complex equity workflows into clear, automated, user-friendly software.

This role is a strong fit if you’re ready to take ownership of well-scoped projects, grow your technical judgement, and contribute across the stack while learning from senior peers.

Location: We hire remotely across the UK, Spain, Germany, Poland, and Romania. For candidates based in London, we use a hybrid model with 2 days in the office per week.

Teams we are hiring for:

  • Core Equity — Owns the foundational logic that powers Ledgy’s equity engine. Every equity-related event — such as issuing shares, creating new pools, or adjusting ownership — generates transactions. This team defines and maintains the transaction logic, data model, and core domain behaviour that ensure Ledgy’s platform remains accurate, scalable, and compliant. They also enable employees to sell their shares seamlessly once vested.
  • Workflows & Automation — Focuses on automating complex equity workflows and integrating with third-party services, including the trading exchange. The team builds systems that help company admins efficiently onboard and offboard employees, automate equity grants and terminations.
  • Reporting — Transforms Ledgy’s core equity data into financial, operational, and compliance reports. The team manages large, complex datasets and ensures reporting is accurate, performant, and reliable across jurisdictions and company structures. Their work powers the insights companies and auditors rely on for decision-making and transparency.
  • Tax — Ensures taxes are correctly reflected throughout equity operations, especially moments such as exercising, selling, mobility, and other taxable events. As a future team, Tax will build end-to-end product capabilities across the stack, helping customers manage complex tax and compliance requirements accurately across jurisdictions.

You will thrive in the role if you

  • You have 3+ years of experience working as a Software Engineer
  • You are comfortable building and shipping production-quality features across the stack
  • You enjoy learning complex domains and turning them into simple, maintainable product experiences
  • You care about clean, tested, readable code and thoughtful collaboration
  • You are curious about equity, financial workflows, and their real-world impact on companies and employees
  • You’re excited to grow your technical judgement through code reviews, pairing, and architecture discussions
  • You take ownership of your work while asking for input early when trade-offs are unclear

Our Tech Stack*:

We have a modern, cohesive stack that lets us move fast while maintaining quality:

  • Language: TypeScript
  • Frontend: React, Tailwind CSS, tRPC
  • Backend: tRPC, Node.js, MongoDB, Temporal
  • Infrastructure: GCP, Terraform Cloud, Kubernetes, Docker, GitHub Actions

*We don’t expect proficiency in this specific stack

What Your Journey Could Look Like

First 30 days:

  • Be paired with an onboarding buddy who will introduce you to the world of equity management
  • Get to know your engineering team, product managers, and designers
  • Learn how your team’s domain connects to the broader Ledgy platform
  • Set up your development environment and start contributing small, well-scoped changes
  • Build familiarity with our codebase, product workflows, and engineering practices

First 3 months:

  • Ship product features and improvements with increasing independence
  • Work with teammates to break down problems, understand trade-offs, and deliver reliable solutions
  • Participate actively in code reviews and team discussions
  • Develop a deeper understanding of how companies manage and automate equity
  • Contribute to improving quality, maintainability, and user experience in your team’s domain

First 6–12 months:

  • Own medium-sized features from implementation through release
  • Collaborate with Product and Design to shape pragmatic, user-centric solutions
  • Contribute to technical discussions around data models, workflows, and scalability
  • Continue growing toward senior-level ownership, judgement, and impact

The interview process:

  • Getting to know you (45 min): Meet with someone from our people team to talk about your experience and to ask questions about the role
    • Hackerrank take-home assessment (30-45mins) - this is a test to assess core coding cability
  • Live Coding (60 min): An equity domain problem to solve collaboratively using your preferred language and IDE. We want to see how you think, so this step does not allow AI. But you can freely look up syntax questions if you need to.
  • System Design (60 min): A system design session focused on practical problem-solving, clear trade-offs, and how you structure technical thinking
  • Behavioural (45 min): Answer behavioural style questions about your experience, using the STAR method - with a PM and EM.
  • Culture Interview: A chance to meet one of our founders and your hiring manager for a 30-minute chat about Ledgy’s mission and values
  • Offer 🎉

Being part of Ledgy means:

  • Recharge and re-energize with flexible working hours, 25 days of vacation, and up to 40 days of remote work from outside your home country.
  • We make space for your own professional development, with a generous yearly learning & development budget.
  • This role will receive a competitive salary + benefits + equity. All salaries are aligned with competitively benchmarked ranges based on work location and levelling.
  • For candidates based in London or Zurich we use a hybrid work model of 2 days in the office per week.

title: Mid-Market Account Executive - France
descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara is a fortress in a volatile market. We are a $1.9B ARR, NYSE-listed powerhouse that sells essential technology to the physical operations powering the global economy. This is a seat built for high performers and incredibly driven individuals who want to accelerate their careers — the bar for entry is high, but those who execute are well rewarded for it.

While the rest of the tech scene is scaling back, our France team continued to perform above 100% last year. We are looking for territory owners who want to manage deal cycles from €20k to €200k, selling a complex suite of 15+ products to 8 different personas, including MDs and Finance Directors. If you want to be pushed to your limit and rewarded with the stability of a market leader, this is the place.

Whilst the role can be worked remotely anywhere in France, there is a need to visit clients in the region as required (typically fortnightly basis).

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara's top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you'll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven't been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara's high-performance Sales culture means you'll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

In this role you will:

  • Own your destiny: Operate as a pure revenue leader, responsible for 80-90% net-new logo acquisition through self-sourced pipeline.
  • Get In Early: The France Mid-Market is a high-achieving segment in the company. The window to build something significant is open right now.
  • Sharpen Your Edge: Access elite enablement — Command the Message and MEDDPICC coaching — built to make you a more effective closer.
  • Navigate Complexity: Move beyond feature-pushing to sell high-level ROI and safety outcomes to sophisticated economic buyers (MDs and FDs) in the field and the boardroom.

Minimum requirements for this role:

  • The Winning DNA: A minimum of 18 months in a full-cycle, outbound-heavy SaaS closing role. You must have a proven history of building your own pipe from scratch.
  • Verified Overachievement: A track record of hitting and exceeding quota in a competitive, complex environment. We'll want to see this on your resume.
  • Strategic Grit: Experience managing multi-stakeholder deal cycles and technical POCs. We value your ability to hunt more than the brand name on your previous CV.
  • Native French language

An ideal candidate also offers:

  • Intellectual Curiosity: You are eager to learn the inner workings of diverse industries, from waste management to food distribution, to better align our technology with their operational pain.
  • A Repeatable Sales Framework: You don't rely on luck or intuition. You have a structured methodology that delivers success and you understand that consistent, high-quality inputs lead to predictable results.
  • A Data-Minded Approach: You are a student of your own funnel. You understand how to structure your activity—prospecting volume, discovery depth, and multi-threading—to ensure a consistent output and forecast accuracy.
  • Continuous Process Iteration: You possess a relentless drive for self-improvement. You are someone who actively seeks feedback, iterates on their approach, and understands that evolving your tactics is the only way to stay ahead of the market.

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara's Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

title: Mid-Market Account Executive
descriptionHtml:
Overview  

This is a new-logo sales role focused exclusively on private-sector accounts with 500–1,999 employees across the UK, Ireland and South Africa. Operating in a channel-first organisation, you will own a fully indirect sales motion and build a greenfield territory without an inherited customer base. This role does not have dedicated BDR support and is accountable for independently generating sufficient pipeline to achieve its ARR target. You will use account, SKU and industry-growth data to create, own and execute a territory plan that delivers sustainable net new ARR growth. 

What will you be doing?  

As a Mid-Market Account Executive, you will identify, develop and close new-logo opportunities across the defined territory. You will manage the full sales cycle through partners, from self-sourced pipeline creation and qualification through to commercial close, with an indicative fully ramped net new ARR target of approximately USD 700,000. 

Your responsibilities will include:  

  • Creating, validating, owning and executing a data-led territory plan that clearly shows how you will achieve your net new ARR target, including the priority accounts, sales plays, partner routes to market and supporting resources required.
  • Developing new prospects solely through new-logo acquisition across private-sector accounts with 500–1,999 employees in the UK, Ireland and South Africa, without an inherited customer base.
  • Managing complex, fully indirect sales cycles through channel partners using a consultative, platform-led rather than point-solution approach, engaging business and technical stakeholders throughout the buying journey.
  • Planning and delivering presentations that give prospective insights into how our solutions solve their challenges 
  • Working in direct partnership with the Partner Account Manager as a core part of territory planning, partner activation, pipeline creation and deal execution. The AE and PAM will jointly develop and execute partner-led routes to market, supported by Solution Engineers and Marketing to progress and close business. Customer Success support becomes available once the customer reaches the appropriate qualifying ARR threshold.
  • Communicating new product developments to prospective clients 
  • Attending remote and on-site meetings with clients (note this is a field role thus in person customer and partner collaboration emphasized)  
  • Collaborating with teams in different territories and offices 
  • Using available account, SKU and industry-growth data to identify whitespace, prioritise opportunities and execute effective sales campaigns across the private-sector territory; this role is not aligned to a single industry vertical.
  • Self-sourcing and qualifying your own pipeline without BDR support. PAM, SE and Marketing resources are expected to complement—not replace—your personal prospecting and pipeline-generation activity.
  • Maintaining an accurate and current pipeline of opportunities within the CRM system  

OK, I'm interested... is this the job for me?  

We look for people who value agility, passion and teamwork; those who can bring fresh ideas to the table and want the opportunity to learn, grow, and expand their careers. Bring your aptitude and build upon what you do best for our customers, partners, team, and you.   

In this role, you are accountable for building a greenfield territory and delivering new business solely through new-logo acquisition. You will use available account, SKU and industry-growth data to identify opportunities across the private sector rather than specialising in a single vertical. Success requires an entrepreneurial, self-motivated approach: you will create your own pipeline, coordinate the resources around you and own execution from territory strategy through to net new ARR delivery. All opportunities will be progressed through partners in line with our channel-first model. 

Other qualities you’ll need to be a fit for this role include:  

  • 3–5 years of previous B2B sales experience, with a demonstrable record of winning new-logo business and delivering against ARR or recurring-revenue targets.
  • Experience in the software/technology industry is preferred, but not essential 
  • Experience with executive selling, both business and technical 
  • Excellent communication and listening skills 
  • Determination to surpass performance goals 
  • Willingness to learn and bring new ideas

title: Mid Market Sales Manager (Paris)
descriptionHtml:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The role

We’re hiring a Sales Leader to build Dust’s go-to-market presence across French Mid-Market and SMB customers. This is an opportunity to shape how we reach and grow a broad range of businesses, from developing an efficient sales motion to helping customers see value quickly and expand over time.

You’ll act as the business lead for the segment, with accountability for revenue. You’ll lead and coach the sales team, stay close to customers and deals, and build a repeatable approach that balances efficient execution with the different needs of SMB and Mid-Market customers.

You’ll also coordinate the teams that support pipeline generation, sales, and customer growth. Working closely with BDR, Growth, Field Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Solutions Engineering, Deployment, and Customer Success, you’ll focus resources on the channels and activities that can best support the segment’s goals.

What you’ll do

  • Lead, coach, and grow the sales team for the Mid-Market and SMB segment, including hiring, performance, and day-to-day execution.

  • Own the segment’s ARR plan, forecast, and qualified pipeline. Set priorities with the CRO, review progress, and address gaps early.

  • Define and refine the sales approach for SMB and Mid-Market customers, adapting qualification, messaging, and deal support to each customer’s needs.

  • Build an efficient path from target account and first conversation through qualification, evaluation, close, handoff, and expansion.

  • Coach sellers on discovery, value-based selling, pipeline discipline, and helping customers make decisions with confidence.

  • Make clear, evidence-based recommendations to Product based on customer conversations, deal patterns, and segment needs.

  • Work with BDR and Growth leaders to build qualified pipeline through targeted outbound and other relevant channels.

  • Partner with Field Marketing to prioritize campaigns, events, customer advocacy, and community programs that support pipeline and revenue goals. Work within the marketing leadership’s standards and methods, and ensure programs are well executed and measured.

  • Set direction for how Partnerships can support segment priorities, working with the Partnerships lead on relevant sourcing, co-selling, and delivery opportunities.

  • Coordinate with Solutions Engineering, Deployment, Professional Services, and Customer Success to support effective evaluations, smooth implementations, adoption, and expansion.

  • Share market learning with the CRO and other segment leads, helping Dust develop a coherent France go-to-market approach.

What we’re looking for

  • A proven B2B software sales professional who has grown from individual contributor into people leadership, with 5+ years leading sales teams and a hands-on understanding of how to help sellers succeed.

  • Experience selling to SMB and Mid-Market customers, with the judgment to adapt the sales motion to different deal sizes, buying processes, and customer needs.

  • A track record of owning a segment or market revenue number end to end and building pipeline through functions you did not directly manage.

  • Experience coaching sellers, building a reliable forecast, and creating consistent sales practices.

  • Good commercial judgment about where to focus team capacity and budget, including how direct sales, marketing, and partners can support growth.

  • Strong collaboration skills across BDR, Growth, Field Marketing, Partnerships, RevOps, and post-sales teams.

  • High EQ, clear communication, and a supportive but accountable leadership style.

  • Comfort building repeatable sales practices in a scaling organization. French fluency and strong working English are important.

What success looks like

The Mid-Market and SMB segment has clear sales ownership, a focused pipeline, and progress against its ARR goals. Sellers are well coached and can execute an efficient, repeatable motion suited to their customers. Cross-functional support is aligned to segment priorities, and learning from customers and deals helps Dust improve how it serves and grows SMB and Mid-Market accounts in France.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.
