This is a senior individual contributor role focused on leading design from problem framing through delivery, partnering closely with cross-functional teams, and contributing to the Airalo Product Design Guild - our community for craft, critique, design systems, research-led decision-making, accessibility, experimentation, AI, and continuous learning.
Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
  • Lead end-to-end product design for Airalo’s consumer mobile and web experiences, from discovery through delivery.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Research, Content Design, Data, Growth, and other designers to translate customer needs, insights, and strategy into high-quality product improvements.
  • Create user journeys, flows, wireframes, prototypes, high-fidelity designs, UX copy, and production-ready specifications.
  • Facilitate workshops, critiques, ideation sessions, and stakeholder conversations that create alignment and momentum.
  • Contribute to Airalo’s Design System, improving consistency, accessibility, quality, and efficiency across products.
  • Mentor other designers through feedback, pairing, critique, and shared practice.
  • Help strengthen the Product Design Guild by raising the bar for craft, collaboration, research-led decision-making, and thoughtful use of AI.

    • Must-haves:
  • 6+ years or similar of dedicated experience in product design at a tech startup, scale-up, product-led company, or product-focused agency.
  • A strong portfolio showing high-quality UI, thoughtful interaction design, strong product thinking, and measurable impact.
  • Extensive experience designing, testing, and shipping native mobile and web applications for B2C products.
  • Ability to lead ambiguous design problems from discovery through delivery, balancing user needs, business goals, technical constraints, and product strategy.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication in English, with the ability to explain design rationale clearly to cross-functional partners and senior stakeholders.
  • Advanced Figma and FigJam skills, with experience creating flows, prototypes, product specifications, and production-ready design assets.
  • Advanced experience working with design systems, native mobile guidelines, responsive design, accessibility, and product quality across mobile and web.
  • Advanced experience with motion, prototyping, or interaction details that bring product experiences to life.
  • Experience working in Lean and/or Agile product development environments, collaborating closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Content, Data, and Growth.
  • Able to facilitate workshops, critiques, ideation sessions, and alignment conversations.
  • Experience using AI and emerging tools to improve the design workflow beyond simple prototyping.

    • Good to have:
  • Experience in telecommunications, travel, marketplaces, subscriptions, or global consumer products.
  • Knowledge of eSIMs, GSMA-related technologies, or mobile connectivity services.
  • Experience partnering deeply with Research, Data, Growth, or Content Design teams.

    • You should apply if…
  • You lead through craft, clarity, and systems thinking. You can turn complex problems into simple, well-crafted experiences while considering journeys, patterns, accessibility, content, edge cases, and scale.
  • You can own ambiguous problems. You do not need every answer before you start. You ask good questions, define the path forward, make smart trade-offs, and keep momentum without waiting to be told what to do.
  • You care about outcomes, not just output. You use research, data, customer feedback, and product strategy to make decisions that improve the user experience and support business goals.
  • You communicate with confidence and humility. You can explain design decisions clearly to designers, engineers, product managers, and senior stakeholders without becoming defensive.
  • You raise the bar for the design community. You give thoughtful feedback, invite critique early, mentor others, and contribute to a Product Design Guild where designers learn and improve together.
  • You are curious about AI and new ways of working. You actively explore how AI and emerging tools can improve design workflows, speed up learning, and help teams make better decisions.

    • This isn't for you if…
  • You only want to design screens. This role requires shaping problems, influencing direction, collaborating across disciplines, and staying involved from discovery through delivery.
  • You need certainty or close direction to make progress. Senior designers at Airalo are expected to move through ambiguity, create momentum, and make thoughtful decisions independently.
  • You avoid feedback or critique. Our design culture depends on sharing unfinished work, challenging ideas respectfully, and changing direction when the evidence points elsewhere.
  • You optimize for perfection over impact. We care deeply about quality, but we also need to make pragmatic decisions, learn quickly, and ship improvements.
  • You are not interested in customers or the community. Speaking to customers, learning from them, and contributing to the Product Design Guild are central to how we build better products.

    We started Airalo to make staying connected effortless, wherever you are in the world. Today, millions of travelers rely on our eSIMs, and many of the people building the product were customers first.

Join Tether and Shape the Future of Digital Finance

At Tether, we’re not just building products, we’re pioneering a global financial revolution. Our cutting-edge solutions empower businesses—from exchanges and wallets to payment processors and ATMs—to seamlessly integrate reserve-backed tokens across blockchains. By harnessing the power of blockchain technology, Tether enables you to store, send, and receive digital tokens instantly, securely, and globally, all at a fraction of the cost. But that’s just the beginning:

Tether Power: Driving sustainable growth, our energy solutions optimize excess power for Bitcoin mining using eco-friendly practices in state-of-the-art, geo-diverse facilities.

Tether Data: Fueling breakthroughs in AI and peer-to-peer technology, we reduce infrastructure costs and enhance global communications with cutting-edge solutions like KEET, our flagship app that redefines secure and private data sharing.

Tether Education: Democratizing access to top-tier digital learning, we empower individuals to thrive in the digital and gig economies, driving global growth and opportunity.

Tether Evolution: At the intersection of technology and human potential, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible, crafting a future where innovation and human capabilities merge in powerful, unprecedented ways.

Why Join Us?

Our team is a global talent powerhouse, working remotely from every corner of the world. If you’re passionate about making a mark in the fintech space, this is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the brightest minds, pushing boundaries and setting new standards. We’ve grown fast, stayed lean, and secured our place as a leader in the industry.

If you have excellent English communication skills and are ready to contribute to the most innovative platform on the planet, Tether is the place for you.

Are you ready to be part of the future?

About the job

We're changing how the world moves money. Wallets are where that change becomes real: the first place millions of people truly own their money. You'll own design execution across our wallets, working directly with the Design Lead to shape where they go next.

Responsibilities

  • Own design execution end to end: from concept and prototype to launch and iteration.

  • Turn complex, conceptual ideas into experiences that feel simple to someone using a wallet for the first time.

  • Prototype fast and often: high-fidelity and interactive, in days not weeks, using the best tools available, AI included.

Important information for candidates
Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. To protect yourself, please keep the following in mind when applying for roles:

  • Double-check email addresses. All communication from us will come from emails ending in @tether.to or @tether.io

  • We will never request payment or financial details. If someone asks for personal financial information or payment at any point during the hiring process, it is a scam. Please report it immediately.

When in doubt, feel free to reach out through our official website.

title: (Senior) Product Engineer – AI (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Worum es geht

MAIA ist eine KI-Plattform für Unternehmen. Mit MAIA durchsuchen Teams ihre internen Daten und verankern Agenten tief in ihren Prozessen. Wir begleiten Unternehmen dabei, KI nicht nur in einzelnen Abteilungen, sondern im ganzen Unternehmen einzusetzen.

Technisch heißt das: Wir bauen eine GenAI-Anwendung mit eigenen Agentensystemen, RAG-Pipelines und agentenbasierten Workflows, binden externe Systeme unserer Kunden an und analysieren ihre Daten. Wir nutzen die besten verfügbaren Modelle, betrieben in der EU, und machen sie verlässlich für anspruchsvolle Arbeit mit großen, komplexen Datenmengen.

Zahlreiche Industrieunternehmen arbeiten seit Jahren intensiv mit MAIA. Nach unserer erfolgreichen Finanzierungsrunde 2026 bringen wir MAIA jetzt in die Breite. Entwickelt wird MAIA seit 2021 in Leipzig.

Was du bei uns machst

Als Product Engineer verantwortest du Features von Anfang bis Ende: vom Gespräch mit Kunden über das Konzept bis zur Umsetzung und Weiterentwicklung in Produktion.

Woran du arbeiten kannst:

  • Kunden und Markt verstehen. Du sprichst mit Nutzerinnen und Nutzern, begleitest Kundentermine und wertest Nutzungsdaten aus. So findest du heraus, wo MAIA im Arbeitsalltag am meisten helfen kann. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit Produktmanagement und Customer Success zusammen.

  • Vom Problem zum Konzept. Du schreibst Konzepte, baust Prototypen, um Ideen schnell zu testen, und schneidest Features so, dass sie früh bei Nutzerinnen und Nutzern ankommen.

  • Umsetzen über den ganzen Stack. Du schreibst den Implementierungsplan, lässt Coding Agents umsetzen und verantwortest Architektur und Qualität, vom Datenmodell bis zur Oberfläche.

  • KI, die man versteht. Du gestaltest, wie Menschen mit MAIA arbeiten: Fragen stellen, Kontext mitgeben, Agenten mehrstufige Aufgaben erledigen lassen und Ergebnisse nachvollziehen.

  • Messen und weiterentwickeln. Nach dem Release prüfst du, ob ein Feature genutzt wird und hilft, und entwickelst es anhand von Feedback, Nutzungsdaten und Evals weiter.

Was wir suchen

  • Solides Software Engineering. Du hast Produkte gebaut und in Produktion betrieben, mit denen Menschen täglich arbeiten, über Backend und Frontend hinweg. Schwache Architektur erkennst du auch dann, wenn ein Coding Agent sie geschrieben hat.

  • Sehr gut in mindestens einer unserer Sprachen. TypeScript, Python oder Go, am besten eine der statisch typisierten. Alle drei musst du nicht mitbringen. In die anderen arbeitest du dich ein.

  • Produkterfahrung. Du hast mit Kundinnen und Kunden gesprochen, Anforderungen hinterfragt und Features von der ersten Idee bis zur täglichen Nutzung begleitet. Du hörst genau hin und erkennst, welches Problem hinter einem Wunsch steckt.

  • Gespür für gute Bedienung. Du merkst, wenn eine Oberfläche Menschen überfordert, und baust lieber eine einfache Lösung, die verstanden wird, als eine mächtige, die niemand findet.

  • Zu Hause im LLM-Ökosystem. Du hast Anwendungen mit LLMs gebaut, beruflich oder in komplexen eigenen Projekten, und kennst ihre Eigenheiten: Antworten schwanken, brauchen Zeit, und Agenten scheitern an unerwarteten Stellen. Du baust Produkte, die damit ehrlich umgehen.

  • Messen statt vermuten. Ob ein Feature wirkt, prüfst du mit Nutzungsdaten, Feedback und Evals. Du baust die einfachste Lösung, die das Problem löst.

  • Agentisch arbeiten. Coding Agents gehören für dich zum Alltag. Du schreibst Pläne, die andere prüfen und auf denen Coding Agents aufbauen können, prüfst die Ergebnisse kritisch und weißt, wo sie helfen und wo nicht.

  • Klar kommunizieren. Deine Konzepte versteht man beim ersten Lesen. Mit Kundinnen und Kunden redest du ebenso gern wie mit Engineers. Du sprichst sehr sicher Deutsch und ebenso Englisch.

Die Rolle umfasst keine Personalverantwortung. Ob du als Product Engineer oder Senior Product Engineer einsteigst, besprechen wir spätestens nach dem technischen Interview offen mit dir.

Arbeiten bei MAIA

Uns verbindet ein gemeinsames Ziel: ein richtig gutes Produkt zu bauen. Jede und jeder übernimmt Verantwortung für das eigene Thema. Wir haben Spaß an der Arbeit und sind stolz auf das, was unsere Kunden mit MAIA erreichen. Die Wege sind kurz, und Entscheidungen fallen schnell. Im Engineering-Team hinterfragen wir kritisch, wie wir entwickeln, und verbessern unsere Prozesse laufend, gerade in der agentischen Entwicklung.

Wir arbeiten gern zusammen in unserem Büro, zentral zwischen Innenstadt und Zoo, und kochen fast jeden Tag gemeinsam. An mindestens drei Tagen pro Woche sind wir vor Ort, an den übrigen arbeitest du, wo du möchtest. Wann dein Tag beginnt, legst du selbst fest.

  • Zugang zu aktuellen Frontier-Modellen und Coding Agents

  • Unterstützung bei Weiterbildungen, die zu deiner beruflichen Entwicklung passen

  • Zugang zu einer Wellpass-Mitgliedschaft

Vergütung

Das Jahresbruttogehalt liegt bei 75.000 bis 95.000 €. Wo du in dieser Spanne liegst, hängt von deinem Level ab. Darüber sprechen wir spätestens nach dem technischen Interview. Dazu kommt eine virtuelle Beteiligung über unser VSOP.

Bewerbung und nächste Schritte

Ein Anschreiben brauchst du nicht. Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und beantworte uns in ein paar eigenen Sätzen eine Frage: Warum willst du MAIA mitgestalten?

Wir arbeiten jeden Tag mit KI. Für diese Antwort zählt aber deine eigene Perspektive. Schreib sie deshalb bitte selbst, gern kurz und ohne Feinschliff.

Passt es, folgen ein 30-minütiges Kennenlernen, ein 90-minütiges technisches Interview, in dem es auch um Produktentscheidungen geht, und ein Abschlussgespräch mit der Geschäftsführung. Nach jedem Schritt hörst du in der Regel innerhalb von zwei Werktagen von uns. Unser Ziel ist eine Entscheidung in rund drei Wochen.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung.

title: (Senior) Product Engineer – AI (m/f/d) – Remote
descriptionHtml:
What we do

MAIA is an AI platform for companies. With MAIA, teams search their internal data and embed agents deep into their processes. We help companies use AI not just in individual departments, but across the entire organisation.

On a technical level, this means: we build a GenAI application with our own agent systems, RAG pipelines and agent-based workflows, connect our customers' external systems and analyse their data. We use the best available models, operated in the EU, and make them reliable for demanding work with large, complex datasets.

Many industrial companies have been using MAIA intensively for years. Following our successful 2026 funding round, we are now taking MAIA to a broader market. MAIA has been developed in Leipzig since 2021.

What you'll do

As a Product Engineer, you own features from start to finish: from conversations with customers and concept work through to implementation and continuous improvement in production.

What you can work on:

  • Understanding customers and the market. You talk to users, join customer meetings and analyse usage data. This way, you find out where MAIA can help most in people's daily work. You work closely with product management and customer success.

  • From problem to concept. You write concepts, build prototypes to test ideas quickly, and slice features so they reach users early.

  • Building across the full stack. You write the implementation plan, let coding agents implement it, and own architecture and quality, from the data model to the user interface.

  • AI that people understand. You shape how people work with MAIA: asking questions, providing context, letting agents complete multi-step tasks and following their results.

  • Measuring and improving. After a release, you check whether a feature is used and actually helps, and you keep improving it based on feedback, usage data and evals.

What we're looking for

  • Solid software engineering. You have built products that people use every day and operated them in production, across backend and frontend. You recognise weak architecture even when a coding agent wrote it.

  • Very strong in at least one of our languages. TypeScript, Python or Go, ideally one of the statically typed ones. You don't need all three. You'll get up to speed in the others.

  • Product experience. You have talked to customers, questioned requirements and taken features from the first idea to daily use. You listen closely and recognise the problem behind a request.

  • A feel for good usability. You notice when an interface overwhelms people, and you'd rather build a simple solution that people understand than a powerful one that nobody finds.

  • At home in the LLM ecosystem. You have built applications with LLMs, professionally or in complex personal projects, and you know their quirks: answers vary, take time, and agents fail in unexpected places. You build products that deal with this honestly.

  • Measure, don't guess. You check whether a feature works using usage data, feedback and evals. You build the simplest solution that solves the problem.

  • Agentic engineering. Coding agents are part of your daily work. You write plans that others review and that coding agents can build on, you review the results critically, and you know where agents help and where they don't.

  • Remote-ready. You communicate proactively, document your work so others can follow it, and move things forward without constant coordination.

  • Clear communication. People understand your concepts on first read. You enjoy talking to customers as much as to engineers. You are fluent in English. German is a strong plus, as many of our customer conversations are in German.

This role has no people management responsibility. Whether you join at regular or senior level is something we'll discuss openly with you after the technical interview at the latest.

Working at MAIA

We share a common goal: building a really great product. Everyone takes ownership of their own area. We enjoy our work and are proud of what our customers achieve with MAIA. Paths are short and decisions are made quickly. In the engineering team, we critically question how we develop and continuously improve our processes, especially in agentic development.

Much of the team works together in our office in Leipzig, centrally located between the city centre and the zoo, where we cook together almost every day. You work remotely from anywhere in Germany. You need to live in Germany for this role. Twice a year, we meet in person for team events, and from time to time there are team days in Leipzig. When your day starts is up to you.

  • Access to the latest frontier models and coding agents

  • Support for training that fits your professional development

  • Access to a Wellpass membership

Compensation

The annual gross salary is €75,000 to €95,000. Where you fall within this range depends on your level. We'll discuss this after the technical interview at the latest. On top of that, you receive a virtual share in our VSOP.

Application and next steps

You don't need a cover letter. Send us your CV and answer one question in a few sentences of your own: Why do you want to help shape MAIA?

We work with AI every day. For this answer, though, your own perspective is what counts. So please write it yourself. Short and unpolished is fine.

If there's a fit, you'll have a 30-minute intro call, a 90-minute technical interview that also covers product decisions and a final conversation with our management. After each step, you'll usually hear from us within two business days. Our goal is a decision in about three weeks.

We look forward to your application.

Was Dich erwartet

Du wirst Teil eines kleinen, schlagkräftigen Teams, in dem jeder Verantwortung übernimmt und Ergebnisse erzielt:

  • Remote-first Engineering-Team, mit Büro in Bielefeld.

title: Senior Product Engineer (DevTools & AI reliability, remote)
descriptionHtml:
(Fully remote, async-first, DevTools SaaS, 32-40h/week, time zones: UTC-3 to UTC+3)

The best developers don't wait for a customer to tell them something's broken.

They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist. We give developers and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: end-to-end tests and synthetic monitoring defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, versioned and reviewed like everything else they ship. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.

Thousands of them, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password, build with us. In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel.

Here's the thing about 2026: AI agents and coding assistants are shipping more software, faster, than any team could review by hand, and more of it is breaking in ways nobody has seen before. LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. You will build reliability for this kind of software.

Our stack is AI (Codex, Claude, use what you like best), Vue.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Golang, Postgres, ClickHouse and AWS. We ship to prod all day, every day. We practice Agile (not scrum) and take pride in good documentation and good looking products.

We’re a remote-first startup that keeps things simple—low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love building cool things, working async, actually listening to and working with customers, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!

What you'll do

Build and ship with AI

You will actively use coding agents for full stack development, from exploring solutions and generating scaffolding to refactoring, test generation and debugging. At Checkly we push the limits of AI tools every day.

Talk to our users

You will talk directly to the developers, DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams who are on-call, debugging incidents, or wiring Checkly into production pipelines. You will understand their workflows, pain points, and feedback. You use those conversations to validate ideas, course-correct early, and iterate on what you build. Customer calls and the weekly support rotation are part of the job, not a distraction from it.

Find the right problems to solve

In a world where the cost of building software trends to zero, the hard part is picking what to build. You will focus on real developer pain: flaky tests and flaky checks, unclear failures, noisy alerts. You will favour pragmatic solutions that ship quickly, validate assumptions in production, and compound into long-term reliability improvements.

Own your work end to end

From shaping the initial idea, through implementation and rollout, to watching how it behaves in production. You will take part in on-call and help support customers when things don’t work as expected.

What you should have

  • You have shipped features with AI, not just experimented with them. You have taken work from zero to shipped with a comparable stack, made implementation decisions that held up, and put things in front of real users.

  • You have built and run production software. You know the realities of operating software that people depend on: edge cases, incidents, regressions, and the need for observability and follow-up. You are not surprised when things break. You help fix them.

  • You can hold a product conversation, not just a technical one. You can look at a customer problem and reason about whether the thing we are about to build actually solves it.

  • You work well without an office around you. You are autonomous and self-motivated in a remote setup, and you still enjoy getting to know your colleagues and helping other people get unstuck.

  • FULLY remote role, within the UTC-3 to UTC+3 time zones. You need to be able to travel to (other) European countries without having to wait for a visa appointment, for our annual kickoff, a team meetup or a conference.

What you will hate about us

We would rather tell you now than have you find out in month two.

  • We use AI for everything, and we mean everything. AI skepticism is not a thing here. If you have the slightest hesitation about working with AI every day, this is not the place for you, and that is completely fine.

  • We write more than we talk. We are async-first, so a lot of decisions happen in documents and threads, not meetings. If you do your best thinking out loud in a room full of people, you will miss it here.

  • We are lean, so you own the unglamorous parts too. There is no separate QA team, no ops layer to hand things off to, and you are on the support rotation and the on-call rotation like everyone else.

  • We ship constantly and change our minds. Priorities move as we learn from customers. If you need long, stable planning cycles, this will feel chaotic.

  • Customer signals come first, and most of the time they matter more than your instinct. We build what customers actually want, not the clever thing we dreamed up.

Benefits

  • Transparent salary because your salary shouldn't be dictated by how good a negotiator you are. (more info below)

  • Remote-first, flexible work hours, async-first (low meeting, high productivity) and transparent culture

  • Become part of a fast-growing, international, and remote team where your work matters, and your impact won't get lost in layers of bureaucracy.

  • Stock options

  • 27 days of paid vacation + your local public holidays

  • Paid sick leave & up to 14 weeks of paid parental leave

  • Co-working budget or home office setup

  • Annual company kickoffs

Find out more here.

What we pay

Fair, competitive, and transparent pay is very important for us. Therefore we work with a standardized salary calculator that includes several factors such as seniority level as well as location.

For this role, the range is

  • €88k - €105k for someone in a similar cost of market as UK, Germany etc, + stock options

  • €79k - €97k for someone in a similar cost of market as Spain, Poland, Ukraine etc, + stock options

Apply

If this sounds interesting, please apply! Studies by several different sources have shown that on average men will apply for a job if they meet 60% of the application requirements. Women, non-binary people and POC will seek to match a much higher percentage of requirements before applying. If you're not sure you're the right fit, apply anyway and let us know what you bring to the table. We'd love to hear from you!

We're all about being transparent and setting clear expectations. That's why we've put together our hiring playbook and open-sourced our employee handbook. There you'll find a sneak peek of who we are, how we work and what you can expect in our hiring process.

title: Senior Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Deducta

Senior Product Engineer

Location: London, UK, near London Bridge. Hybrid, 2 in-person days a week.

Compensation: £120k base salary plus equity

Visa Sponsorship: Available for the right candidate

Start Date: As soon as possible

Why we exist

Every decision a business makes, from the suppliers it trusts to the risks it accepts, eventually shows up as spend. This makes spend data the most honest record of how a company operates. Not the strategy deck or the org chart: spend describes what really happened.

This record exists, but it's scattered across dozens of systems and decades of legacy technology. Companies spending billions a year still can't easily answer: Who are our suppliers? Where are we exposed? What are we paying for twice?

We believe a business that can't see itself clearly can't make great decisions. Deducta exists to give the world's most complex organisations a true picture of how they operate, and the intelligence to act on it. Our ambition is to become the category-defining platform for enterprise data intelligence.

How we do it

Most tools start and stop with dashboards. We start with the hard part: turning fragmented, messy enterprise data into a consistent foundation people can trust. Then we use AI to make it conversational, so anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer they can act on.

We're well funded, growing fast, and have already processed more than £1 trillion of spend for some of the world's largest and most recognisable companies. Our partners use Deducta to deliver major business transformations orders of magnitude faster.

Why this role matters

The data is only half the story. As AI gets better at analysing large volumes of data, the hard part shifts to the product: helping customers explore and understand what the model finds, designing for trust, and turning insight into action.

You’ll shape how customers work with agentic AI, balancing the stability and reliability enterprises expect with the new, agent-driven experiences we’re building at the cutting edge. You’ll have real autonomy in how you approach it, working in a small, high-trust team with genuine influence over product, architecture and how engineering grows.

What you'll do

  • Design, build and ship high-quality frontend experiences across Deducta's platform.

  • Work directly with customers to understand their problems, and turn those insights into product decisions.

  • Build interfaces that make large datasets, dynamic metrics and AI-generated analysis clear and useful.

  • Design for the limits of AI, so customers know when to trust an answer and how to check it.

  • Push the boundaries of applied AI, both in the product and in how we build it.

  • Own problems end to end, from definition to deployment, making sound calls on architecture, usability, performance and maintainability along the way.

Success in this role means:

  • Customers go from data to decisions: Features you've shipped help customers explore AI-generated analysis and act on it, not just search through data.

  • Trustworthy AI experiences: Customers can see where an answer came from and when to check it, so their confidence in Deducta grows as they use it more.

  • A product foundation others build on: The components and patterns you've built are fast, consistent and reused across the product by the team.

Who you are

You're a senior product engineer who cares as much about the problem as the code, and takes ideas all the way to production. You don't need a background in enterprise data or procurement. We care about how you think and the quality of the products you've built.

You might be the right fit if you have:

  • Strong JavaScript and TypeScript fundamentals, with experience building high-quality frontend applications.

  • Experience making complex data, information or workflows easy for people to understand and act on.

  • A clear view of what AI systems can and can't do, and how good product design accounts for outputs that aren't always right.

  • Sound judgement on architecture and product trade-offs, and the ability to explain the reasoning behind your decisions.

  • A track record of owning problems from investigation through to production.

  • High standards for testing, code quality and maintainability, and clear communication with engineers, customers and stakeholders.

  • A founder mindset: you see a problem and feel empowered to work out how to solve it.

We care most about how you think, the quality of your work and how you approach unfamiliar problems. Previous startup experience isn't essential, but the pace, initiative and judgement to thrive in one are.

How we work

We believe in freedom and responsibility. We set clear priorities, share the context and trust people to decide how to deliver. You'll thrive here if you value:

  • Ownership: You own the outcome, not just the task. You deliver what you commit to, follow through when things get difficult, and own your mistakes.

  • Unreasonable hospitality: You treat prospects, clients and teammates with exceptional care as a default. You anticipate needs, communicate with clarity, and help others succeed.

  • Bias for action: We don’t have every answer upfront. You move things forward without waiting to be asked, take calculated risks, and adapt as you learn.

  • Craft: Moving quickly matters, but so does doing work that stays clear, reliable and useful as we grow.

  • System building: You create leverage beyond your own output, building processes, tools and documentation that others reuse and that keep working without you.

  • Candor: You tell the hard truth early, give and receive feedback thoughtfully, ask for help when you need it, and push back when priorities need to change.

  • Curiosity about AI: You’re excited by what applied AI makes possible, and you look for ways to use it in your own work.

As an early team member, you'll help shape our culture, our processes and where Deducta goes next. We're growing quickly, and this role will grow with us.

  3. Technical interview

  4. Final interview

  5. Offer, referencing and start

title: Senior Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Engineering team

At hyperexponential, engineering is at the heart of our mission to transform the insurance industry. Our engineers build and scale, enabling insurers to model complex risks and make smarter pricing decisions at speed. By combining deep technical expertise with creativity, the team pushes the boundaries of what’s possible in insurance technology.

Within engineering, our product teams are cross-functional, pairing frontend and backend engineers with designers and product managers. This enables end-to-end ownership of features, with engineers contributing across design, architecture, implementation, and testing. Collaboration is a core part of how we work, ensuring that every release is both technically sound and valuable to our users.

About the role

Underwriters at the world's largest insurers still do much of their work in spreadsheets, email threads, and systems that were never designed for the decisions they are making. We are rebuilding that from the ground up.

You will join the Workflow Underwriting stream, building the next generation of our underwriting platform. This is not a platform with AI features bolted on. We are designing it around the agents we build, which means the architecture, the domain model, and the interaction patterns are all genuinely open questions. You will help answer them.

You will contribute at code, architecture, and domain level from your first weeks, and you will talk directly to the underwriters who use what you build.

 

What you’ll be doing

  • Design, build, and operate backend services in Kotlin or Java, and own them in production.

  • Turn ambiguous underwriting problems into simple, reliable software. Much of the work is deciding what to build, not just building it.

  • Shape architectural decisions: APIs, domain models, persistence, reliability, observability, and how the platform evolves without collapsing under its own weight.

  • Build real depth in the underwriting domain, to the point where you can challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.

  • Design and build agent-assisted workflows, and make judgement calls about where an agent should act, where it should advise, and where a human must stay in control.

  • Use AI coding tools, including Claude, as a core part of how you work. You delegate substantial work to them and you remain accountable for the quality, security, and correctness of everything you ship.

  • Work across boundaries with frontend engineers, product partners, and client-facing teams, and step outside your specialism when the problem demands it.

  • Give and take direct feedback, and raise the engineering bar around you.

 

What you’ll need to have done

  • Strong professional experience building and running backend systems in Kotlin, Java, or another JVM language.

  • Judgement in architecture and system design: a feel for what to build now, what to defer, and what will hurt in two years.

  • Evidence of shipping software that solved a real customer or business problem, ideally something you owned end to end.

  • A self-starting approach. You find the highest-value problem rather than waiting for a ticket.

  • Clear communication. You can hold the same conversation with an underwriter, an executive, and an engineer, and adjust for each.

  • Genuine appetite for problems with no known answer, and comfort working without a precedent to copy.

  • Confident, responsible use of AI coding tools, with a critical eye on their output.

  • Receptiveness to feedback. We give it directly and often, and we expect you to give it back.

 

Helpful, not required

  • Experience in insurance, underwriting, or another complex regulated domain. We will teach you the domain. We cannot teach curiosity about it.

  • Experience across both backend and frontend.

  • Experience building workflow, decision-support, or agent-assisted products.

  • Experience working directly with enterprise clients.

 

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

 

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your talent partner will be able to share more details about this.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

title: Senior Product Engineer (Software) (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Roger is the operating system for dental practices. We automate the work dental teams shouldn’t be doing by hand – from treatment plans to patient communication to revenue optimization – and we plug directly into the practice management systems (PMS) that German practices already run on. We’re early, well-funded, and moving fast.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Engineer who wants to own a product area end to end: understand the practice’s problem, decide what to build, ship it, run it, and improve it with real usage data. Not tickets. Outcomes.

We call the role Product Engineer on purpose. You work directly with product, design, and practices, and you’re accountable for whether what you built actually solves the problem – not just for whether the code merged.

What you’ll build
Everyone works across the whole product; people build deeper expertise in some areas, but who works on what can change quickly. Over a typical quarter you’ll touch things like:
• PMS integrations – connecting Roger to the practice management systems German practices run on, so our workflows sit on top of live practice data instead of beside it
• Treatment plans and cost estimates (HKP) – turning a manual, error-prone paper process into something a practice team gets right the first time
• Patient communication – recalls, reminders, and follow-ups that practices today handle by phone, fax, and sticky note
• Revenue and billing workflows – helping practices bill what they actually did, correctly and on time
• The Roger apps – web and Flutter clients that practice staff use all day, every day

Whatever your area, you’ll own it from the first conversation with a practice to the dashboard that tells you whether it worked.

What we expect
• Own outcomes, not tasks. You define scope, timelines, and success criteria for your area, and you align stakeholders around them
• Make technical decisions and stand behind them. Architecture, trade-offs, what to build versus buy – you decide, document why, and course-correct when the data says so
• Know the system, not just your service. Roger is one product. You keep enough context across PMS integrations, data model, and clients to make decisions that hold up outside your corner
• Raise the bar continuously. Testing, documentation, CI/CD, observability – you leave every area better than you found it
• Shape how we work with AI. Our tooling and practices are still evolving. You contribute to them actively rather than waiting for a playbook
• Enable others. Code reviews, knowledge sharing, pairing – a senior here makes the people around them better

How we work
AI-native engineering, honestly described. Most of us run several coding agents in parallel, all day. Writing code is no longer the bottleneck. Reviewing it, testing it, and deciding what not to ship is. So here’s what that actually means for you:
• You write specs and plans before you prompt. Skipping design thinking is where projects fail – not the AI
• You review agent output with the same rigor as any PR. If you can’t explain what a module does, it doesn’t ship
• You test relentlessly. A solid test suite is how you turn an unreliable agent into a reliable system
• Your fundamentals are strong enough to evaluate, correct, and improve whatever AI produces – architecture, security, performance
• You know the spectrum: when a throwaway prototype is fine and when full engineering discipline applies
• You expect to spend as much time reviewing and validating as writing. If that sounds like a downgrade, this isn’t the right team. If it sounds like leverage, read on

Patient data is not a detail. Roger handles health data (GDPR Art. 9) and sits inside practices bound by professional secrecy (§ 203 StGB). Data minimization, access control, EU processing, and a clear head about what may go to which model provider are part of the engineering bar here – not a compliance checkbox someone else owns.
Small team, short paths. You talk to practices, to product, and to the people who answer the phones for our customers. Decisions get made in a conversation, not a committee.

Who you are
• Senior-level, with significant experience shipping and operating production systems – you’ve been paged for your own code
• A track record of owning projects end to end: from a vague problem statement through delivery to production and iteration
• Used to working cross-functionally with product, design, data, and non-technical stakeholders – and comfortable talking to end users directly
• You think beyond your own code: business context, user needs, and product goals shape what you build
• You take ownership without waiting for instructions, make decisions under ambiguity, and escalate when it matters
• You communicate openly and clearly, in writing and in person, with technical and non-technical people alike
• Our stack is Ruby on Rails, Go, and Dart/Flutter. Deep experience in at least one of these helps; strong fundamentals matter more than any specific language
• Bonus, not required: experience in healthcare, dental, or another regulated domain; or with integrating into legacy on-premise systems

Location, language, and setup
• Location: You live in Germany and can be in our Berlin office regularly. The role is hybrid: 2–3 days a week on site, the rest remote
• German: Business-fluent German (C1 or better) is required. You’ll talk to practices, read PMS vendor documentation, and work with German regulatory and billing concepts daily. Our team language is English
• Eligibility: You already hold the right to work in Germany.
• Working hours: Full-time

Why Roger?
• The opportunity is absurd. A market worth billions that still runs on fax machines and phone tag
• Real leverage. You’ll be one of 6 engineers. Your area is yours – your decisions shape the product, not a committee’s
• Hard, interesting problems in a space most tech companies ignore: legacy integrations, regulated data, real-world workflows with real-world stakes

title: Senior Product Lifecycle Manager
descriptionHtml:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Program Management Team

Wayve’s Program Management team turns complex technical goals into coordinated delivery. Working closely with engineering, product, safety and validation teams, we align priorities, manage dependencies and bring clarity to ambiguous challenges. We combine technical depth with cross-functional leadership to help teams move faster, more predictably and with purpose—focusing on meaningful outcomes rather than process for its own sake.

As Senior Product Lifecycle Manager, you’ll connect Wayve’s product milestones to the detailed technical plans, system-level artefacts and readiness evidence needed to deliver them. You’ll lead complex, multi-team programmes from one milestone to the next, ensuring teams work from a shared, credible plan across our Level 2 and Level 4 products.

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Partner with engineering and product leads to translate product milestones into integrated cross-team schedules, priorities and delivery plans.

  • Review technical progress, backlog health, dependencies and system-level evidence to determine whether programmes are ready to move forward.

  • Identify technical risks and sequencing bottlenecks early, then drive the decisions and mitigation plans needed to protect delivery.

  • Facilitate difficult conversations around scope, resources and competing priorities, helping teams reach clear and practical decisions.

  • Adapt plans quickly as technical understanding, product priorities or delivery constraints change.

  • Communicate programme status, schedule changes, risks and decisions clearly and proactively across technical teams and senior stakeholders.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

  • Owning and maintaining integrated lifecycle plans for complex Level 2 and Level 4 product milestones, creating a clear source of truth across teams.

  • Managing cross-team dependencies and critical-path activities across engineering, product, safety, verification and validation.

  • Managing system-level artefacts throughout the product lifecycle, ensuring the right information and evidence are available at each milestone.

  • Establishing clear milestone-readiness criteria and using technical status, metrics and backlog data to support evidence-based delivery decisions.

  • Aligning programme scope, sequencing and resource decisions with Wayve’s strategic and commercial priorities.

  • Improving lifecycle-planning practices and tooling so teams can identify risk earlier, coordinate more effectively and deliver with greater predictability.

🙌 You should apply if:

  • You have 5+ years of experience leading complex, multi-team technical or product programmes, with responsibility for planning, execution and delivery across several engineering teams.

  • You bring a strong background in the automotive or autonomous-vehicle industry and understand the complexity of delivering integrated vehicle and software products.

  • You have the technical depth to work closely with engineers, evaluate complex system architectures and challenge delivery plans constructively—not simply track execution.

  • You think in systems, understanding how technical decisions, dependencies and changes in one area affect downstream teams and product outcomes.

  • You’re decisive under uncertainty and can make sound prioritisation and trade-off recommendations with incomplete or evolving information.

  • You have a strong track record of identifying delivery, technical and dependency risks early and driving them through to resolution.

  • You use metrics, technical evidence and backlog health to assess readiness and guide programme decisions.

  • You’re product-minded and outcome-focused, connecting delivery decisions to customer value and business impact rather than process completion alone.

  • You can facilitate challenging stakeholder conversations, resolve conflicting technical priorities and create alignment without relying on formal authority.

  • You communicate clearly in writing and in conversation, tailoring complex programme information for both technical and business audiences.

  • You’re proficient with Jira, Confluence and modern backlog, planning and programme-management tools.

  • Experience working in a safety-critical, regulated or complex multi-stakeholder environment would be valuable.

  • A programme-management qualification such as PMP, CAPM or PRINCE2 would be a plus.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

This is a full-time role based in our London office.

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes)

  • Competency Interviews (HM Call; 60 minutes)

  • Deep-dive technical interviews (Stakeholder Management, Delivery Use Case; 2 hours)

  • Final interview: mission & values alignment (45 minutes).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

title: Senior Product Manager - 12 Month FTC
descriptionHtml:
This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK. This is a 12 month FTC.

Role Summary

PLOS is a nonprofit Open Access publisher with an ambitious mission: to help transform research communication so that science can be shared, understood and used more effectively. We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Product team for a 12-month maternity cover contract. It's an interesting time to join us. 

Research publishing is changing rapidly. Researchers' expectations are changing. Technology is creating possibilities that didn't exist a few years ago. And at PLOS we're rethinking some of the services, systems and assumptions that have shaped scholarly publishing for decades. 

That means there are interesting product problems to solve - not just features to deliver. 

You'll take responsibility for a product area and work with designers, engineers and colleagues across PLOS to understand the problems that matter, work out where we can make the greatest difference and help the team learn its way towards good solutions. 

Although this is a fixed-term role, it isn't a caretaker role. You'll be joining active product teams working on significant problems and will have plenty of opportunity to shape what we do and how we do it. 

How we work 

We want our product teams to be curious, evidence-led and comfortable with uncertainty. 

We don't expect a Product Manager to arrive with all the answers. We do expect them to ask good questions. 

You'll use continuous discovery alongside delivery: spending time with users, looking at data, understanding the wider service, identifying assumptions and finding practical ways to test them. 

You'll help the team break large problems into smaller things we can learn from, rather than waiting until everything is known before we release something. 

And you'll make the team's thinking visible - explaining what we're trying to achieve, what we've learned, what we're uncertain about and why we're making the choices we are. 

Responsibilities

As a Senior Product Manager, you'll: 

  • Understand the problem. Build a deep understanding of our users, their needs and behaviours, as well as the organisational, operational and technical context surrounding them. 
  • Shape product direction. Work out where the greatest opportunities lie within your area and help translate PLOS's objectives into clear product outcomes and priorities. 
  • Practise continuous discovery. Work closely with design, engineering and others to explore problems, identify assumptions and regularly test ideas with users and through data. 
  • Turn uncertainty into learning. Frame hypotheses, design useful experiments and look for the smallest sensible way to learn whether we're heading in the right direction. 
  • Make good product decisions. Weigh evidence, impact, effort, risk and opportunity when deciding what to pursue - and what not to pursue. 
  • Measure whether things are getting better. Define useful measures of success and use qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand whether our work is having the intended effect. 
  • Work iteratively. Help the team deliver in small steps, learn from what happens and adapt rather than treating plans as fixed commitments. 
  • Communicate your thinking. Clearly explain problems, evidence, choices, trade-offs and learning to people with very different levels of technical and product knowledge. 
  • Create strong feedback loops. Use conversations, demos, reviews and other forums to get useful feedback early rather than presenting finished thinking late. 
  • Work as part of a team. Create the conditions in which designers, engineers and other specialists can contribute to product decisions rather than treating product management as something the PM does alone. 
  • Look beyond the product interface. Understand the wider service, including processes, systems and teams around it, and recognise when solving a user problem requires changing more than software. 

Experience and qualifications 

Essential 

  • Degree-level qualification or equivalent professional experience.  
  • At least three years' experience working as a Product Manager in a multidisciplinary digital product team, working closely with disciplines such as design, engineering, research and delivery. 
  • Experience using product discovery alongside delivery - for example, user research, data, experimentation and hypothesis testing - to understand problems and inform what a team should do next. 
  • Experience working with significant uncertainty or ambiguity: identifying what is known, what is assumed and what needs to be learned before making larger commitments. 
  • Experience taking complex problems and helping a team turn them into clear priorities, outcomes and practical next steps. 
  • Experience making product decisions using a combination of user evidence, data, organisational goals, technical constraints and product judgement. 
  • Experience communicating product thinking clearly to a wide range of people, including explaining evidence, uncertainty, trade-offs and why particular decisions have been made. 
  • Experience working collaboratively with people outside the immediate product team, particularly where different groups have different needs, incentives or perspectives. 

Particularly useful 

We'd be especially interested in candidates who have experience of one or more of the following: 

  • Working in an organisation going through significant product, digital or organisational transformation. 
  • Working in complex service environments where improving the user experience involves changes to technology, operations, policy or organisational processes - not simply changing an interface. 
  • Helping teams move towards more iterative, outcome-focused or evidence-led ways of working. 
  • Working in a mission-led, research, publishing, education, scientific or other knowledge-based organisation. 

Experience of scholarly publishing is useful but isn't required. 

What we're looking for in a Senior Product Manager 

For us, seniority isn't about having a larger backlog or knowing more product framework: it's about judgement. 

You'll be able to take a complex and uncertain problem, help people understand it, decide what we most need to learn, bring a team together around a sensible course of action and change that course when the evidence tells us to. 

You'll be comfortable making decisions without perfect information while being clear about the assumptions and risks involved. 

And you'll help the people around you think more clearly about the product - not simply tell them what to build. 

Working at PLOS 

You'll join PLOS's Product team and work collaboratively with colleagues across Digital and the wider organisation. 

The role has no direct line-management responsibility. 

The job is fully remote. Some flexibility to work across time zones and occasional national or international travel may be required. 

The base salary range we’ve established for these positions is (UK) £65,000 - £73,500. PLOS also offers a comprehensive benefits package summarized below. 

BENEFITS: 

  • Private medical insurance 
  • Life assurance 
  • Income protection  
  • Personal accident insurance 
  • Pension with up to 10% employer match 
  • 25 days holidays, market competitive Maternity and Paternity leave 
  • Birthday and three winter holidays days off 
  • 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year 
  • Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office

About PLOS 

Building on a strong legacy of pioneering innovation, PLOS continues to be a catalyst in open science, reimagining models to meet open science principles, removing barriers and promoting inclusion in knowledge creation and sharing, and publishing research outputs that enable everyone to learn from, reuse and build upon scientific knowledge.

Our work is supported by a highly skilled global in-house team, partnerships with local scholarly organizations, and the valued contributions of a diverse, international community of scientific researchers.

We’re committed to equal opportunity

We’re working to create a more equitable system of scientific knowledge and understanding. Removing barriers to inclusion and facilitating broad participation of voices is core to our success, inside and out. 

Beyond accepting distinct perspectives, we seek and support divergent backgrounds among our staff because we know differences strengthen our teams, our work, and our communities. We strongly encourage applicants of all identities to join us as we work towards a future where science is open to all, for all. 

Visit plos.org/careers to learn more.

To learn more about how PLOS protects your privacy, see our Employee Privacy Notice.

title: Senior Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
We are the platform turning browsing into shopping. We connect 200 million shoppers with deals they love while boosting local sales for hundreds of top retailers and brands.

We help consumers save time and money while making smart shopping decisions, and we support retailers and brands in engaging customers from online research to in-store purchases.

In 2024, Shopfully joined forces with the North American company Flipp, creating a global leader in the sector. Together, we reach 400 million households and serve over 1,000 top retailers and brands across 27 markets, including Europe, Canada, the USA, Latin America, and Australia.

Ready to spark your growth with us?

WHO WE LOOK FOR 🦄

Flipp + Shopfully’s Product team focuses on driving adoption and revenue of our products by identifying the biggest market opportunities, building the case for investing in them, and shipping solutions with engineering, all while representing the voice of our merchant customers.

About the role

The Senior Product Manager is a senior, commercially minded product leader who already understands digital advertising. This role requires a strong strategic thinker with good business sense and solid hands-on product skills who leads opportunity identification, builds decision-ready business cases, and works with engineering to ship.

You will work closely with Sales, Engineering, Data, and Marketing teams across markets to align on key business objectives. By combining market insight, customer feedback, and industry trends, you will make sure our products resonate with merchants and drive growth. We’re looking for someone who can ramp up quickly and contribute independently.

WHAT YOU WILL DO 🏄

Market Understanding and Opportunity Identification

  • Work with Product Marketing, Sales Engineering and customer-facing teams to understand customer needs and prioritize the opportunities that matter most.
  • Find the highest-leverage areas to invest in, and weigh customer demand against our resources, capabilities and strategic direction.
  • Turn complex questions into clear priorities. For example: how do we create more value for retail partners as their strategies move toward e-commerce? How do we find and build opportunities at scale as products launch in new markets?

Business Cases and Strategy

  • Build business cases that size opportunities, weigh revenue trade-offs, and structure a clear recommendation so leadership can make a decision.
  • Own your recommendations, and be ready to explain them and adapt them as you learn.
  • Lead the strategy for how our products differentiate from competitors in the market.
  • Partner with Sales and Finance on pricing and monetization so our offering stays cohesive.

Product Discovery and Delivery

  • Lead discovery with merchants, advertisers, and internal teams to define problems worth solving.
  • Prioritise ruthlessly, balancing revenue impact, effort, and strategic fit.
  • Work hands-on with engineering to define requirements and ship, from alpha and testing through broad launch.
  • Partner with Sales and Marketing on launch timing and readiness, and run retrospectives on past launches to improve future ones.

Alignment and Stakeholder Management

  • Generate cross-functional alignment (Engineering, Data, Sales, Marketing, Content) with a shared focus on goals and timing.
  • Work across markets and levels of seniority, including senior leadership, with confidence.
  • Track progress and impact of product initiatives and communicate results clearly.
  • Build relationships with industry analysts, partners, and customers, and represent Flipp + Shopfully at conferences and industry events where relevant.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED🪄

Must-haves

  • Digital advertising foundations: supply vs. demand, how exchanges, SSPs, and DSPs work, programmatic bidding, pricing models (CPM, CPC, CPV), and fill rate and yield. Ideally gained in ad tech, a retail media network, a publisher, or a marketplace.
  • Proven experience building business cases: sizing opportunities, weighing revenue trade-offs, and structuring recommendations for decisions.
  • High autonomy: you figure things out, own the outcome and don’t need close management.
  • Genuine excitement about using AI tools and rethinking how work gets done.
  • Hands-on product skills: discovery, prioritisation, and working with engineering to ship, not only strategy.
  • Stakeholder management, with the confidence to work across markets and levels of seniority.
  • A scrappy, curious and confident approach. You’re hungry to make an impact.

👉 At our company, we value diversity and actively encourage it — we believe a variety of perspectives and backgrounds makes us stronger. We focus on potential rather than on having a “perfect” CV. If this role excites you and you believe you could grow into it — even if you don’t tick every single box in the requirements — we’d love to hear from you!

NICE TO HAVE  🎆

  • Retail, CPG, or retail media background
  • Multi-market experience
  • Can speak Italian or German

LOCATION 🌐 

While we have offices in Milan, Berlin, Barcelona, you can benefit from our flexible hybrid model (full remote available), empowering you to work where you're most effective.

HOURS ⏰
Your manager and several partner teams are in North America, so you’ll need to be flexible about working some later hours, beyond a standard 9-5 CET.

WHAT YOU WILL FIND AT SHOPFULLY 🤗

🌎 An opportunity to thrive in a rapidly scaling multinational company

🕶️ A vibrant, informal, and inclusive work environment

🧠 We champion autonomy, flexibility, and a hybrid work model, empowering you to own your work

📚 Access to learning opportunities and regular feedback sessions

🍓 Enjoy our central, modern offices featuring fresh snacks, coffee (including vegan options!), and ergonomic setups

🎉 Engage in meaningful team events: offsites, happy hours, company parties and celebrations that unite us beyond daily tasks

💻We provide all the necessary equipment for you to work effectively and set up your workspace, wherever you are

🧰 Benefit from additional country-specific advantages based on local contracts and practices

WHO WE ARE 💜 

We’re a team of 450 people (and counting!), from 30 different nationalities. We’re on a mission to innovate, and we believe the key to that is seeing the world through a variety of perspectives. That’s why building a more diverse team, as well as bringing in even more talent, is so important for us.

TO FEEL AT HOME 🛋️ IN SHOPFULLY YOU NEED 🎯

  • Progress Over Perfection: We move forward. Always. In a fast-moving world, speed with purpose beats certainty without action. Momentum matters—not for its own sake, but because it drives results.
  • Clarity Through Transparency: We bring each other along. We work in teams, not silos. Transparency gives context, and context enables action. That means we share decisions early, publish work in progress, and document outcomes so others can learn, move faster, and build better.
  • Learn Loudly: We grow by doing and by daring. Big bets unlock big breakthroughs. But real innovation demands risk, and risk always carries the possibility of failure. That’s not a flaw. It’s the price of ambition.
  • Challenge with Empathy: We speak up, even when it’s hard—because candor shows care, and leads to better outcomes. Listening deeply is how we grow. Disagreeing openly is how we build trust.

Always Build Better: We are builders—of products, systems, and ideas. But more than that, we are builders of better. Better has no finish line. It’s a mindset.

Our Total Rewards philosophy is to ensure that you are rewarded for impact, take part in accelerated career growth, thrive with highly flexible benefits, and are empowered to do your best work in a remote-first environment.
