title: Staff Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Hi 👋 I’m Rich Ashworth, Director of Engineering at hyperexponential.

I lead the Model Authoring value stream that owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models. An actuary might start with an Excel rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved, and is pricing live business. Our job is to turn that into an exceptional user experience and make every step of that credible enough to trust.

I'm hiring a Staff Product Engineer to help set our technical direction and build the next version of our products. It's an individual contributor role, but influence is a huge part of it: the standards the pods work to, the shared enablers underneath the product, and the interfaces where our problems meet other teams'. You’ll be hands-on where the risk is highest.

There's no established playbook for any of this, but there’s an incredible opportunity in front of us. If this sounds like a role that would excite you, I'd love to hear from you.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Model Authoring team

Model Authoring owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models: the model developer experience and our actuarial agent. An actuary might start with an Excel-based rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved and is pricing live business. Our job is to make every step of that credible enough to trust. The team is distributed across our Warsaw and London offices.

As the Staff Product Engineer, you will help set the team's technical direction. This is an individual contributor role, but influence is a large part of it: you'll help define the standards the team works to, raise the technical bar across pods, and own the interfaces where our problems meet those of teams elsewhere in Technology. You'll be expected to move fast and start shaping technical conversations early. We work in an AI-native way, and you'll help define and evolve what that means here.

What you'll be doing

  • Establish a set of engineering standards across the Model Authoring pods. The standards are documented and actively referenced in code review, with new pod work conforming by default.

  • Set and own the technical direction for the team's shared enablers, including how we represent and persist models, the model registry, secure context access, and shared agentic infrastructure.

  • Establish the technical interfaces between Model Authoring and other parts of the business. Dependencies with other teams are agreed, documented, and progressing without needing to be brokered by someone else.

  • Work hands-on on the hardest problems in the stream. This is not an advisory role: we would expect you in the code where the risk is highest.

  • Help define how we work in an AI-native way. Which parts of model development and of our own engineering we hand to agents, what stays human, and what evidence we need before trusting either.

  • Visibly lift the engineers around you. You're sought out for design input across pods, and there's at least one engineer whose growth is clearly attributable to your support.

What you'll need to have done

  • Worked in an AI-native environment, and genuinely want to keep doing so. You've used AI or agentic tools in your own engineering workflow, introduced or experimented with them, and have a real view on what's worked and what hasn't.

  • Been product-focused rather than purely technical. You understand who your users are, where their pain points are, and how your technical decisions connect to commercial outcomes.

  • Set technical direction while navigating genuine ambiguity. A proven track record of owning architecture in a domain with no established playbook, and making clear calls on imperfect information rather than deferring them.

  • Owned a significant technical challenge or service end to end, with the depth to walk through it in detail - the trade-offs, the contracts, the things you'd do differently.

  • Influenced across teams. You can hold a position under challenge, genuinely listen to pushback, and persuade others - not just present your own view and hope it lands.

  • Worked effectively across distributed teams - this role spans our Warsaw and London offices, so you'll need to be comfortable building relationships and influence across both.

You're unlikely to thrive here if

  • You'd rather focus purely on the technical problem than get close to users, customer pain points, and the commercial implications of what you build.

  • You're not comfortable setting technical direction in ambiguity, or you'd rather wait for an established playbook than make a call on imperfect information.

  • You're not excited about helping define what the future of software engineering looks like and are prepared to embrace tooling and new ways of working to support this.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

  1. Initial call with our Talent team

  2. Hiring Manager Interview

  3. Skills Assessment & follow-up interview

  4. Values Interview

  5. Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. All applicant data will be processed in accordance with data protection regulations and our privacy policy.

You combine sharp product judgment with hands-on discovery skills, and you measure yourself on commercial impact, not output.

We're not looking for someone to write specs and manage a backlog. We want someone who helps us think better, decide better, and ship better. The goal isn't more process, it's higher quality decisions made faster.

You will work directly with our Head of Product, CTO, founders and senior engineers to shape what we build and why.

What you will own

You will not hand anything over. You will own the bet from first insight to shipped impact.

  • Own discovery through delivery for our most important product bets, from early ambiguity to validated direction to launched product

  • Work directly with engineers and founders from the start of any initiative as the accountable product owner, not a coordinator

  • Frame the problem, define the hypothesis, and choose the fastest route to signal: interviews, prototypes, fake doors, experiments, or just shipping and measuring

  • Translate messy qualitative and quantitative signals into clear product direction, then drive that direction through to execution

  • Set success metrics, make the call on when there's enough signal to build, and own the outcome either way

  • Embed structured learning loops into how we operate so insight compounds over time

  • Raise the bar of product thinking across the team: coach others, introduce lightweight frameworks, and get the whole company closer to customers

Who you are

You are a full-stack product thinker.

  • Outcome owner: You connect user behaviour to funnels, retention, and revenue. You think in bets and expected value, not feature lists, and you hold yourself accountable to results.

  • Discovery-strong: Genuinely fluent across qualitative research, behavioural insight, and experimentation. You generate strong signal quickly and pick the right method for the decision at hand, rather than outsourcing the thinking.

  • Engineering partner: You work shoulder to shoulder with engineers, translating insight into crisp problem framing and practical tradeoffs. Engineers want to work with you because you make the work clearer, not slower.

  • Decision oriented: You know when there's enough signal to move. You sharpen hypotheses, clarify thinking, and make confident calls under uncertainty. You'd rather ship and learn than perfect and wait.

  • Force multiplier: Your impact shows up in how the whole team operates. You build repeatable systems for discovery and decision-making that outlast any single project.

The Role

You will be the senior product voice on our most important initiatives, working directly with the Head of Product, CPGO, founders, and senior engineers. This is not a support function. You will be embedded in high impact work from day one, with real authority over what we build and why.

You will operate at speed. We care about generating signal quickly, making informed decisions, and shipping fast. You are comfortable working with imperfect information and tightening your thinking as you go.

You will move fluidly across the full product lifecycle. Some weeks you will be deep in user interviews or pressure testing a major bet, other weeks you will be in the detail with engineers getting something over the line.

You will have significant autonomy. We expect strong judgment, clear communication, and ownership of outcomes.

If there are specific tools you believe are critical to moving faster or generating better signal, we will support that. We want you to design the right setup, not work around constraints.

Why Fyxer?

We are intentional about our team. We believe a small, exceptional team working with extreme focus will always outperform a large, bloated organization.

  • Autonomy: We hire people who want ownership and then we actually give it to them.

  • Velocity: You will be fast-tracked into senior responsibilities far earlier than at a traditional company.

  • Scale: We are on track to hit $100M in revenue by the end of 2026. This is a rare opportunity to join a high-growth rocket ship at the foundational stage.

title: Staff QA Automation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

The Role

We're hiring a Staff QA Automation Engineer to help shape how quality engineering works across tem.

QA sits inside Platform, a central team that builds the tooling and standards the rest of engineering runs on. You'll design the frameworks and practices that let them test well themselves, and scale into the future. As we scale, you'll lead and develop scripts that equip engineering teams with the automation and standards to own quality themselves.

The product is built on a microservice architecture that brings real complexity to testing. You'll own the quality engineering approach as the organisation scales — setting the standards, building the tooling, and driving adoption across engineering.

What you'll work on:

  • A risk-aware CI testing standard any team can run: a dependency model that drives test selection and breaking-change detection, so most PRs get a fast targeted run with a clear confidence signal at the point of change.

  • Unit, integration, and contract testing standards with an observability layer that keeps pipelines honest and not flaky. Proven through reference test suites in real service repos, not a QA-authored checklist.

  • The quality side of canary releases: working with the wider Platform team to define automated pass/fail analysis against production traffic so deployments promote or roll back without manual sign-off.

  • AI in the quality pipeline: LLM-based change-risk classification, targeted mutation testing, test generation, and self-healing checks. We already use LLM tooling across QA and want someone to take it further.

You report to Bartek Kucharski (QA). Specialist individual contributor, no direct reports.

Requirements

Must haves:

  • Expertise in test automation frameworks including pytest, Playwright, Selenium, and API testing or similar.

  • Experience architecting and maintaining test automation frameworks and tooling used across a wider engineering organisation.

  • Deep knowledge of testing across microservice or distributed systems, including API-level automation, CI/CD integration, and service-level testing strategies.

  • Experience leading innovation and PoCs in testing, particularly AI-led regression optimisation and change-risk analysis.

  • Strong collaboration and delivery focus across multi-project environments and distributed teams.

  • Contract testing or consumer/provider verification (Pact, OpenAPI schema validation, or similar).

  • AWS infrastructure experience (Lambda, GitHub Actions self-hosted runners, deployment tooling).

Nice to have:

  • Progressive deployment experience: canary releases, feature flags, automated rollback from production signals.

  • Mutation testing, whether traditional tooling or LLM-based.

  • Test-data management and environment-isolation strategy in shared environments.

  • Experience in a regulated or high-stakes domain (energy, fintech, payments).

Benefits & Perks

  • Our current band for this role is £104,000 or equivalent in local currency.

    • We pay against a clear benchmark for your role and level. No fixed once- or twice-a-year cycle - pay moves when the evidence for it does.

  • Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

  • 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off.

  • Remote first within the UK and Europe.

  • Home working and wellbeing budgets.

Interview Process

We move fast. Most processes take 2 to 3 weeks from first chat to offer. If you need us to adapt anything, let us know.

  • Intro call with Talent, 30 minutes.

  • Behavioural Interview with the Hiring Manager, 60 minutes.

  • Skills interview with cross-functional leaders, 90 - 120min minutes, including a practical exercise on framework design and AI-in-test.

  • Bar Raiser interview with leadership stakeholders, 45 minutes.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

descriptionHtml:
Location: Bristol or London, UK (hybrid, three days a week in the office)

Level: Staff Engineer TL2

Team: Release Engineering

Salary: £97,600 - £125,000 + discretionary bonus

Contract: Permanent

Reporting To: Software Engineering manager

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.


About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.


What you'll do

As a Staff Release Engineer, you will set the technical strategy and global architecture for Kaluza’s continuous integration, delivery, and automated release ecosystems. You will empower our entire engineering organization to deploy high-quality software safely, frequently, and with minimal friction.

  • Architect Release Ecosystems: Lead the high-level design and long-term roadmap definition for building, scaling, and governing the systems and practices that reliably move software from source to production through centralized developer tooling across all Kaluza engineering domains. 

  • Drive Engineering Productivity & SRE Practices: Strategize and embed automated deployment & release mechanisms, testing frameworks, Site Reliability Engineering principles and AI tooling  to drastically reduce toil and accelerate software delivery speed and safety across the organization. 

  • Establish Global Standards & Metrics: Lead the definition, continuous improvement and enforcement of company-wide DevOps practices, standards, and frameworks such as DORA for compliance and auditability but also to measure and target improvements that elevate engineering productivity.

  • Orchestrate Complex Infrastructure Tooling: Own the strategy for deployment platforms and infrastructure-as-code tools (e.g., GitHub Actions, Terraform, AWS, Kubernetes, ArgoCD), ensuring multi-tenant SaaS environments are secure, scalable, and efficient.

  • Mentor & Upskill: Provide technical ownership, guidance, and mentorship to engineers across Kaluza, fostering deep expertise in automated delivery, developer experience, and modern release engineering practices including AI enablement.

  • Hands-off & Hands-on Technical Leadership: Drive platform-wide release architecture through audits and strategic design, while retaining the capability to build high-impact proofs-of-concept for mission-critical release infrastructure.


What you'll bring

Ideally you'll have:

  • Strategic CI/CD & Release Architect: Deep experience architecting, scaling, and maintaining enterprise-grade CI/CD frameworks, release pipelines, and internal developer platforms in cloud-native environments.

  • DevOps & DORA Expert: Comprehensive mastery of DevOps practices, software development lifecycle (SDLC) automation, and practical application of DORA metrics to drive measurable engineering productivity.

  • Technical Mentor & Leader: A proven track record of upskilling senior engineering talent, driving technical strategy, and establishing consensus across multi-disciplinary engineering domains.

  • Infrastructure & Automation Mastery: Extensive hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), container orchestration (Kubernetes, ArgoCD), and workflow automation (GitHub Actions). Experience of GitHub Enterprise administration and GitHubAsCode experience would be a bonus.

  • Developer-Centric & Data-Driven: Strong customer obsession—viewing developers as your primary customers—paired with data-driven decision-making to optimize developer experience and eliminate toil.

What will set you apart:

  • LLM Integration Experience: Hands-on experience integrating large language models into production applications or developer workflows, whether via APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock) or open-source models, with a solid understanding of prompt engineering, context management, and evaluation.

  • AI Tooling Advocacy: A track record of introducing AI-assisted developer tooling and workflows (e.g., Copilot, Cursor, Claude, or similar) into a team and upskilling colleagues, not just using it personally.

  • Enterprise Release Strategy & Domain Exposure: Experience designing, building, and governance-proofing release architectures specifically for enterprise clients or highly regulated global platforms, ideally with direct domain exposure to energy technology, smart device orchestration, billing SaaS platforms, or high-throughput IoT platforms.


Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.


Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app


Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

title: Staff Security Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Build security platforms, not security processes

We are looking for a Staff Security Engineer to strengthen the security of our products, data and engineering platform.

This is a highly technical and hands-on role. You will work closely with Engineering teams to continuously harden our systems while helping design the next generation of our security architecture.

You will operate across two horizons:

  • Strengthen security today: continuously harden our applications, access controls and data-protection mechanisms against evolving threats.

  • Build the privacy architecture of tomorrow: move beyond traditional perimeter and access-control security by designing systems where sensitive data is cryptographically isolated, minimally exposed, and increasingly usable without being directly revealed.

The ultimate objective is not simply to make Swile harder to breach. It is to make a breach increasingly uninteresting, because there is less usable data available to steal.


What you will do

We want Security Engineering to create capabilities that scale across hundreds of engineers.

You will:

  • Identify and reduce high-impact security risks across our applications, APIs and internal tools.

  • Strengthen authentication, authorization and access controls.

  • Improve the protection of sensitive and personal data.

  • Design controls that limit the blast radius of compromised accounts, services or infrastructure.

  • Improve security monitoring, auditability and detection of suspicious access patterns.

  • Perform threat modelling and targeted security reviews.

  • Build reusable security capabilities directly into our engineering platform and development lifecycle.

  • Contribute to long-term architectures around data isolation, encryption, tokenisation and privacy-preserving systems.

  • Partner with engineering teams to address systemic security risks rather than individual findings.

    • Where possible, a security requirement should become code rather than documentation.


What we are looking for

You are first and foremost a strong engineer.

You have significant experience building or securing production software and distributed systems. You are comfortable reading and writing production code, designing systems and working directly with Engineering teams.

You have deep security engineering expertise and strong experience in several of the following areas:

  • Application and Product Security

  • API Security

  • IAM, authentication and authorization

  • OAuth2 / OIDC, WebAuthn / FIDO2

  • RBAC / ABAC and privilege management

  • Cloud security

  • Cryptography, KMS / HSM and envelope encryption

  • Tokenisation and secrets management

  • Data Security and Privacy Engineering

  • Threat modelling and secure software architecture

  • Security monitoring and detection

    • Stronger attacker mindset

    You naturally ask:

  • What happens if this employee becomes malicious?

  • What happens if this backend is compromised?

  • What happens if someone dumps this database?

  • Can this endpoint be called directly?

  • How much data can one account access before we notice?

  • Where else does this information get replicated?

  • Why do we have this data at all?

    • You think in terms of attack paths, blast radius and least privilege, not just compliance requirements.

    Pragmatism

    You know that security engineering is a prioritisation problem.

    You can distinguish between:

  • something that needs to be fixed this week;

  • something that requires an architectural redesign;

  • something cryptographically elegant but operationally unnecessary.

    • You are comfortable deploying simple, high-impact controls quickly while designing stronger long-term foundations.

    What would make you stand out

    Experience with:

  • large-scale SaaS or fintech platforms;

  • highly sensitive or regulated data;

  • multi-tenant architectures;

  • insider risk or data-loss prevention;

  • advanced cryptographic or privacy-enhancing technologies.

    • What success looks like

  • Sensitive data is exposed to fewer systems and people.

  • Access to sensitive resources is increasingly scoped, attributable and auditable.

  • Compromising a single account or service has a limited blast radius.

  • Security controls are increasingly enforced by the platform rather than by process.

  • Product teams can build secure systems faster and with less friction.

    • What this role is not

    This is not primarily a GRC, SOC, compliance, policy-writing or penetration-testing role.

    Those disciplines are important, but this role exists to change how our products and systems are engineered.

    We expect this person to design systems, write code, influence architecture and ship security capabilities into production.


    Localization of this position
    This position can be based at our offices in Paris, Toulouse, or Montpellier on a flex-remote basis.

title: Staff Security Operations Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

We're looking for a Staff Security Operations Engineer to join our Cybersecurity team at Pleo. In this role, you'll define and deliver the SecOps roadmap, building the detection, response, and investigation capability that protects a fast-growing fintech. If you're excited about owning a security operations function end to end, from framework-based strategy through to the code that makes it run, then this is the opportunity for you!

 

Who you'll be working with and reporting to

You'll report to our VP of Fraud & Security and work closely with Fraud, DevSecOps, Engineering, and Risk & Compliance. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to protecting Pleo's customers and their money. You'll also have the chance to partner with teams across the organisation and to bring less experienced security engineers up with you as the function matures.

 

What you'll be doing

As a Staff Security Operations Engineer, you will:

  • Build and own a structured SecOps roadmap grounded in well-known frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, and CIS benchmarks.

  • Lead security investigations and digital forensics, from suspicious traffic through to full incident response, and bring the findings back into how we detect and prevent.

  • Design, tune, and scale our SIEM and logging pipeline through standardized log ingestion across services so signal isn't lost in the noise.

  • Strengthen our perimeter and authentication posture, including WAF configuration, authorisation tuning, and monitoring for suspicious traffic.

  • Protect sensitive data through DLP controls, and make sure the coverage matches where the data actually lives.

  • Improve our on-call rotation for the team, defining the alerting, escalation paths, and response SLAs that make it work.

  • Automate detection and response workflows, using code and AI to reduce manual toil and shorten time to resolution.

  • Reduce SecOps-attributed risk identified through compliance gaps, and collect the evidence that demonstrates it.

  • Build dashboards and reporting that give the team and leadership real visibility into response times, coverage, and risk reduction.

  • Work cross-functionally with engineers who don't have a security background, translating threat models into changes they can actually ship.

 

What you bring

You'll thrive in this role if you have:

  • 10+ years of experience in security operations, incident response, or a closely related discipline, with a proven track record of materialised risk reduction through monetary impact, incidents contained, forensics that changed outcomes.

  • A strong development and engineering background. You are comfortable writing the automation, not just specifying it.

  • Hands-on SOC and SIEM management experience, including detection engineering and log pipeline design.

  • Experience in scale-up environments, where you've built capability rather than inherited a mature one.

  • A strong understanding of cloud architectures as we use AWS. With part of our estate on GCP and how infrastructure decisions shape detection and response.

  • Demonstrated experience using AI and/or coding automation to get security controls built, implemented, and operating in practice.

  • Fintech, payments, fraud, or trust & safety experience is a real advantage, as is exposure to highly regulated environments.

  • Backgrounds that tend to do well here: incident response, IR management, SOC engineering, security engineering, DevSecOps, red or blue team.

 

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You want a large blast radius. We have high-impact projects where the outcome shows up in real business metrics, at a pre-IPO company.

title: Staff / Senior Product Manager, Payments
descriptionHtml:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the Role

As a Senior / Staff Product Manager, you will play a defining role in shaping the future of global money movement, embedded commerce, and unified payment acceptance at Airwallex. Operating at the intersection of core clearing/settlement infrastructure, merchant-facing experiences, and developer-first toolkits, you will own the end-to-end product lifecycle—from long-term strategy and architectural design to global roadmap execution.

In this role, you will bridge our online payments-for-platforms suite (enabling marketplaces and SaaS platforms to collect, route, and embed payments) with next-generation in-person commerce (smart POS, SoftPOS, hardware/software integrations, and loyalty engines). You will lead cross-functional teams to modernise omnichannel workflows, scale coverage across international markets, and deploy AI-native capabilities that remove operational friction for global merchants.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the vision, roadmap, and delivery plans for Airwallex’s platform payments and in-person commerce solutions, expanding our reach across key verticals, marketplaces, and global geographies.

  • Architect seamless integrations connecting POS terminal workflows and embedded platform checkouts directly to core clearing, ledgering, and multi-currency settlement engines—optimising for processing speed, fee netting, and dynamic routing.

  • Build developer-first APIs, unified commerce SDKs, and intuitive terminal management systems (TMS) that drastically reduce integration overhead for marketplaces, platforms, and third-party software vendors.

  • Pioneer AI workflows and autonomous agents across merchant onboarding, automated terminal setup, dispute/risk management, transaction reconciliation, and proactive loyalty/reward engine optimisations.

  • Expand capabilities around alternative payment methods (APMs), card acquiring, and integrated loyalty redemption loops to help platforms monetize payments and retain underlying sellers.

  • Ensure high-availability infrastructure (including offline POS processing resilience) while delivering tooling to help merchants satisfy regulatory mandates (PCI-DSS, EMV, PSD3/local frameworks) and manage platform risk.

  • Partner closely with Engineering, Hardware/Firmware, Commercial, Legal/Compliance, and Operations teams to build scalable feedback loops and launch high-impact products from concept to global scale.

Who You Are

Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years of product management experience building high-scale, mission-critical platform products in fintech, payments, or commerce infrastructure (Staff-level scope).

  • Hands-on domain expertise in card acquiring, embedded finance/platform payment models (marketplaces, payfac-like setups), or card-present ecosystems (POS/SoftPOS, EMV/NFC standards, terminal management).

  • Proven ability to engage deeply with engineering on complex architectural discussions covering API design, distributed ledgers, high-throughput transaction processing, and hardware/software interfaces.

  • Exceptional analytical rigor with a track record of structuring complex ecosystem workflows, leveraging data to drive strategic trade-offs, and solving ambiguous problems.

  • High agency, persistence, and an entrepreneurial bias for action—capable of executing fast and driving complex initiatives to completion in a high-growth environment.

  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills; proven success influencing cross-functional teams and executive stakeholders across diverse international regions.

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher with strong academic performance, preferably with coursework in Computer Science, Engineering, or quantitative disciplines.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience designing or scaling developer-first payment APIs, unified commerce SDKs, or multi-sided platform architectures.

  • Hands-on exposure to deploying Generative AI, agentic workflows, or automated intelligence in fintech operations, transaction reconciliation, or onboarding.

  • Working familiarity with international card networks, alternative payment methods (APMs), cross-border settlement rails, and regional regulatory frameworks (UK/EU, APAC, or Americas).

All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

descriptionHtml:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

Role:

System Software builds the software that runs IonQ's quantum computers: the runtime, orchestration, quantum tools, controllers and transport software that sit between the Quantum Operating System and the hardware. It is where a next-generation system either comes together or doesn't.

We're hiring a Staff Technical Programme Manager to lead delivery across this stack. You'll report to the Group Program Manager, Software in our Programme Management Office and be matrixed to the VP, Software for day-to-day work.

You'll work across five engineering teams (runtime, orchestration, quantum tools, controllers and transport) and the interfaces between them and their cross-functional stakeholders, serving several next-generation system programmes at once, with hardware being co-developed alongside the software and teams in both Oxford and the US. Those programmes draw on the same engineers, so the central problem of this role is making sure that capacity is spent by decision, not by default.

We run a centralised PMO model. This role will not own engineering headcount or define product but it will make the programme around those things run. It carries real ownership of delivery: the plan, the trade-offs put in front of decision-makers, and the honesty of the status. In this role you will interface with everyone from technical software engineers to a wide range of the most senior stakeholders. You will also coordinate with your fellow programme managers, across Science, Infrastructure and broader Software teams, making sure all plans are shared and coordinated, rather than operating in silos.

Turning a research-grade quantum system into a dependable product is a problem nobody has finished solving, and the delivery standard you'll work within is being built now. If writing the first version of the plan sounds like the interesting part, we should talk.

Responsibilities:

In this role you will own the end-to-end delivery of the Systems Software roadmap across several concurrent programmes including managing dependencies between hardware, science and systems integration teams. You will partner closely with engineering leadership, the engineering teams run the day to day planning and boards, you will provide the direction that creates incremental milestones that ship.

You will identify risks and blockers early and work with the teams to resolve them. You will also run intake and triage, so requests reach the right team with the right priority and engineers can stay focused on planned work.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Make contention visible: when two programmes need the same team in the same quarter, bring it to the right decision-maker with the options and a recommendation before it becomes a slip.

  • Keep the systems of record honest. Requirements, plans, schedules and Jira drift apart; you'll close the gap and automate the checking.

  • Make invisible work visible: on-call load, sustaining work and technical debt tracked as rigorously as feature delivery.

  • Surface risks early, before you have a full solution or complete alignment. We'd rather hear it messy and on time.

  • Run intake and triage so requests reach the right team, with priority set by the people who own it, and engineers stay on planned work.

  • Work hand in hand with the Quantum Systems Infrastructure and Science TPMs in Oxford and the Software TPMs in the US: shared processes where teams meet, and no duplicated ceremonies, boards or reports.

  • Write concise, plain-English status on progress, risks and decisions for programme directors, engineering leaders and senior leadership.

  • Help shape how IonQ runs software delivery across sites, working with the Group Program Manager, Software on the shared delivery standard.

Requirements:

You will have significant experience running technical programmes across several software teams, ideally in systems, embedded, compiler or platform software. You can discuss scope and trade-offs directly with engineering leads, read and reason about code, and re-plan when a timeline is no longer realistic. You will have a track record of leading teams through genuine ambiguity, writing the first version of the plan when there isn't one, not just executing a defined one.

You can break broad problems down into specific, assignable actions, and you have designed a team's operating cadence before. No quantum background is needed. Experience of software that works closely with hardware, for example in labs, robotics, aerospace or scientific instruments, would be beneficial.

You’d be a great fit with:

  • A habit of turning diffuse problems into specific, minimal, assignable asks.

  • Technical fluency to engage engineering leads directly on scope and trade-offs, and comfort reading and reasoning about code.

  • Willingness to re-baseline against reality rather than defend dates that have stopped being true, and the judgement to tell a target that motivates from one that just generates fiction.

  • Experience with software that works closely with hardware: labs, robotics, aerospace, scientific instruments or similar.

  • A chase-without-nagging, escalate-without-drama style, and a clear sense of the difference between a risk and a noise.

  • AI as a core part of how you work, for example agent-driven tracking, reconciliation or reporting.

  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication with both technical and senior stakeholders.

Additional desirable skills include capacity and staffing modelling, designing operating cadences and experience leading work across sites and time zones. Experience working with programmes and systems such as Jira, Confluence and GitHub, with a preference for lightweight processes, is also helpful.

Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment.

title: Stage 3 Mois - 35H - Conseiller De Vente (H/F) - Galeries Lafayette Paris
locations: Grands Magasins, Paris, Île de France
descriptionHtml:
LA MAISON Jacquemus a été fondé par Simon Porte Jacquemus en 2009 à Paris, en France. Dédiée à la mémoire de la mère du créateur, la marque puise son inspiration dans une passion pour la culture. Les collections femme et homme font référence à l’art de vivre à la française et aux gestes universels de beauté, intégrant des influences allant de la photographie d'art aux arts décoratifs, en passant par le cinéma, la peinture et la sculpture. Au fil des années, Jacquemus a mis en scène ses défilés dans des lieux uniques et inattendus, notamment une piscine parisienne, le Musée Picasso, un champ de lavande en Provence, un champ de blé aux abords de Paris, un marais salant en Camargue et une plage à Hawaï. Plus récemment, la marque a investi des lieux tels que le canal du Château de Versailles (Le Chouchou), la Fondation Maeght (Les Sculptures), la Casa Malaparte (La Casa) et l’appartement parisien d’Auguste Perret (La Croisière). Basé dans le 8ᵉ arrondissement de Paris, Jacquemus est une maison de mode indépendante comptant plus de 300 employés. Réputée pour sa forte présence numérique et son expansion internationale, la marque a développé des expériences de vente innovantes à travers le monde avant d’ouvrir son premier flagship permanent au 58 Avenue Montaigne à Paris en 2022. Depuis, des boutiques ont été ouvertes à New York (SoHo) et Londres (New Bond Street) et Dubai. VOTRE RÔLE En tant que Conseiller(ère) de vente, vous serez ambassadeur / ambassadrice de la Maison et vous jouerez un rôle essentiel afin d’offrir à chaque client une expérience unique dans le respect et l’engagement de la Maison Jacquemus. Vous vous efforcerez de découvrir la personnalité de vos clients et d'identifier leurs désirs, tout en leur faisant découvrir l’ADN de la Maison et tous les univers produits. VOS MISSIONS · Participer activement au développement du chiffre d’affaires en accompagnant l’équipe dans l’atteinte des objectifs du point de vente. · Accueillir et conseiller nos clients pour leur offrir une expérience exceptionnelle. · Découvrir et partager votre expertise sur nos produits auprès des clients. · Faire preuve de proactivité en suggérant des produits complémentaires. · Contribuer à la fidélisation de notre clientèle en développant des relations privilégiées. · Assurer la bonne tenue du point de vente en collaboration avec l’équipe. · Participer aux missions opérationnelles : Visual merchandising, réassort, gestion des stocks, SAV. · Appliquer et respecter les procédures internes et guidelines. · Représenter l’esprit Jacquemus à travers votre créativité et votre sens de l’excellence. PROFIL · Étudiant(e) en école de commerce, de mode ou de management, avec une forte sensibilité pour l’univers de la mode et du luxe. · Première expérience en vente ou relation client appréciée. · Excellentes capacités de communication et sens du service client. · Enthousiaste, curieux(se) et doté(e) d’un esprit d’initiative. · Adaptable et proactif(ve), avec un fort esprit d’équipe. · Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, une troisième langue serait un plus. STAGE À POURVOIR A PARTIR DE NOVEMBRE

title: Stage - Account Executive: Gestion locative
descriptionHtml:
En rejoignant l’équipe Sales de Matera, tu auras l’opportunité d’échanger chaque jour avec des propriétaires bailleurs aux profils et aux besoins très différents!

Nos prospects peuvent aussi bien être des propriétaires qui mettent leur premier appartement en location que des bailleurs possédant plusieurs biens, déjà autonomes ou à la recherche d’un accompagnement plus complet. Notre rôle est de comprendre leur situation, de leur présenter la solution la plus adaptée et de les convaincre de confier la gestion de leur bien à Matera.

En tant que stagiaire Account Executive, tu seras formé·e aux différentes étapes du cycle de vente : découverte des besoins, présentation de notre offre, réponse aux premières objections et suivi des prospects jusqu’à leur souscription, en binôme avec nos commerciaux et sous la responsabilité de ton ou ta manager.

Tes missions en soutien de l’équipe Sales

En binôme avec nos commerciaux et sous la responsabilité de ton ou ta manager, tu seras formé·e progressivement au métier d’Account Executive.

  • Participer aux rendez-vous commerciaux : préparer et assister aux démos organisées par l’équipe SDR, puis prendre progressivement en charge certaines parties des échanges ;

  • Comprendre les besoins : échanger avec les propriétaires bailleurs pour identifier leur situation, leurs attentes et les difficultés rencontrées dans la gestion de leurs biens ;

  • Présenter notre offre : apprendre à présenter la solution de gestion locative Matera et à répondre aux premières questions des prospects avec l’appui de l’équipe ;

  • Accompagner le suivi commercial : contribuer aux relances, à la formalisation des prochaines étapes et au suivi des dossiers jusqu’à leur souscription ;

  • Découvrir nos outils Sales : participer à la tenue à jour de notre CRM HubSpot et appliquer les bonnes pratiques de suivi ;

  • Contribuer à l’amélioration continue : faire remonter les retours des prospects et proposer des idées pour améliorer notre discours, nos supports et nos processus commerciaux.

Ton parcours d’intégration et d’apprentissage

  • Deux semaines d’immersion : découverte de Matera, de nos métiers, de nos équipes et des enjeux de la gestion locative ;

  • Intégration à la Sales Academy : formations sur notre offre, la découverte client, les méthodes de vente et le traitement des objections ;

  • Accompagnement progressif : observation des premiers rendez-vous, participation en binôme, puis prise en charge de certaines étapes selon ta progression ;

  • Suivi régulier : échanges hebdomadaires avec ton ou ta manager pour accompagner ta montée en compétences et lever tes éventuels blocages ;

  • Découverte du cycle de vente : tu pourras progressivement participer aux différentes étapes du parcours commercial, toujours avec l’appui de l’équipe.

Les avantages

  • Salaire : 1 000 € (Césure) - 1 200€ (fin d’études de master) + une variable selon l’atteinte de tes objectifs,

  • Une forte montée en compétences sur les métiers Sales, la relation client et le secteur immobilier,

  • Poursuite possible en CDI,

  • Une demi-journée de congé par mois,

  • Un ordinateur et équipements te seront fournis,

  • Carte ticket restaurant Swile,

  • Abonnement à Gymlib,

Informations pratiques

  • Localisation : Paris 10e

  • Type de contrat : stage conventionné

  • Durée : 6 mois

  • Date de démarrage : janvier

  • Télétravail : selon les modalités en vigueur au sein de l’équipe


Idéalement, tu :

  • Recherches un stage de fin d’études ou de césure dans le domaine commercial.

  • As un bon relationnel, es à l’écoute et te sens à l’aise au téléphone.

  • Aimes comprendre les besoins de tes interlocuteurs et leur présenter des solutions adaptées.

  • As envie de monter en compétences et de découvrir le métier d’Account Executive.

  • Fais preuve de curiosité, d’organisation et d’esprit d’équipe.

  • Es à l’aise avec les outils numériques.

Bonus : tu as déjà réalisé un stage, un job étudiant, une mission d’intérim ou une expérience dans la vente ou la relation client.

Tu souhaites découvrir les métiers Sales tout en échangeant avec des interlocuteurs aux profils variés ? Tu recherches une équipe dans laquelle tu pourras apprendre, être accompagné·e et progresser rapidement ?

Ne cherche plus et postule pour nous rejoindre !

Recruitment process

Pour postuler, il te suffit d’un CV. Pas besoin de lettre de motivation classique et interminable : explique-nous simplement pourquoi tu souhaites rejoindre Matera à ce poste.

1️⃣ Premier entretien téléphonique de 20 à 30 mn avec notre recruteuse,

2️⃣ Entretien avec 2 Sales Manager, pour une mise en situation (30 en visio)

3️⃣ Last round dans nos bureaux avec la VP sales

4️⃣ Prise de références puis offre

descriptionHtml:
Au sein de l'équipe Grands Comptes, rattachée à l’Adminsitration des Ventes, vous contribuerez directement à la croissance et à la sécurisation du chiffre d'affaires de Doctolib. Vous jouerez un rôle opérationnel clé dans le processus de closing mensuel et la gestion du cycle de facturation, tout en développant une expertise complète du cycle commercial et financier chez Doctolib.

Vos missions

Vos responsabilités incluent, mais ne sont pas limitées à :

  • Accompagner le closing mensuel en soutenant les équipes commerciales Grands Comptes dans leurs démarches contractuelles et en anticipant les pics d'activité de fin de mois
  • Assurer le suivi opérationnel de l'ARR closé en identifiant les dossiers présentant des risques de facturation et en alertant les équipes concernées
  • Coordonner avec les équipes Finance l'envoi effectif des factures une fois tous les justificatifs réceptionnés et validés
  • Piloter le suivi du chiffre d'affaires non facturé par commercial/équipe, en maintenant un reporting en temps réel pour minimiser les délais
  • Participer à la facturation mensuelle des comptes publics et accompagner les clients dans leur suivi de factures

Les qualités attendues 

Avant de poursuivre votre lecture, si vous n'avez pas le profil exact décrit ci-dessous, mais que vous pensez que cette description de poste correspond à vos compétences et à vos besoins, nous vous encourageons tout de même à postuler.

Vous pourrez être le prochain membre de notre équipe si vous :

  • Êtes actuellement en formation ou étudiant(e) en école de commerce, université (Master) ou formation équivalente avec une spécialisation commerciale, administrative ou finance
  • Faites preuve de rigueur et d'attention aux détails dans le traitement des données financières et contractuelles
  • Savez gérer les priorités et travailler efficacement dans une periode de forte activité, notamment lors des périodes de closing
  • Maîtrisez les outils bureautiques (Excel, Google Sheets) et avez une appétence pour les outils de reporting
  • Possédez d'excellentes capacités de communication pour coordonner avec différentes équipes (Key Account Sales/Managers , Finance, Legal)

Ce serait fantastique si :

  • Vous avez une première expérience en environnement commercial ou financier (stage, alternance, job étudiant)
  • Vous maîtrisez les processus de facturation B2B ou avez des notions de comptabilité
  • Vous êtes à l'aise avec les outils CRM et de gestion commerciale

Notre offre

  • Un programme d’onboarding complet, avec la Doctolib Academy et de nombreuses sessions de formation au sein de votre équipe (langues, soft skills, compétences techniques)
  • Une carte Swile et de nombreuses offres de restauration au sein de nos locaux 
  • Une offre de sport : un abonnement Urban Sports Club, des cours de sport gratuits dans les bureaux ou à distance
  • Le remboursement des titres de transport à 50%
  • De nombreux bureaux offrant des espaces de collaboration et de bien-être 
  • Une politique de travail flexible avec un mode hybride

Le processus de recrutement

  • Un entretien avec Flore, talent partner (15 minutes)
  • Un entretien avec Chloé, KA Sales Administration Manager, votre future manager (1 heure)

Détails du poste

  • Stage conventionné à temps plein
  • Durée : 6 mois
  • Début souhaité : Janvier 2027
  • Lieu de travail : Levallois-Perret
  • Rémunération : À définir selon niveau d'études
  • Ce poste est éligible au télétravail partiel (3 jours au bureau, 2 jours en télétravail possibles)

title: Stage: Afdeling Commercie
descriptionHtml:
Over Nedlin

Nedlin is een industriële textielverzorger voor Healthcare, Hospitality en Industry, waar veiligheid, kwaliteit, continu verbeteren en verantwoord ondernemen centraal staan. Als groeiend B-Corp familiebedrijf investeren we graag in jong talent en versterken we de verbinding tussen onderwijs en arbeidsmarkt. Daarom bieden we studenten de kans om praktijkervaring op te doen, zich te ontwikkelen en Nedlin te leren kennen, met waar mogelijk mooie doorgroeikansen na het afstuderen.

De stageopdrachten

Bij de afdeling Commercie hebben we meerdere interessante stageopdrachten openstaan. Samen kijken we welke opdracht het beste aansluit bij jouw opleiding, interesses en kwaliteiten. Tijdens je stage draai je mee binnen onze commerciële binnen- en/of buitendienst en krijg je de kans om jouw commerciële vaardigheden in de praktijk verder te ontwikkelen.

Mogelijke werkzaamheden en stageopdrachten zijn:

  • Ondersteunen van de commerciële binnen- en buitendienst

  • Contact onderhouden met bestaande en potentiële klanten

title: STAGE - Assistant Chef de Produit Poker (H/F)
descriptionHtml:
Basés en plein cœur de Paris, nous faisons bouger l’industrie des jeux en ligne. Leader du poker et des paris sportifs en France avec 350 000 joueurs et 600 000 parieurs mensuels, nous sommes présents en Espagne, en Allemagne et bientôt en Italie et au Portugal. Nous offrons à nos joueurs une expérience exceptionnelle, à la fois technique, créative et qualitative. Innovation, unité et appartenance : nos valeurs façonnent une culture d’entreprise multiculturelle et unique. Et si tu avais un futur dans le jeu ? Techniquement, Winamax c’est :
  • Un moteur de jeu puissant et innovant : adaptation dynamique de l'offre de jeu, parties de poker hautement configurables, détection de fraude
  • Une architecture distribuée et scalable conçue pour traiter en temps réel les flux de la plateforme
  • Une plateforme modulaire soumise à des contraintes de haute disponibilité et de sécurisation des données, capable de gérer de fortes audience

C'est quoi l'équipe Produit Poker ?

Notre mission est de concevoir et faire évoluer l'expérience poker chez Winamax. Nous définissons la roadmap produit, aussi bien pour les nouvelles fonctionnalités (Reveal, Moods, Shots, Winamax Legends...) que pour les grands projets structurants de l'application (refonte des lobbys, nouveaux parcours utilisateurs, nouvelles variantes de jeu, etc.).

A PROPOS DU POSTE

Ton grand défi sera d'imaginer une solution innovante pour améliorer l'expérience des nouveaux joueurs. Un objectif ambitieux que tu concrétiseras grâce à l'apprentissage progressif de notre métier et de nos méthodes.

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

L'un de nos principaux enjeux est de lever les barrières à l'entrée et de proposer une expérience utilisateur fluide et engageante, capable de renforcer l'attractivité de notre application et de maximiser la rétention des nouveaux utilisateurs.

Dès ton arrivée, tu seras pleinement intégré aux réflexions menées sur les projets les plus stratégiques de l'équipe (refonte de parties de l'application, nouvelles fonctionnalités, nouveaux parcours joueurs...). Au fil du stage, tu seras progressivement associé à leur conception et gagneras en autonomie dans leur pilotage.

Tu seras notamment amené à :

  • Participer aux phases de discovery et aux ateliers de réflexion avec les équipes Produit et UI/UX
  • Participer à la définition des fonctionnalités, aux arbitrages et à la priorisation des solutions
  • Participer aux réflexions autour de la roadmap produit
  • Suivre le développement avec les équipes techniques
  • Participer aux recettes et à la validation d'un projet avant son lancement
  • Découvrir toutes les étapes de conception d'un produit digital, de l'idée jusqu'à sa mise entre les mains de plusieurs centaines de milliers de joueurs.

Ce que tu vas accomplir :

Au fil du stage, tu seras donc progressivement intégré au processus de définition et de pilotage de nos projets produits. Cette montée en compétence te conduira à ton projet de fin de stage : repenser et optimiser l'expérience d'accueil et d'intégration du nouveau joueur.

Ton objectif : t'appuyer sur l'identification des barrières à l'entrée et l'analyse des faiblesses de notre application pour concevoir, en collaboration avec un UI/UX Designer, une solution capable d'augmenter durablement la rétention des nouveaux joueurs sur notre application.

Tu seras amené à rédiger les spécifications fonctionnelles pour les développeurs, suivre le développement et assurer la recette ainsi que la mise en production de ton projet.


PROFIL RECHERCHÉ
Tu es étudiant en Bac+5 (école de commerce, marketing, management ou formation équivalente)
et tu recherches un stage de fin d'études avec de vraies responsabilités.
Joueur dans l’âme, tu possèdes une bonne expérience du poker en ligne et tu connais

title: Stage: Bedrijfsprocessen & Veiligheid
descriptionHtml:
Over Nedlin

Nedlin is een industriële textielverzorger voor Healthcare, Hospitality en Industry, waar veiligheid, kwaliteit, continu verbeteren en verantwoord ondernemen centraal staan. Als groeiend B-Corp familiebedrijf investeren we graag in jong talent en versterken we de verbinding tussen onderwijs en arbeidsmarkt. Daarom bieden we studenten de kans om praktijkervaring op te doen, zich te ontwikkelen en Nedlin te leren kennen, met waar mogelijk mooie doorgroeikansen na het afstuderen.

De stageopdracht

Tijdens deze hbo-stage ga je aan de slag met Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO). LOTO is een veiligheidsmethode waarbij machines en energiebronnen tijdens onderhoud of werkzaamheden veilig worden uitgeschakeld en vergrendeld. Zo wordt voorkomen dat een machine onverwacht wordt ingeschakeld terwijl eraan wordt gewerkt. Jij helpt Nedlin om deze werkwijze verder te ontwikkelen, te standaardiseren en praktisch toepasbaar te maken.

  • Je onderzoekt de huidige LOTO-werkwijze en brengt risico’s, energiebronnen en isolatiepunten in kaart.

  • Je ontwikkelt een uniforme LOTO-procedure en machine-specifieke LOTO-kaarten.

  • Je brengt de benodigde materialen en hulpmiddelen in kaart.

  • Je ontwikkelt instructie- en toolboxmateriaal voor medewerkers.

  • Je stelt een praktisch implementatieadvies op om LOTO binnen Nedlin verder te borgen.

Wat bieden wij?

  • Stagevergoeding:

    • € 300,- bruto per maand voor mbo-studenten (op basis van 40 uur per week);

    • € 400,- bruto per maand voor hbo-studenten (op basis van 40 uur per week);

  • Een leerzame stage binnen één van de modernste en duurzaamste wasserijen van Europa;

  • Ruimte en begeleiding om te werken aan jouw (afstudeer)opdracht;

  • Persoonlijke begeleiding en korte lijnen;

  • Een familiaire en positieve sfeer: samen feestdagen vieren, een jaarlijkse familiedag en leuke uitjes;

  • Kans op een (bij)baan bij Nedlin na afronding van je stage, bij wederzijdse match.

Veiligheid tijdens je stage

Veiligheid staat ook tijdens de uitvoering van de stageopdracht voorop. Je voert daarom geen risicovolle onderhoudswerkzaamheden zelfstandig uit. Eventuele technische aanpassingen worden uitsluitend uitgevoerd door bevoegde medewerkers of externe partijen. Machinekaarten worden vóór ingebruikname gevalideerd door de Technische Dienst.


Wie ben jij?

  • Je volgt een hbo-opleiding, bijvoorbeeld Integrale Veiligheidskunde, Technische Bedrijfskunde, Werktuigbouwkunde, Elektrotechniek, Engineering of Facility Management.

  • Je hebt interesse in techniek en veiligheid en combineert graag theorie met praktijk.

  • Je werkt zelfstandig, nauwkeurig en proactief en communiceert gemakkelijk met collega’s.

  • Je bent 32 tot 40 uur per week beschikbaar voor een meewerk- en/of afstudeerstage.

  • Je kunt zelfstandig naar onze locatie in Elsloo of Hoensbroek reizen.

Pak het moment

Wil jij tijdens je stage niet alleen werken aan een interessante opdracht, maar vooral ook leren, ervaring opdoen en jezelf ontwikkelen? Bij Nedlin krijg je de ruimte om jouw kennis vanuit je opleiding toe te passen in de praktijk, mee te kijken binnen onze organisatie en samen te werken met ervaren collega’s. Maak van jouw stage een waardevolle stap richting je toekomst. Solliciteer eenvoudig via de solliciteerknop. Heb je eerst nog vragen over de stage of de opdracht? title: (Stage) Chargé(e) de Communication & Branding - Janvier 2027
descriptionHtml:
QUI SOMMES-NOUS ?

Sowefund est la plateforme pionnière du co-investissement Venture Capital en France, adossée au groupe Founders Future (le fonds fondé par Marc Ménasé).

Notre métier : repérer les pépites de la tech et permettre à notre communauté de plus de 180 000 investisseurs d'entrer à leur capital aux côtés des meilleurs fonds.

Le Venture Capital finance l'économie réelle et les boîtes qu'on utilise tous les jours sans y penser : Lydia pour rembourser ses potes, Yuka pour scanner ses courses, Lunii pour occuper les enfants, et demain des startups qui façonnent l'IA ou la santé.

Quelques chiffres :

  • Plus de 145 pépites financées (Mon Petit Placement, Merveilles du Monde,ekWateur, Lemrock...).
  • Plus de 150 M€ injectés dans l'économie réelle.
  • Une communauté de plus de 180 000 membres actifs.

TON RÔLE : FAIRE RAYONNER SOWEFUND ET BOOSTER NOTRE NOTORIÉTÉ

Ton défi principal : faire connaître Sowefund, vulgariser l'univers du VC et positionner notre marque comme le réflexe n°1 pour investir dans les futures pépites françaises.

Au cœur de notre visibilité, tu seras le moteur de notre création de contenu et de nos prises de parole.

1. Réseaux Sociaux & Notoriété de Marque

  • Élaboration stratégique & animation : piloter nos prises de parole sur LinkedIn et Instagram. Trouver les angles, concevoir le calendrier éditorial et animer la communauté.
  • Storytelling & Formats : vulgariser l'actualité tech, imaginer des carrousels percutants et mettre en lumière les sociétés qui lèvent des fonds chez nous.
  • Suivi de performance : analyser les métriques (portée, engagement, croissance des abonnés) pour tester de nouveaux formats en continu.

2. Podcast & Vidéo : De l'Enregistrement à la Diffusion

  • Gestion du podcast : participer à la production du podcast du fondateur de Sowefund
  • Post-production & Formats courts : monter les meilleurs extraits pour concevoir des capsules courtes et rythmées (TikTok, Reels, Shorts, LinkedIn) avec titrages et sous-titrages dynamiques.
  • Distribution : assurer la mise en ligne sur les plateformes audio (Spotify, Apple...) et YouTube avec des visuels et miniatures qui donnent envie de cliquer.

3. Création Visuelle, Ads & Supports Clés (Decks & Slides)

  • Decks & Présentations : concevoir et mettre en page des présentations visuelles irréprochables (Pitch Decks, présentations partenaires, bilans) pour valoriser Sowefund auprès de toutes nos parties prenantes.
  • Assets visuels : créer les visuels, bannières et carrousels pour rythmer les annonces de levées et les temps forts de la marque.
  • Formats publicitaires : décliner les créas visuelles pour nos campagnes d'acquisition payante (Meta Ads, Google Ads).

4. Gestion de Projet Communication

Être le garant de la cohérence de l'image de marque et du ton Sowefund sur l'ensemble des points de contact.

CE QUE TU APPRENDS ICI

Une liberté d’action directe : une structure agile où tes initiatives du matin peuvent être concrétisées l'après-midi.

Une immersion dans l'écosystème tech : des échanges directs avec les fondateurs et figures de l'écosystème startup français.

Un portfolio concret et valorisable : tes présentations, formats vidéos, podcasts et créations visuelles touchent une audience de grande envergure.

PROFIL RECHERCHÉ

Formation : BAC+3 à BAC+5 en École de Communication, Médias, Journalisme ou École de Commerce.

Sens du format & réseaux : tu maîtrises les codes de TikTok, LinkedIn et Instagram pour capter l'attention dès les premières secondes.

Boîte à outils créative : tu es à l'aise sur Canva, PowerPoint / Google Slides ou Figma pour structurer des présentations claires et élégantes, et sur CapCut / Premiere pour monter des vidéos courtes.

Aisance rédactionnelle : une plume vive, une orthographe irréprochable et un esprit de synthèse pour rendre limpide n'importe quel sujet complexe.

Énergie et curiosité : envie de proposer des idées neuves et de tester des formats originaux sans attendre un brief rigide.

POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE ?

Visibilité immédiate : tes créations, vidéos et supports sont vus chaque mois par des centaines de milliers de professionnels et d'investisseurs.

Cadre de travail : des bureaux au cœur de Paris (quartier Opéra), au sein d'une équipe accessible et dynamique.

Autonomie : une équipe à taille humaine où tes idées du matin peuvent être déployées l'après-midi.

title: Stage Chef.fe de projet migration applicative en santé
descriptionHtml:
Dans le cadre de la migration de notre application desktop, nous recherchons un.e stagiaire pour piloter le suivi de l’adoption et accompagner nos clients tout au long de leur transition vers la nouvelle solution.

L’objectif sera de permettre au plus grand nombre de clients de migrer dans les meilleures conditions avant le transfert progressif du suivi à notre équipe Support, à l’issue du stage.

Ce stage combine gestion de projet, communication client, accompagnement au changement, analyse de données et compréhension des environnements informatiques hospitaliers.

Tes missions

Piloter la communication autour de la migration

Tu construiras et déploieras un plan de communication adapté aux différentes étapes de la migration :

  • Identification des clients à contacter et segmentation des populations ;

  • Préparation des messages de premier contact ;

  • Organisation des relances et suivi des réponses ;

  • Adaptation des communications selon le niveau d’avancement des clients ;

  • Gestion des objections, questions et éventuels points de blocage ;

  • Formalisation des bonnes pratiques et des argumentaires.

Prioriser les migrations

Tu contribueras à définir une stratégie de priorisation des clients en fonction de différents critères :

  • Taille et typologie des établissements ;

  • Niveau de maturité ou de préparation technique ;

  • Contraintes liées à l’environnement informatique ;

  • Niveau d’engagement et de réponse des interlocuteurs ;

  • Risques identifiés et complexité de l’accompagnement nécessaire.

L’objectif sera de concentrer les efforts sur les clients présentant le meilleur potentiel de progression ou nécessitant un accompagnement spécifique.

Mettre en place un tableau de suivi et des outils de reporting

Tu concevras et maintiendras un tableau de bord permettant de suivre l’avancement global de la migration, notamment :

  • Nombre de clients contactés ;

  • Taux de réponse et de relance ;

  • Clients migrés, en cours de migration ou non encore engagés ;

  • Principales raisons de blocage ;

  • Actions réalisées et prochaines étapes ;

  • Indicateurs d’adoption et d’utilisation.

Tu t’appuieras notamment sur Mixpanel et sur les outils internes disponibles afin de fiabiliser le suivi et de produire des reportings réguliers à destination des équipes concernées.

Accompagner les clients

Selon les besoins identifiés, tu pourras également participer directement à l’accompagnement des clients :

  • Réponse aux questions liées à la migration ;

  • Coordination avec les équipes techniques et Support ;

  • Aide à la préparation des étapes de migration ;

  • Suivi des situations nécessitant un accompagnement personnalisé ;

  • Remontée des irritants et des besoins récurrents ;

  • Contribution à l’amélioration continue du parcours de migration.

Préparer le transfert à l’équipe Support

Une partie importante du stage consistera à préparer la reprise du suivi par l’équipe Support :

  • Documentation du processus de migration ;

  • Centralisation de l’historique et du statut de chaque client ;

  • Formalisation des procédures et réponses types ;

  • Identification des cas particuliers et des risques résiduels ;

  • Transmission des outils, méthodes et indicateurs de pilotage.

Profil recherché

Tu es étudiant.e en école d’ingénieur ou en formation supérieure spécialisée en informatique, systèmes et réseaux, gestion de projet ou domaine équivalent.

Tu disposes idéalement de connaissances en :

  • Administration système et réseau ;

  • Environnements informatiques d’entreprise ;

  • Analyse et suivi de données ;

  • Gestion de projet ou conduite du changement ;

  • Outils de reporting et d’analyse produit, notamment Mixpanel.

Une première compréhension des systèmes d’information hospitaliers serait un véritable plus.

Nous recherchons surtout une personne :

  • Structurée et organisée ;

  • À l’aise dans les échanges avec des interlocuteurs variés ;

  • Capable de gérer plusieurs sujets en parallèle ;

  • Curieuse et autonome ;

  • Dotée d’un bon esprit d’analyse ;

  • À l’aise pour formaliser, synthétiser et suivre des plans d’action ;

  • Orientée résultats et satisfaction client.

Ce que tu apprendras

Ce stage te permettra de développer une expérience concrète sur :

  • Le pilotage d’un projet de migration à grande échelle ;

  • La communication et l’accompagnement de clients professionnels ;

  • La conduite du changement dans un environnement exigeant ;

  • L’analyse de données produit et l’utilisation de Mixpanel ;

  • La construction d’indicateurs de suivi ;

  • La coordination entre équipes Produit, Technique, Customer Success et Support ;

  • Les enjeux liés aux systèmes d’information hospitaliers.

Informations pratiques
